entries.nuer_sentence: Dämaar ni Lual ɛ camjiɛc.

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛŋa ci dɔw jiaath kac ɔ?

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu mandɔɔŋ gaak kä cuɛ rɔal.

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɔn diiw nɛy ni Lual.

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu nɛy ɛ la̱r mandɔɔŋ.

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu mandɔɔŋ ɛ thiec kä cuɛ jɛ lar i̱ ɛ jɛn.

entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä kɛ pɛ̈th, Lual /cɛ puɔ̱nydɛ jek ɛ gɔaa.

entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ riŋ duel coowni.

entries.nuer_sentence: Lual cuɛ jicdɛ käp.

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu mandɔɔŋ thiec i̱, "Ɛŋu mi ci yɛn ɛ ŋa̱c kɛ kui̱c kä mɛmɛ?"
entries.english_sentence: Grandmother asked, "What lesson did you learn from Lual's experience?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyawdä ɛ nikä?
entries.english_sentence: Where is my cat?

entries.nuer_sentence: Tëë piny laŋrɛpkä?

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn nɛn!

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Both kɛnɛ Nyayow ni̱n lɔ̱ŋä duëëlgɔ̱rä tin bi ben lip.
entries.english_sentence: Both and Nyayow waited for the school holidays to come.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛ jɛn gua̱a̱th in ro̱ŋ kɛ ɣöö bikɛ mandɔɔŋdiɛn gui̱l kɛ jɛ.
entries.english_sentence: It was time for them to visit their grandmother.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cukɛ gër kɛ rɛy pääm, le̱y dɔaar amäni ka̱a̱k.
entries.english_sentence: They drove past mountains, wild animals and farms.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔr gua̱th mi tɔt, cu Both kɛnɛ Nyayow niɛɛn kɛ näk.
entries.english_sentence: After a while, Both and Nyayow fell asleep.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cukɛ mandɔɔŋdiɛn jek te lɔ̱ŋä thaar jiaath.
entries.english_sentence: They found their grandmother resting under a tree.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu mandɔɔŋ ra̱w kä tuaarɛ.Cu gaat jɛ moc kɛ muc.
entries.english_sentence: Grandmother danced and sang.The children gave her presents.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu mandɔɔŋ Both kɛnɛ Nyayow poth kɛ puɔ̱th rɛy ciëŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Grandmother blessed Both and Nyayow in a traditional way.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Both kɛnɛ Nyayow ŋar kɛ ɣɔ̱kkuthni kɛnɛ diit.
entries.english_sentence: Both and Nyayow played with butterflies and birds.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɔ jiɛn kööt kä cukɛ ŋar kɛ dhur dhur rɛy puɔ̱ɔ̱l.
entries.english_sentence: They climbed trees.They splashed in the water of the lake.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kɛn cuuc.Cu niɛɛn kɛ näk ɛ /kenkɛ mi̱eth kua̱n thiaŋ thuk.
entries.english_sentence: They were tired.They fell asleep before finishing their dinner.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cukɛ mandɔɔŋ luäk.Cu kɛn toŋ ruɔ̱ɔ̱l kä cukɛ dɛy wal pon.
entries.english_sentence: They helped grandmother.They collected eggs and picked vegetables.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu mandɔɔŋ Both kɛnɛ Nyayow ŋi̱ec kɛ tha̱t kuaan ti gööl.
entries.english_sentence: Grandmother taught Both and Nyayow how to cook different foods.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Both ɣɔ̱k mandɔɔŋ naŋ laak.Cu kɛn dɛy wal ji̱ thieekä cam.
entries.english_sentence: Both took grandmother's cows to graze.They ate a neighbour's crops.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kɛn wä thok luaak mandɔɔŋdiɛn gua̱th ko̱kä.
entries.english_sentence: They went to their grandmother’s stall at the market.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ thiaŋ, cu kɛn mandɔɔŋdiɛn luäk kɛ kuen yio̱wnikɛ.
entries.english_sentence: In the evening, they helped grandmother to count her money.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ pɛ̈th, cu ni̱n lɔ̱ŋä thuɔ̱k.Cu mandi̱t mi̱eth guir kɛ kui̱ ja̱liɛn.
entries.english_sentence: Soon, the holidays were over.Grandmother packed food for their journey.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Gaat /ci kɛn jɛ gör i̱ jiɛnkɛ."Mandɔɔŋ, bër kɛ nɛy kɛɛl."
entries.english_sentence: The children did not want to leave."Grandmother, come with us."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Both kɛnɛ Nyayow mandɔɔŋ bom."Dothni kɛ mal, mandɔɔŋ."
entries.english_sentence: Both and Nyayow hugged grandmother."Goodbye, grandmother," they said.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Gɔaa ni ŋadiɛn, tëk rɛ̈ɛ̈k kiɛ tëk rɛy ciëŋ?
entries.english_sentence: What is better, city life or village life?
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Tëëkɛ gua̱n kakä mi tekɛ thäk mi dɔaaŋ.
entries.english_sentence: A farmer had an old ox.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä tëëkɛ kacik bä. Ɛn thäk kɛnɛ kacik kɛ mäth.
entries.english_sentence: He had a donkey too.The ox and the donkey were friends.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ thiaŋ, cu thäk kacik jiök i̱, "Ɣän cä cuuc ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛn wa̱lɛ."
entries.english_sentence: One evening, the ox told the donkey, "I am very tired today."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "/Ka̱n lɔ̱ɔ̱ŋ ɛn wa̱lɛ."
entries.english_sentence: Another evening the ox told the donkey, "I did not rest today."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kacik ɛ loc i̱, "Ci lät ni ɣän ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä ji̱."
entries.english_sentence: The donkey replied, "I worked harder than you."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ruɔ̱n, cu thäk wee i̱, "Ɛn wa̱lɛ ɛ cäŋ mi jiääk ɛlɔ̱ŋ."
entries.english_sentence: The next day, the ox said, "Today was a bad day."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kacik wee, "Mi wä wut wä bën, wakni, 'Ɣo̱o̱o̱!' Jɛn bɛ ji̱ jakä lɔ̱ŋ."
entries.english_sentence: The donkey said, "When the farmer comes, say, 'Moo!' He will let you rest."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bakädɛ, cu thäk röt, "Ɣo̱o̱o̱!" Cu gua̱n kakä jɛ jakä lɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: The next morning, the ox cried, 'Moo!'The farmer let him rest.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu gua̱n kakä kacik nööŋ raar wëë puur.
entries.english_sentence: The farmer took the donkey out to plough the land.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kacik lät ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ cäŋ kɛɛliw. Cuɛ bën cieŋ ɛ cɛ cuuc.
entries.english_sentence: The donkey worked hard all day.He was very tired when he came home.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ thäk jiök i̱, "Ci gua̱n kakä jɛ lar i̱ bɛ ji̱ näk kä bɛ ri̱ŋdu cam."
entries.english_sentence: The donkey told the ox, "The farmer said he will kill you for meat."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu thäk wee, "Kä bä lät i̱ ruun. Ci puɔ̱nydä pual ɛn täämɛ."
entries.english_sentence: The ox was afraid.He said, "I will work tomorrow. I feel better now."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Guɔ̱r kɛl wëë maath kɛ pi̱.
entries.english_sentence: One elephant is going to drink water.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Guëc da̱ŋ rɛw wäkɛ maath kɛ pi̱.
entries.english_sentence: Two giraffes are going to drink water.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mök da̱ŋ diɔ̱k kɛnɛ diit da̱ŋ ŋuaan wäkɛ maath kɛ pi̱ bä.
entries.english_sentence: Three buffaloes and four birds are also going to drink water.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Thi̱i̱l da̱ŋ dhieec kɛnɛ di̱eri da̱ŋ bäkɛl wäkɛ pi̱i̱ni.
entries.english_sentence: Five antelopes and six warthogs are walking to the water.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cɔ̱triaali da̱ŋ bärɔw riŋkɛ pi̱i̱ni.
entries.english_sentence: Seven zebras are running to the water.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Guëëk da̱ŋ bädäk kɛnɛ rɛc da̱ŋ bäŋuan tekɛ ket rɛy pi̱i̱ni.
entries.english_sentence: Eight frogs and nine fish are swimming in the water.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Lony kɛl tëë ro̱tdä. Jɛn bä go̱o̱rɛ ma̱th pi̱i̱ni. Ɛŋa dual kɛ lony ɔ?
entries.english_sentence: One lion roars. He also wants to drink. Who is afraid of the lion?
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Guɔ̱r tëë mäth pi̱i̱ni kɛnɛ lony kɛɛl.
entries.english_sentence: One elephant is drinking water with the lion.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Manpalɛ̈k kɛnɛ Ci̱rci̱r cikɛ kɔn a mäth.
entries.english_sentence: Chicken and Millipede were friends.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cukɛ wä ŋar kɛ kurɛ.
entries.english_sentence: They went to play football.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Manpalɛ̈k a käp go̱o̱nä.
entries.english_sentence: Chicken was the goal keeper.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Ci̱rci̱r gööni diɔ̱k la̱th!
entries.english_sentence: Millipede scored three goals!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Manpalɛ̈k lɔcdɛ jiääk.
entries.english_sentence: Chicken was annoyed.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Manpalɛ̈k Ci̱rci̱r roc.
entries.english_sentence: Chicken swallowed Millipede.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔrɛ, cu Manpalɛ̈k röm kɛnɛ man Ci̱rci̱ɛr.
entries.english_sentence: Then, Chicken met with Millipede's Mother.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Ci̱rci̱r wiee jic Manpalɛ̈k, "Mama, luäk ɣä! Manpalɛ̈k cɛ ɣä roc."
entries.english_sentence: "Mother, help! Chicken swallowed me!" cried Millipede from inside Chicken.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ci̱rci̱r cuɛ ŋuäny ɛ ji̱äk, kä cuɛ Manpalɛ̈k moc juey.
entries.english_sentence: Millipede tasted bad.Chicken felt sick.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Manpalɛ̈k ɛ tok kɛ mi kiɛlɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Chicken started coughing.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Manpalɛ̈k Ci̱rci̱r kiɛl raar.
entries.english_sentence: Chicken coughed out Millipede.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Manpalɛ̈k kɛnɛ Ci̱rci̱r cua ji̱ tɛ̈r amäni walɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Chicken and Millipede are now enemies.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, ɣän kɔnɛ nyi̱maar jäl nɛy kɛ raŋ duɔ̱p.
entries.english_sentence: One day my sister and I were walking near the road.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ tekɛ lörɛ mi di̱i̱t mi lëër piny wi̱i̱ pa̱a̱m.
entries.english_sentence: A big truck was driving down the hill.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä thurbil riŋɛ nhial kɛ pɛth wee wi̱i̱ pa̱a̱m.
entries.english_sentence: A car was speeding up the hill.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn ge̱e̱r lörɛkä wëëkɛ mi ruacɛ kɛ tɛlɛpon. Jɛn /cɛ duɔ̱p guic.
entries.english_sentence: The truck driver was talking on his mobile phone. He was not looking at the road.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu lörɛ rɔɔdɛ yiɛth kä thurbil!
entries.english_sentence: The truck smashed into the car!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu thurbil duëël wal kɛnɛ bolith ben kɛ kui̱ lua̱k.
entries.english_sentence: An ambulance and the police came to help.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu thurbiɛɛli da̱ŋ rɛw ti di̱t ben. Bikɛ lörɛ kɛnɛ thurbil ben yɔ̱c.
entries.english_sentence: Two tow trucks came. One towed the truck. The other towed the car.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɔn cu nɛy ŋɔakni diaal nɛn, ɛ cu nɛy ga̱a̱c ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: We saw everything. We were shocked.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jio̱k Nyapëc mi ci buɔthɛ näk tëë käk.
entries.english_sentence: Hungry Jackal was hunting.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn cuɛ kun joc.Ɛn kun cuɛ rɔ tɔ̱w piny pa̱a̱m mi di̱i̱t.
entries.english_sentence: He chased a mouse.The mouse hid under a big rock.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jio̱k Nyapëc cuɛ päm tɛt.Ɛn päm cuɛ pɛn cio̱kädɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Jackal dug.The rock fell on his paw.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Pɛlpɛl cuɛ Jio̱k Nyapëc liŋ cio̱tdɛ.Jɛn cuɛ riŋ kä Jio̱k Nyapëc.
entries.english_sentence: Rabbit heard Jackal calling.He ran to see what happened.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Jio̱k Nyapëc Pɛlpɛl jiök i̱, "Mi wi̱i̱ ɣä wä luäk, bä ji̱ moc kɛ kuän."
entries.english_sentence: Rabbit agreed to help Jackal.Jackal promised to give Rabbit food.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Pɛlpɛl cuɛ päm ɣɔk.Ɛn päm cuɛ lɛy piny cio̱kä Jiöök Nyapëc.
entries.english_sentence: Rabbit pushed the rock.The rock rolled off Jackal's paw.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Pɛlpɛl cuɛ Jio̱k Nyapëc thiec kɛ muc.Jio̱k Nyapëc cu ŋɛ̈ɛ̈ny i̱ bi cam.
entries.english_sentence: Rabbit asked for his reward.Jackal threatened to eat him!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jio̱k Nyapëc kɛnɛ Pɛlpɛl cukɛ wut mi di̱i̱t jek mi bi lukdiɛn lat.
entries.english_sentence: Jackal and Rabbit found an old man to judge their case.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jio̱k Nyapëc cuɛ ŋɛ̈ɛ̈ny kɛ gua̱ndi̱t, go̱o̱rɛ ni ca̱mdɛ bä!
entries.english_sentence: Jackal threatened to eat the old man too!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn wut cuɛ wee, "Ɛ ɣä nɛ̈ɛ̈nä päm ɛ ŋot /ka̱nɛ ni gok."
entries.english_sentence: The man said, “Let me see the rock before I decide.”
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jio̱k Nyapëc kɛnɛ Pɛlpɛl cua gua̱ndi̱t naŋ pa̱a̱m.
entries.english_sentence: Jackal and Rabbit took the man to the rock.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jio̱k Nyapëc cuɛ ta̱a̱ ëë pɛn kɛ päm ciökädɛ lat.
entries.english_sentence: Jackal explained how the rock fell on his paw.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu gua̱ndi̱t Pɛlpɛl thiëc ɛn ɣöö bɛ jɛ nyuɔ̱th ta̱a̱ ee wocɛ ni päm.
entries.english_sentence: The man asked Rabbit to show how he pushed the rock.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Pɛlpɛl päm nyɔk kɛ ɣöök.Cuɛ jɛ luɔc ciökä Jiöök Nyapëc.
entries.english_sentence: Rabbit pushed.The rock was back on Jackal's paw.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu gua̱ndi̱t ɛ lar i̱, "Ɛn täämɛ cɛ ku pay pa̱a̱r. Can jiɛn wanɛ cieŋ."
entries.english_sentence: The man said, “Now it is fair. Let us go home.”
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu gua̱ndi̱t kɛnɛ Pɛlpɛl jiɛn, kä cua Jio̱k Nyapëc ba̱ny rɛy rikä.
entries.english_sentence: The man and Rabbit went.Jackal was left trapped.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän cɔalkɛ ɣä i̱ Yien.
entries.english_sentence: My name is Simo.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ta̱a̱kɛ mäthni da̱ŋ ŋuaan.
entries.english_sentence: I have four friends.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ciöötkiɛn ɛ Lam kɛ Nyagɔaa kɛ Dak kɛ Nyajuɔk.
entries.english_sentence: Their names are Zizo, Lele, Sisa and Ayanda.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Määthdä ni Lam nhɔkɛ ŋar kurɛkä.
entries.english_sentence: My friend Zizo likes to play soccer.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Määthdä ni Nyagɔaa nhɔkɛ kët.
entries.english_sentence: My friend Lele likes to swim.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Määthdä ni Dak la nhɔkɛ ŋar kɛ kumdakuany.
entries.english_sentence: My friend Sisa likes to play hide-and-seek.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Määthdä ni Nyajuɔk la nhɔkɛ ni kuën.
entries.english_sentence: My friend Ayanda likes to read.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän? Ɣän nhɔakä ŋa̱a̱ri diaal tin nhɔk kɛn kɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Me? I like to do the things they like to do.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän la ŋarä kɛ kurɛ kɔnɛ Lam.
entries.english_sentence: I play soccer with Zizo.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä la wä nɛy kɛt kɔnɛ Nyagɔaa.
entries.english_sentence: I swim with Lele.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: La ŋarä kɛ kumdakuany kɔnɛ Dak.
entries.english_sentence: I play hide-and-seek with Sisa.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bër, määth, ɛŋu mi nhɔki?
entries.english_sentence: Come, friend, what do you like?
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bër, canɛ ŋar kɛ kurɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Come, play soccer with us.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bër, canɛ ben kɛt.
entries.english_sentence: Come, swim with us.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bër, canɛ ben ŋar kɛ kumdakuany.
entries.english_sentence: Come, play hide-and-seek with us.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bër, canɛ ben kuën!
entries.english_sentence: Come, read with us!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn gua̱a̱th cuŋä thuɔ̱rbiɛɛli rɛy rɛ̈ɛ̈kda la thiäŋɛ kɛ naath.
entries.english_sentence: The bus stop in my town was full of people.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu cio̱o̱t thuɔ̱rbiɛɛl wak, "Wa̱a̱ rɛɛk in di̱i̱t! Jianä ɛn täämɛ!"
entries.english_sentence: The bus conductor shouted, "Going to the city! Leaving now!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Naath ɣɔakɛ rɔ kɛ ɣöö göörkɛ wä rɛy thuɔ̱rbiɛɛl.
entries.english_sentence: People pushed to get on the bus.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu män tin tekɛ gaat nyuur.Jɛn ja̱l cuɛ bär ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Women with children sat down.The journey was going to be long.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän cua̱ nyuur thiekä wernyinä, gekä wutdä.
entries.english_sentence: I sat at the window, next to a man.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän cua̱ ca̱r i̱, "Wa̱a̱ rɛy rɛ̈ɛ̈k ɛ di̱i̱tdɛ bä ciëŋ wä tim."
entries.english_sentence: I thought, "I am going to the big city! I will miss home."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ tekɛ köök ti ŋuan ti kɔakɛ nyinkiɛn.
entries.english_sentence: There were many hawkers selling their goods.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu tha̱a̱ŋ ja̱a̱li rɔ ko̱k ikä.Ɣän cua̱ thil yio̱w ti dëë kɔk ni duɔ̱ɔ̱r.
entries.english_sentence: Some passengers bought things.I had no money to buy anything.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ pɛ̈th, cu geer kaŋ koth.Cuɛ cua̱ jɛn jiɛɛn kiɛ däk nath piny.
entries.english_sentence: Suddenly, the driver blew the horn.It was time to leave.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn köök ɣɔakɛ rɔ kä rɔdiɛn benä diɛn raar rɛy thuɔ̱rbiɛɛl.
entries.english_sentence: The hawkers pushed each other to get out of the bus.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän cua̱ rɔ thiec kärɔa, "Bä lunyjɔk i̱ nɛy?"
entries.english_sentence: “When will I return?" I asked myself.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu rɛy thuɔ̱rbiɛɛl le̱e̱th.Cuɔ wäŋkä kum.
entries.english_sentence: It was hot inside the bus.I closed my eyes.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän cua̱ car ni maar kɛnɛ dämaar tin te cieŋ.
entries.english_sentence: I thought about my mother and brother at home.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔr gua̱th mi tɔt, ɣän cua̱ cu niɛɛn.
entries.english_sentence: Gradually, I fell fast asleep.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔr thakni ti ŋuan, cua̱ keer käcuɛ ce̱tkɛ mi thiɛlɛ ram mi ci duɔth.
entries.english_sentence: Many hours later, I woke up.Almost everyone had left.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cuɛ la gua̱a̱th kɛ ɣöö bä näärä wä go̱r.
entries.english_sentence: It was time to find my uncle’s house.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Thoriydɛ ciɛkɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: His hoe was too short.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä thokduëëlɛ tëë piny ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: His doorway was too low.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä dhaŋdɛ ciɛkɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: His bed was too short.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä jio̱kthiliɛkdɛ ciɛkɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: His bicycle was too short.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn ɛ wut mi bäär ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: This man was too tall!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ taŋ thoriyädɛ la̱t ɛ la mi bäär ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: He made a very long hoe handle.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cuɛ thi̱i̱k thuɔkduëëlɛ jakä bär.
entries.english_sentence: He made very high door frames.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cuɛ dhaŋ mi bäär la̱t.
entries.english_sentence: He made a very long bed.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cuɛ kɔk kɛ jio̱kthiliɛk mi bäär.
entries.english_sentence: He bought a very high bicycle.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cuɛ cua nyuurɛ kɛ kɔm mi bäär. Kä la mithɛ kɛ tuŋ mi bäär.
entries.english_sentence: He sat on a very high chair.He ate with a very long fork.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cuɛ dhɔrɛ päl, cuɛ wä ciɛŋ ni rɛy dɔaar kɛ run ti ŋuan.
entries.english_sentence: He left his house and lived in a big forest.He lived for many years.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Cows and goats in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn yaŋ kɛnɛ dɛl kɛ ley ti gɔw ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä Nuäär.
entries.english_sentence: Cows and goats are important animals in Nuer culture.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Cows and goats in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: Nuääri larkɛ jɛ ɛ kɛn i̱, "Yaŋ ɛ muɔɔr amäni lia̱a̱du."
entries.english_sentence: Nuer people say that the cow is your mother until your death.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Cows and goats in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan, la naath ɛ wee, "Ti̱i̱kɛ muɔɔri da̱ŋ rɛw."
entries.english_sentence: In the ancient days, the Nuer said that you have two mothers.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Cows and goats in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: Muɔɔr in nhiam ɛ muɔɔr in daap ji̱.
entries.english_sentence: Your first mother is the mother who delivered you.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Cows and goats in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä muɔɔr in rɛwdɛ kɛnɛ nyiman, ɛ yaŋ kɛnɛ dɛl.
entries.english_sentence: Your second mother and her sister are the cow and goat.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Cows and goats in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn nɔmɔ nyoothɛ ɣöö Nuääri nhɔakɛ ɣɔ̱k kɛnɛ det ɛlɔ̱ŋ rɛy leyni diaal.
entries.english_sentence: That is why Nuer people love cows and goats above all animals.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Cows and goats in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣɔ̱k kɛnɛ det kuenkɛ kɛ naath rɛy Nuäärä. Thöpkɛ kɛ ɛ la muc ti gɔw kɛ kui̱c rikni.
entries.english_sentence: Cows and goats are used as dowry in the Nuer community.They are given as offerings when there is a problem.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Cows and goats in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣɔ̱k kɛnɛ det thiɛlɛ kɛ päär rɛy Nuäärä.Kɛ kui̱c ɛmɔ, Nuääri ŋi̱eeckɛ gaatkiɛn ɛn ɣöö, ba ɣɔ̱k kɛnɛ det guic ce̱tkɛ manikiɛn.
entries.english_sentence: Cows and goats have no comparison in Nuer culture.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Tëëkɛ ciek mi di̱i̱t mi cieŋ kä rɔɔadɛ rɛy wi̱lɛkä. Kä la diɛrɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ ni ciaŋ.
entries.english_sentence: There was once an old woman. She lived by herself inside a bottle.She complained all the time.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, cu buuk bën kɛ gëkdɛ kä cuɛ jɛ nɛn ɛn ɣöö jiek lɔcdɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: One day a fairy passed by her home.She saw her looking very sad.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu buuk cuɔ̱ŋ kä cuɛ ciek thiec, "Ɛŋu la riɛk ɔ? Kä ɛŋu mɛ ci lɔcdu jiääk inɛ mɛ?"
entries.english_sentence: The fairy stopped and asked her, "What is the problem? Why are you so sad?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu ciek ɛ luoc i̱, "Ɣän cä cuuc kɛ ciaaŋ rɛy wi̱lɛkä."
entries.english_sentence: "I am tired of living in a bottle," replied the old lady.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu buuk ɛ jiök i̱, "Jiɛc rɔ kä pat tetku nikä rɛɛw kä ri̱tni rɔ nikä diɔ̱k."
entries.english_sentence: The fairy said to her, "Stand up, clap your hands twice, and turn around three times."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔr kä mëë cɛ tɔ̱tɔ̱ la̱t, cu mandi̱t rɔɔdɛ wä jek ni rɛy duëël mi tɔt.
entries.english_sentence: The old woman did as she was told.She found herself in a small house.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä kɛ kɔr ni̱ni ti tɔt cu buuk luny jɔk kä cuɛ mandi̱t leni jek ŋuot lɔcdɛ kɛ mi /cɛ tɛth.
entries.english_sentence: After a few days the fairy came back and found the woman still unhappy.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu buuk ɛ thiec i̱, "Ɛŋu ci jiek ɛn täämɛ? Ɛŋu ci lɔcdu leni jiek ɔ?"
entries.english_sentence: The fairy asked her, "What is wrong now? Why are you sad?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu mandi̱t ɛ jiök i̱, "Duel ɛmɛ kui̱yɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ. /Ci ɣän jɛ nhɔk."
entries.english_sentence: "This house is too small. I do not like it," responded the old woman.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu buuk ɛ jiök i̱, "Jiɛc rɔ kä pat tetku nikä rɛɛw kä ri̱tni rɔ nikä diɔ̱k."
entries.english_sentence: The fairy said to her, "Stand up, clap your hands twice, and turn around three times."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci mandi̱t kɛ la̱t, cuɛ rɔɔdɛ wä jek rɛy duëël mi di̱i̱t.
entries.english_sentence: The old woman did as she was told.She found herself in a big house.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu buuk mandi̱t ben gui̱l ɛ nyɔk. Cuɛ jek ŋuotdɛ /ci lɔcdɛ tɛth kä ŋɛ̈nyɛ.
entries.english_sentence: The fairy came to see the old woman again.She found her still unhappy and grumpy.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu buuk ɛ nyɔk nikɛ thiec i̱, "Ɛŋu ci rɔ nyɔk kɛ tuɔk ɔ mandi̱t?"Cu mandi̱t ɛ luoc i̱, "Duel ɛmɛ cuolɛ kä jiek rɛydɛ."
entries.english_sentence: The fairy asked her, "What is wrong old lady?"The old lady responded, "This house is dark and dirty."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu buuk mandi̱t jiök i̱, "Jiɛc rɔ kä pat tetku nikä rɛɛw kä ri̱tni rɔ nikä diɔ̱k."
entries.english_sentence: The fairy said to her, "Stand up, clap your hands twice, and turn around three times."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä kɛ kɔr kä mëë ci mandi̱t tɔ̱tɔ̱ la̱t, cuɛ rɔɔdɛ wä jek ni rɛy wi̱lɛkä ɛ nyɔk.
entries.english_sentence: The old woman did as she was told.She found herself back inside the bottle.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Dɔaaŋ ciëk mi te rɛy wi̱lɛkä
entries.nuer_sentence: /Ken mandi̱t puɔ̱th in cɛ jek nɛn.Cuɛ luoc ni rɛy wi̱lɛkädɛ mëë cieŋɛ thi̱n kärɔa kä cu lɔcdɛ ŋuot kɛ jieek.
entries.english_sentence: The old woman could not see the blessings she received.She ended up in her bottle, alone and unhappy.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rɛy dhɔaariɛn Bol tëkɛ thurbil kɛl kärɔa.Ɛ mi di̱i̱t kä ɛ mi tɔ̱c. Ɛ mi wuɔ̱ɔ̱w ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: There was only one bus in Bol's village.It was big and blue. It was very noisy.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "I̱ ruun banɛ wä rɛɛk," cu man Bol jɛ lar. Ban bieyni duëëlgɔ̱rkädu wä kɔk.
entries.english_sentence: "Tomorrow we will go to town," said Bol's mother. "We will buy your school uniform."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bol cuɛ ŋa̱a̱th ɛlɔ̱ŋ. Dee kɛ wä kɛ thurbil in tɔ̱c in di̱i̱t./Kerɛ niɛɛn ɛn wäär ëë.
entries.english_sentence: Bol was very excited. They would travel in the big blue bus.He could not sleep that night.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Min ci man ben kɛ ɣöö ba ben ke̱r, cua Bol jek cɛ rɔ ku thuŋ ruk kɛ bi̱i̱ni ni wän.
entries.english_sentence: When his mother came to wake him, Bol was already dressed.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bol kɛnɛ man cukɛ wä gua̱a̱th cuuŋä thurbiɛɛli. Cuɔ thurbil in tɔ̱c in di̱i̱t lip.Dundɛ ɣöö /ken thurbil ben.
entries.english_sentence: Bol and his mother walked to the bus stop. They waited for the big blue bus.But the bus did not come.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu tha̱a̱ŋ nath ti kɔ̱ŋ cop gua̱a̱th cuuŋä thurbiɛɛli.Cu kɛ koom kɛ ɣöö ci thurbil jääny. "Jɛnɛ winith, ɛn thurbil?" thieec kɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Other people arrived at the bus stop.They complained because the bus was late. "Where is the bus?" they asked.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bol cuɛ diɛɛr. "Ci kɔn rɔ bi luäŋ kɛ wä rɛɛk," cuɛ ca̱r. "/Ci ɣän bieyni duëëlgɔ̱rkädä bi luäŋ kɛ jek."
entries.english_sentence: Bol was worried. "We will not be able to go to town," he thought. "I will not be able to get my uniform."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Tha̱a̱ŋ nath cukɛ ŋɔ̱a̱a̱ŋ kä cu kɛ wä cieŋ. Bol cuɛ wiee. /Cɛ jɛ go̱r i̱ derɛ loc cieŋ."Ban li̱e̱p ɛ määth ɛlɔ̱ŋ," laar man ɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Some people gave up and went home. Bol cried. He did not want to go."We will wait a bit longer," said his mother.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Niɛ gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ, cuɔ wuɔ̱ɔ̱w liŋ. Cuɔ tur nɛn nhial.Thurbil tëë benä!
entries.english_sentence: Suddenly, they heard a noise. They saw dust in the air.The bus was coming!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Dundɛ ɣöö thurbil /ciɛ mi tɔc. Jɛn /ciɛ mi di̱i̱t. Ɛ mi lual mi tɔt./Ci naath ɛ go̱r ɛn ɣöö dee kɛ wä rɛy thurbiɛɛl ɛmɔ.
entries.english_sentence: But this bus was not blue. It was not big. It was red and small.The people did not want to get in this bus.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "Wi̱ɛ̈ɛ̈ rɛc! Wi̱ɛ̈ɛ̈ rɛc!" rɔaal geer. "Canɛ jääny ɛn wa̱lɛ," laarɛ jɛ.
entries.english_sentence: "Get in! Get in!" shouted the driver. "We are very late today," he called.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bol kɛnɛ man cukɛ wä rɛc kɛ nhiam. Kɛ pɛ̈th, cu nɛy diaal wä rɛy thurbiɛɛl in lual in tɔt.
entries.english_sentence: Bol and his mother got in first.Soon everyone else got in the small red bus.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bol cuɛ guic kɛ wernyini thurbiɛɛl.Cuɛ nɛy tä ŋuan nɛn cuuŋä gua̱a̱th cuuŋä thurbiɛɛli.
entries.english_sentence: Bol looked out the window.He saw more people at the bus stop.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nɛy ti ŋuan riŋ kɛ kɔɔr thurbiɛɛl kɛ ɣöö dëë cop.Dundɛ ɣöö ci kɛ jääny ni ɛlɔ̱ŋ. Thurbil in lual cɛ thia̱a̱ŋ. Cuɛ wä rɛɛk.
entries.english_sentence: Even more people were running to catch the bus.But they were too late. The red bus was full. It left for town.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "Thurbil in tɔ̱c in di̱i̱t ɛ ni̱kä?" thieec man Bol."Cɛ ri̱a̱p," cuɔ geer ɛ loc. "Te nɛy läätdädɛ. Bɛ ben i̱ ruun."
entries.english_sentence: "Where is the big blue bus?" asked Bol's mother."It broke down," replied the driver. "We are fixing it. It will come tomorrow."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bol /kenɛ diɛɛr kɛ biɛl thurbiɛɛl. /Kenɛ diɛɛr kɛ di̱t thurbiɛɛl.Ɛn thurbil ɛmɛ wëë rɛɛk!
entries.english_sentence: Bol did not care about the colour of the bus. He did not care about the size.All he cared about was that this bus was going to town!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɔk, ɛ ŋaprɔkɛdhɔ̱t, jɛn tɔ̱ɔ̱cä rɛy duëëlɛ kɛ bɛ̈c pua̱a̱ny.Kä cuɛ thiɛl ti̱i̱t.
entries.english_sentence: Ajao, a bat, lay in his house very ill.There was no one to attend to him.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔrɛ, Jɔk cuɛ li̱w.
entries.english_sentence: Then, Ajao died.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ji̱ thieekädɛ cukɛ wee, "Jɔk cɛ li̱w. Kɔn banɛ ji̱ maarädɛ cɔl kɛ ɣöö ba ben kony."
entries.english_sentence: The neighbours said, "Ajao is dead. We must call his relations to come and bury him."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ji̱ thieekädɛ cukɛ wä kä cɔalkɛ diit laar kɛn ɛ i̱, "Ram mi maar kɛ yɛ cɛ li̱w."
entries.english_sentence: The neighbours went and called the birds saying, "A relative of yours is dead."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn diit cukɛ ben kä cua nɛn jɛn ɛ Jɔk.Cu kɛ wee i̱, "Ɛn ley ɛmɛ /ciɛ ram kɛl kä kɔn."
entries.english_sentence: The birds came and saw that it was Ajao.They said, "This animal is not part of our family."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "Ji̱ dhɔaaran kɛndiaal tekɛ kɛ juät duŋni ɣöö Jɔk thiɛlɛ juät. Kɛ kui̱c ɛmɔ /ciɛ ram kɛl kä kɔn."Kɛn diit cukɛ jiɛɛn.
entries.english_sentence: "All our family have feathers but Ajao has none. So, he is not one of us."The birds went away.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn ji̱ thieekä cukɛ ruac ɛmɔ lat kɛɛl.Kɛn cua mat kä ɣöö, "Kɛn diit tekɛ cuɔ̱ɔ̱ŋ. Jɔk thiɛlɛ juät. Kɛ kui̱c ɛmɔ /ciɛ raan maarä diɛn."
entries.english_sentence: The neighbours reasoned together.They agreed, "The birds are right. Ajao has no feathers. So, he is not their relative."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ram kɛl kä kɛ cuɛ wee, "Jɛn bɛ yi̱k ɛ raan kuɔ̱ɔ̱ni. Jɛn ta̱a̱dɛ cäätdɛ ni kɛ."
entries.english_sentence: One of them said, "He must be part of the family of rats. He looks like them."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn ji̱ thieekä cukɛ wä kä kuɔ̱ɔ̱n kä laar kɛn ɛ i̱, "Ram kɛl kä ji̱ dhɔaarun cɛ li̱w."
entries.english_sentence: The neighbours went and called the rats saying, "One of your family is dead."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn kuɔ̱ɔ̱n cukɛ ben kä cu kɛnɛ nɛn ɛ Jɔk."Nɛmɛ ley /ciɛ ram kɛl kä ji̱ dhɔaaran."
entries.english_sentence: The rats came and saw that it was Ajao.They said, "This animal is not part of our family."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "Ɛni raan kä ji̱ dhɔaara tëkɛ juäl. Jɔk thiɛlɛ juäl."Kuɔ̱ɔ̱n cu jiɛɛni kɛn.
entries.english_sentence: "Everyone in our family has a tail. Ajao has no tail."The rats went away.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Thilɛ nɛy ti ca jek ti maar kɛ Jɔk kä jɛn cuɛ ŋot /ka̱nɛ kony.
entries.english_sentence: No relations were found for Ajao and he remained unburied.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mɛmɛ ɛ Rialgiɛɛr.Rialgiɛɛr cɔɔlɛ jio̱kdɛ.
entries.english_sentence: This is Lekishon.Lekishon is calling his dog.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rialgiɛɛr kɛnɛ jio̱kdɛ wäkɛ yien ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k kɛ naŋdiɛn laak.Kä cäŋ lethɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Lekishon and his dog are going to graze the animals.The sun is hot.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rialgiɛɛr kɛnɛ jio̱kdɛ ci rɛw kɛnɛ buɔth kɛ näk.
entries.english_sentence: Lekishon and his dog are thirsty and hungry.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn cikɛ wä go̱r pi̱i̱ni.
entries.english_sentence: They go to look for water.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rialgiɛɛr ci pöör ciökni ɣɔ̱ɔ̱kɛ bath.
entries.english_sentence: Lekishon loses track of his cows.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rialgiɛɛr cuɛ tok ni wiee.
entries.english_sentence: Lekishon starts to cry.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn cuɛ mɛk ni ɣöö bikɛ wä cieŋ kɛnɛ jio̱kdɛ.
entries.english_sentence: He decides to go home with his dog.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn ɣɔ̱k cua duɔ̱ɔ̱p ciëŋ jek!Rialgiɛɛr kɛnɛ jio̱kdɛ cu lo̱ckiɛn tɛɛth ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: The cows found the way home!Lekishon and his dog are very happy.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, Gatdet kɛnɛ man cikɛ wä duel kuɔth.Kä kääp man tëtdɛ min jälkɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Luwo went to church with his mother.She was holding his hand on the path.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rɛy duëël kuɔth tëëkɛ nɛy ti ŋuan ti te kitdä.
entries.english_sentence: Inside the church there were many people gathered.They were singing.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ rɔɔdɛ kual raar kä /ken man ɛ nɛn.
entries.english_sentence: Luwo left the church.His mother didn't see him.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ cuɔ̱ŋ dup kä cuɛ piny guic.Cuɛ wee, "Kä duɔ̱p dhɔara ja nikä?"
entries.english_sentence: Luwo stood in the path.He looked down the path, and thought, "Where is my house?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ wä dup kɛl. Cuɛ duel mi di̱i̱t nɛn.Cuɛ nyɔk kɛ guec, cuɛ wee, "Ɣëy, /ciɛ jɛn dhɔra. Dhɔra thilɛ duel mi di̱i̱t mi ce̱tkɛ nɛmɛ."
entries.english_sentence: So, he followed the path. He saw a big house."No, that's not our house. Our house is small."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ wee kɛ ja̱l. Cuɛ duel mi ca la̱t kɛ ciök nɛn. Cuɛ wee i̱, "Nɛmɛ derɛ kula jɛn dhɔra?"Cuɛ wee, "Ɣëy, /ciɛ jɛn dhɔra. Dhɔra thilɛ bilɛ mi ca la̱t kɛ ciök."
entries.english_sentence: Luwo walked a bit more. He saw a house on stilts."No, that's not our house. Our house is not on stilts."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ ŋuot kɛ mi wëë kɛ wä. Cuɛ dhɔr mi tekɛ duel mi tɔt mi /ka̱n pänydɛ buth nɛn.Cuɛ leni wee i̱, "Ɣëy, /ciɛ jɛn dhɔra. Dhɔra tëkɛ duel mi ca pänydɛ buth kɛ mun."
entries.english_sentence: He kept on walking. He saw a small house of straw."No, that's not our house. Our house has mud walls."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ räth nhiam. Cuɛ dhɔr mi tɔt mi tekɛ jiath kɛl nɛn.Cuɛ leni wee i̱, "Ɣëy, /ciɛ jɛn dhɔra. Dhɔra tëkɛ jɛn da̱ŋ rɛw."
entries.english_sentence: Luwo went farther. He saw a small house with a tree outside."No, that's not our house. Our house has two trees outside."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔrɛ cuɛ man nɛn bë kä jɛ. Cuɛ riŋ kä jɛ.Cu man ɛ jiök i̱, "Wanɛ cieŋ!"
entries.english_sentence: At last Luwo saw his mother coming toward him. Luwo ran to her.His mother said, "Let's go home!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ man thiec i̱, "Dhɔran ɛ mindiɛn?"
entries.english_sentence: Which house is Luwo's house?
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu mandi̱t ni cäŋ ɛ car i̱ bɛ nyiman ni pay gui̱l. Kä pay cieŋɛ nhial kui̱c in dɔ̱ŋ.Cu cäŋ pua̱r jiök i̱, "Bä luny jɔk kɛ pɛ̈th."
entries.english_sentence: Mother Sun decided to visit her sister, Moon. Sister Moon lives on the other side of the sky."I will be back soon," said Sun to the clouds.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci cäŋ jiɛɛn, cu pääm tarɛ ni wuɔ̱thnikiɛn ti bo̱o̱r la̱th.
entries.english_sentence: When Sun left, the mountains put on their white scarves.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu jiɔam tekɛ ŋaknom kɛnɛ jɛn. Cu jɛn gaak.Cu kɛ ji̱thkiɛn yuɔr kä cukɛ gua̱a̱th thiäŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Wind had an argument with the trees. The trees became angry.They threw their leaves all over the place.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu nhial ma̱a̱r tuok. Cuɛ luɔc ɛla mi cuor.
entries.english_sentence: The sky started to grumble.She turned grey.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu pua̱a̱r gaak kɛ nën kä ti diaal ɛ tɔ̱.Cukɛ wiee tuok. Cuɛ tekɛ mer ti ŋuan.
entries.english_sentence: The clouds were sad to see all this.They started crying. There were many tears.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu wi̱c muɔ̱ɔ̱n kɛɛliw di̱ŋ tuok piny pi̱i̱ni.
entries.english_sentence: The whole world began to sink under water.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ gua̱a̱th mi tɔt, kui̱c in dɔ̱ŋ cu cäŋ rɔɔdɛ rialikä bänyɛ nyiman piny.Cuɛ pay cim nerɛ jɛ kä cuɛ wä cieŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Meanwhile, on the other side of the sky, Sun was ready to leave her sister.She kissed Moon goodbye and went home.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu nhial lɔcdɛ tɛɛth kɛ nën ca̱ŋ mi luoc rɔɔdɛ ɛla mi yel mi riaŋriaŋ.Cu pääm bieynikiɛn tin gɔw tin tɔɔc la̱a̱th.
entries.english_sentence: Sky was so happy to see Sun that she turned bright blue.The mountains put on their pretty green dresses.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu jiɔam wä tɔ̱ɔ̱c.Cu jɛn yuankiɛn riny kä cu dɛykiɛn duɔth.
entries.english_sentence: The wind went to sleep.The trees stretched their branches and smiled.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu pua̱a̱r lo̱ckiɛn tɛɛth kɛ nendiɛn kɛ cäŋ.Cukɛ wä ŋar.
entries.english_sentence: The clouds were very happy to see mother Sun again.They went away to play.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu juaac tin tɔani päl piny wee kɛn i̱, "Ɣa̱a̱y."Cu wi̱c muɔ̱ɔ̱n kɛɛliw rɔ lɛp.
entries.english_sentence: Lots of little plants popped out of the earth to say, "Hello."The whole world sparkled.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: The day the Sun went away
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu cäŋ buaydɛ lɛ̈p gua̱thni diaal."Cuɛ wee cä lar yɛ i̱ bä luny jɔk," cuɛ kɛ buum.
entries.english_sentence: Mother Sun shined her light everywhere."I told you I would be back," she beamed.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuay ɛ guar nyaal mi puɔl ce̱tni kɛ jiɔm.Jɛn nhɔkɛ ɣöö bɛ to̱k dɔl, ni ciaŋ la ɣɔ̱nɛ jɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛn ɣöö bɛ ŋɔaani tin ca la̱rɛ la̱t.
entries.english_sentence: Fati was a little girl who ran like the wind.She loved to laugh, and always tried hard to do as she was told.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cäŋ kɛl, Nyabuay cuɛ wä kɛɛl kɛ man kɛnɛ gua̱n kɛ gör tɔɔŋni.
entries.english_sentence: One day, Fati went with her mother and father to look for firewood.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuay nhɔkɛ ɣöö bɛ man kɛnɛ gua̱n luäk, duŋdɛ ɣöö lät di̱tdɛ kä tin guicɛ ŋuan kɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ.Tëëkɛ diit, kɛ gɔakni kɛnɛ puɔ̱ɔ̱r nhial!
entries.english_sentence: Fati liked to help her mother and father, but there was so much to do and so much to see.There were birds, monkeys, and the sky!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu man wee, "Nyabuay, liŋ ɣä! Ji̱n go̱rni tɔɔŋ gua̱a̱th ɛmɛ kɛnɛ thɔ̱ŋɛ mi̱i̱.
entries.english_sentence: Mother said, "Fati, please listen! You can look for firewood here and you can look for firewood there."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "Duŋdɛ ɣöö Nyabuay, guicɛ in gua̱th wi̱ thi̱n kä tit rɔ."Jɛn cuɛ loc, "Gɔaaɛ ma."
entries.english_sentence: "But Fati, please watch where you go and be very careful."She replied, "Yes, mother."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔrɛ man Nyabuay kɛnɛ gua̱n cu teni wuɔ̱thkiɛn rɛy la̱t ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Soon Fati's mother and father were very busy.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn cua tɔɔŋ ti dhökdhöök jek.Kɛn cua tɔɔŋ ti ciɛwciɛɛw jek.
entries.english_sentence: They found big pieces of firewood.They found small pieces of firewood.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuay bä te wi̱cdɛ ni tɔɔŋni.Jɛn cuɛ tɔɔŋ ti ciɛwciɛɛw jek.Jɛn cuɛ tɔɔŋ ti ciɛwciɛɛw ɛlɔ̱ŋ jek.
entries.english_sentence: Fati was also very busy.She found small pieces of firewood.She found very small pieces of firewood.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Niɛ wa̱nɔ Nyabuay cuɛ nhial liɛc.Cuɛ dit mi dɛ̈ɛ̈r nɛn rɛy juaacni ti ba̱rba̱a̱r.
entries.english_sentence: Then Fati looked up.She saw a red bird in the tall grass.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔrɛ, Nyabuay cuɛ piny liɛc.Cuɛ muarmuar nɛn rɛy duɔ̱p.
entries.english_sentence: Next, Fati looked down.She saw a brown ant on the dusty path.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuay cuɛ ji̱th jiaath mi tekɛ lɔ̱ɔ̱l nɛn. Ɛn ji̱th jiaath riaŋɛ kä ɛ mi tɔ̱c.Jɛn cuɛ yiatdɛ kɛl kuëŋ wi̱i̱ ji̱thä jiaath in tekɛ lɔ̱ɔ̱l.
entries.english_sentence: Fati saw a beautiful leaf. The leaf was shiny and green.She put one finger on the beautiful leaf.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuay cuɛ wee, "Nɛmɛ /cɛ cäätkɛ ji̱th jiaath."Kɛ pɛ̈th, ɛn ji̱th jiaath cuɛ rɔɔdɛ wany. Nyabuay cuɛ wee, "Mɛmɛ /ciɛ ji̱th jiaath. Nɛmɛ ɛ thɔ̱l mi tɔ̱c!"
entries.english_sentence: Fati said, "This does not feel like a leaf." Suddenly, the beautiful leaf moved!Fati said, "This is not a beautiful leaf. This is a green snake!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuay cuɛ wak, "Ayööw!"Jɛn cuɛ kɛ riŋkɛ pɛ̈th kɛ gör man kɛnɛ gua̱n.
entries.english_sentence: Fati screamed, "Eii!"She ran very fast to look for her mother and father.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuay cuɛ gua̱n nɛn kä wakɛ, "Ɛ thɔ̱l! Ɛ thɔ̱l!"Gua̱n cuɛ wee i̱, "Ja nikä? Ja nikä?"Nyabuay cuɛ wee i̱, "Wi̱nɛ mi! Wi̱nɛ mi!"
entries.english_sentence: Fati shouted, "A snake! A snake!"Father said, "Where? Where?"Fati said, "There! There!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔrɛ cu gua̱n thɔ̱l ɛ tɔ̱c ɛmɔ joc kɛ kɛɛt.Ɛn thɔ̱l in tɔ̱c ɛmɔ cuɛ rɔɔdɛ cu bar.
entries.english_sentence: Then her father chased the green snake with a stick.The green snake slithered away.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Gua̱n cuɛ wee, "Ji̱n ci kään can wä kä muɔɔr kä biɛ wä la̱t duŋ thɔ̱a̱lbelä."
entries.english_sentence: Father said, "Fati, you are safe.Let's go to mother and tell her about the green snake."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu man wee, "Ci lɔcdä tɛɛth kɛ ɣöö /kenɛ ji̱ kac ɛn thɔ̱lbelä ɛ."
entries.english_sentence: Mother said, "Fati, I am happy the green snake did not bite you."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Duŋdɛ mi wëë rɔɔdɛ loc, "Ji̱n, guic gua̱th in wi̱i̱ thi̱n. Kä bi rɔ cu tit ɛlɔ̱ŋ."Nɔmɔ cuɛ cua̱ jɛn thuɔ̱k dɛ.
entries.english_sentence: "But next time, please, look where you go, and be more careful."And that was the end of that.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Dämaar in tɔt la ninɛ kɛ jɔak.Ɣän la kërä kɛ nhiam, kɛ ɣöö ɛ ɣän mi di̱i̱t!
entries.english_sentence: My little brother sleeps late.I wake early,  because I am great!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛ ɣän la lɛp cäŋ rɛc ɔ.
entries.english_sentence: I am the one who lets in the sun.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Maar cuɛ jɛ lar i̱, "Ɛ ji̱n ci̱er bakädä."
entries.english_sentence: "You're my morning star," says Ma.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän lakä rɔɔdä ni ciaŋ, /ci ɣän luäk a göörä.
entries.english_sentence: I wash myself every day,  I don't need any help.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän /cä diɛɛr mi kɔ̱c pi̱, kiɛ thabuuny la̱k bieyni min tɔ̱c.
entries.english_sentence: I don't mind cold water, or the blue soap that washes clothes.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ci maar jɛ tiem ɣä, "/Cu lɛcku päl ruëëc."Cua̱ jɛ loc i̱, "/Cɛ de tuɔɔk kä ɣä!"
entries.english_sentence: Ma reminds me,  "Don't forget your teeth."I reply,  "Never,  not me!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔr la̱k, cuɔ gua̱ndɔɔŋ kɛnɛ maalen ner.Cuɔ kɛ jio̱k i̱ bia buut kɛ mal.
entries.english_sentence: After washing,  I greet Grandpa and Auntie.I wish them a good day.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɔ rɔɔdä moc kɛ bieyni.Cuɔ maar jiök i̱, "Ci ɣän di̱t ɛn tämɛ."
entries.english_sentence: Then I dress myself."I'm big now, Ma," I say.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän lua̱ŋä kueŋ dhura̱a̱ri kɛnɛ yiɛn depni wa̱a̱rikä.
entries.english_sentence: I can close my buttons and buckle my shoes.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän la göörä ɣöö dedämaar lääri duëlgɔ̱rä diaal ŋa̱c.
entries.english_sentence: I make sure my brother knows all the school news.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rɛy ki̱lɛ̈thä la la̱tdä ɛ bum kɛ dupdiaal.
entries.english_sentence: In class I do my best in every way.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän la la̱tdä ti gɔw ti̱ti̱ ni ciaŋ.Duŋdɛ ɣöö min nhɔakä ɛlɔ̱ŋ, ɛ ŋar mi di̱i̱t!
entries.english_sentence: I do all these good things every day.But the thing I like most,  is to play and play!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, tëëkɛ tut manpalɛ̈k kɛnɛ pelpɛl ti määth ti gɔw ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Once upon a time, there was Rooster and Hare.They were good friends.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ wäär kɛl, cu Pɛlpɛl Tut Manpalɛ̈k gui̱l kɛnɛ ji̱ dhɔarɛ.Cukɛ mi̱i̱th kɛ kuän thiaŋ kɛɛl kä cu lo̱ckiɛn tɛɛth ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: One night, Hare visited Rooster and his family.They enjoyed supper together.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä mëë ci gua̱a̱th tɔ̱cä cop, cu Tut Manpalɛ̈k kɛnɛ ji̱ dhɔaarɛ mal niɛn.Duŋdɛ ɣöö /ken Pɛlpɛl wuɔ̱thkiɛn nɛn.
entries.english_sentence: When it was bedtime, Rooster and his family soon fell asleep.Hare could not see their heads.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Tut Manpalɛ̈k kɛnɛ ji̱ dhɔaarɛ cikɛ niɛn ɛlɔ̱ŋ.Kä ɛn pɛlpɛl /kenɛ niɛn kɛ wäär kɛ liw.
entries.english_sentence: Rooster and his family slept very well.Hare was not able to sleep the whole night.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ runwaŋ, cu Pɛlpɛl ɛ görɛ ɛn ɣöö bɛ tɛ̱̈ɛ̱̈ Tut Manpalɛ̈k ŋa̱c."Cia wuɔthkun la̱th nikä thiaŋ?" ci Pɛlpɛl thiec.
entries.english_sentence: In the morning, Hare wanted to know Rooster's secret."Where do you put your heads at night?" he asked.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Tut Manpalɛ̈k ɛ gör ɛn ɣöö kaŋɛ Pɛlpɛl.Cuɛ lar i̱, "Mi wä nɛy tɔ̱c, la nɛy wuɔth a woc. Mi tɔ̱c nɛy ɛ thil wuɔth, la nɛy a nin a gɔaa ɛlɔ̱ŋ."
entries.english_sentence: Rooster decided to play a joke on Hare.He said, "At bedtime, we chop off our heads. Without heads, we sleep very well."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "Kä mi ci ɣɔw baak, la nɛy wuɔthkɔ la loc gua̱a̱thnikiɛn," ci Tut Manpalɛ̈k ɛ lar.
entries.english_sentence: "Then in the morning, we put our heads back on," explained Rooster.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Pɛlpɛl loc dhɔrɛ kä cuɛ ji̱ dhɔaarɛ la̱a̱r tɛ̱̈ɛ̱̈ in te kɛ Tut Manpalɛ̈k.Cu Pɛlpɛl kɛnɛ ji̱ dhɔaarɛ jɛ gör ɛn ɣöö bikɛ jɛ ɣɔ̱ɔ̱n. Ɛŋu diwi bi tuɔk kɛ kɔrɛ?
entries.english_sentence: Hare went home and told his family about the rooster's secret.The Hare family decided to try it themselves. What do you think happened?
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Nhial ɛ wut mi deep rɛc
entries.nuer_sentence: Nhial ɛ wut mi deep rɛc rɛy kiɛɛr kä Yakuac.
entries.english_sentence: This is Jaaka the fisherman from Naminya.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Nhial ɛ wut mi deep rɛc
entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn la wëë dëp kiir Pibo̲o̱r.
entries.english_sentence: He fishes on the river Nile.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Nhial ɛ wut mi deep rɛc
entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn tëëkɛ riey, buɔyɛ kɛnɛ thokkɛl.
entries.english_sentence: He has a boat, fishing net and a hook.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Nhial ɛ wut mi deep rɛc
entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn la keerɛ nikɛ runwaŋ ni ciaŋ kä bɛ wä dëp kɛ ca̱a̱l rɛy kiɛɛr.
entries.english_sentence: He always wakes up very early in the morning to catch the Nile perch.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Nhial ɛ wut mi deep rɛc
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ thaak wäl kɛ runwaŋ, jɛn la kɔkɛ rɛc tin cɛ dɛp kä thuk Yakuac.
entries.english_sentence: At around 10am, he's selling his catch in Jinja central market.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Nhial ɛ wut mi deep rɛc
entries.nuer_sentence: Nhial, ɛŋu ci tuɔɔk? Ci lɔcdɛ jiääk ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Jaaka what happened? Was it a loss?He's so sad.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Nhial ɛ wut mi deep rɛc
entries.nuer_sentence: "Ɛn wa̱lɛ ɛ cäŋ mi jiääk. Ɛn muaŋ kiɛɛr cɛ ɣä pën dëp, kä ci ca̱a̱l thokkɛlä bät!"
