entries.english_sentence: "Today the situation is bad. The Nile breeze did not permit me to fish. And one perch swam away with my hook."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Nhial ɛ wut mi deep rɛc
entries.nuer_sentence: "Duŋdɛ ni ɣöö ɣän ŋa̱thä jɛ iruun dɔ̱ŋ bɛ gɔaa, kɛ ɣöö cä thokkɛl mi pay täth kɔk."
entries.english_sentence: "But I have hope that tomorrow will be good, because I've bought a new hook."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan, Yak kɛnɛ Muul cieŋ kɛ gekä ciëŋ mi thiääk kɛ rɛ̈ɛ̈k.Cukɛ röm ɛ gäc kä cukɛ la mäthni.
entries.english_sentence: Once upon a time, Hyena and Donkey lived near a city.They met by chance and became friends.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kɛn car ciɛɛŋä mat piny ɛn ɣöö bi kɛn la nyue̱k kɛɛl, kä bi kɛn rɔɔdiɛn gaŋ kɛɛl.
entries.english_sentence: They made an agreement to share food, and to defend themselves together.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu kɛn ŋɔak diaal a lät kɛɛl.Cu kɛn ɛ tok amäni ɣöö cieŋ kɛn kɛɛl.
entries.english_sentence: They did everything together.They even started living together.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, cukɛ wä thok yiëër wäkɛ maath kɛ pi̱.Mëë tekɛ dup, jäl kɛ muɔŋ kä dɔalkɛ to̱k.
entries.english_sentence: One day, they went to a river to drink water.On their way, they were chatting and laughing.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë cikɛ cop thok yiëër, cu Muul wä wi̱i̱ lo̱o̱nyä kä cuɛ wä maath thi̱n.Kä cu Yak maath tuk lo̱o̱nyä.
entries.english_sentence: At the river, Donkey went downwards and was drinking downstream.Hyena was drinking upstream.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ gua̱a̱th mi tɔt, cu Yak rɔɔdɛ ka̱p cuɔ̱ŋ mäth.Cuɛ duɔ̱r cak. Cuɛ Muul jiök i̱, "Ɛŋu tuupi pi̱ ɔ?"
entries.english_sentence: Suddenly, Hyena stopped drinking.He complained, "Donkey, why are you stirring up the water?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Muul biɛt nikɛ biɛtdɛ kä wä ni jɛn kɛ mi mäth jɛn.
entries.english_sentence: Donkey kept silent and continued to drink.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu Yak kɛ̈c."Ji̱n /ci li̱ŋ? Ruac ni ɣän kɛ ji̱, Muul." Cu Yak kac nhial kɛ jɔw mi di̱i̱t.
entries.english_sentence: Hyena was very angry."Don't you listen? I'm talking to you, Donkey," shouted Hyena.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Muul Yak di̱el guec kä cuɛ loc i̱, "Ɛ winith ci pi̱ kɔn jiɛɛnɔ kä päl löny ɛ ba löny lor ɛ kɛn?"
entries.english_sentence: Donkey looked at Hyena and asked, "Since when did water move from downstream to upstream?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu Yak ɛ loc i̱, "Kɛn pi̱ ca löny pay lor ɛ kɛn ni kɛ cäŋ ëë ci kɔn määth tok."Cuɛ go̱r ɛn ɣöö bɛ Muul cam.
entries.english_sentence: Hyena replied, "Water started to flow upstream when we became friends."Hyena had decided to eat Donkey.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci Muul ɛ guic ɛn ɣöö cɛ thiɛl lua̱ŋ, cuɛ wee i̱, "Ɛ duerä kɛ ɣöö ci guic ɛla määthdä. Cɛ gɔaa, cam ni ɣä."
entries.english_sentence: Helplessly, Donkey said, "It is my fault for thinking we could be friends. Alright, eat me then."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Yak rɔ yuɔ̱r Muul kä cuɛ tööl piny.
entries.english_sentence: Hyena jumped up and grabbed Donkey.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Tuut bärɛ, kä ɛ dho̱o̱l mi ci̱w kä tekä bok 3.Jɛn la nhɔkɛ laath ko̱tdä mi bärbär mëë ca ka̱m jɛ ɛ näärɛ ni Cuɔɔl.
entries.english_sentence: Parna was a tall, slender boy who was in Grade 3.He liked to wear the long black coat that his Uncle Teteyo gave him.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä gua̱a̱th mi ca duelgɔ̱rä gäk, Tuut la wëë yieen ɣɔ̱ɔ̱kiɛn.
entries.english_sentence: During holiday time, Parna looked after his parents' cows.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cäŋ kɛl, Tuut mëë tëë yien ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k, cuɛ nhiaal tok kɛ wuɔc piny.
entries.english_sentence: One day, as Parna looked after the cows, it suddenly started raining.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Niɛ wa̱nɔ mɔ, yaŋ in nhɔk gua̱n ni jɛ, Cäär, cuɛ dieth.Kɛ dɔw mi gɔaa ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛlɔ̱ŋ mi /ken Tuut ɛ met nɛn ni wal.
entries.english_sentence: Just at that time, his father's favourite cow, Blackie, gave birth.The calf was the most beautiful calf Parna had ever seen.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Tuut cu lɔcdɛ tɛɛth ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ juëcdɛ kɛ Cäär kɛnɛ dɔwdɛ kä cuɛ tha̱a̱ŋ ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k tin kɔ̱kiɛn pa̱l ruëëc.
entries.english_sentence: Parna was so happy caring for Blackie and the calf that he forgot about the rest of the cows.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn cuɛ car ni ɣöö, "Gua̱a̱r cɛ rɔ yac i̱ bɛ ɣä ka̱m dɔw mi wëë wa̱a̱ ŋuɔ̱ɔ̱t."
entries.english_sentence: He thought, "Father promised to give the calf to me if it is female."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rɛy cärädɛ nɔmɔ, cuɛ jakä bum ɛ bɛ tetkɛ kap nhial, Tuut cuɛ näärɛ ni Cuɔɔl nɛn, kä cuɛ duŋ ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k tim, "Nääran, ɣɔ̱k ɛ ni?"
entries.english_sentence: As he daydreamed, a strong hand pulled him up.Parna saw Uncle Teteyo and remembered, "Uncle, where are the cows?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Näärɛ ni Tut cuɛ loc, "Muɔɔr cɛ ɣɔ̱k diaal yian ɛ cikɛ wä luaak, ci duɔthni ji̱n yɛnɛ Cäär."Jɛn cɛ diɛɛr bä, kä cɛ ɣä ja̱k kɛ göru."
entries.english_sentence: Uncle Teteyo replied, "Your mother found all the cows in the shed, except Blackie, and you.She was afraid so she sent me to fetch you."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Tuut cuɛ lɔcdɛ tɛɛth kɛ lärɛ näärɛ i̱ ci Cäär dieth kɛ dɔw mi gɔaa ɛlɔ̱ŋ.Cu näärɛ wee, "Ɣän bä kɔ̱a̱l kap, kä bia ɣä guɔ̱ɔ̱r yɛnɛ Cäär."
entries.english_sentence: Parna excitedly told his uncle how Blackie gave birth to the beautiful calf.Uncle Teteyo said, "I'll carry the calf as you and Blackie follow."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nɛy diaal cu lo̱ckiɛn tɛɛth mëë ca Tuut nɛn kɛnɛ kɔ̱a̱l ɛ puɔl pua̱nykiɛn.
entries.english_sentence: Everyone was happy to see Parna, Blackie and the calf safe.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Tuut cuɛ gua̱n thiec, "Ji̱n bi ɣä ka̱m dɔw yaaŋ ce̱tkɛ mëë ci lar?"
entries.english_sentence: Parna asked his father, "Will you let me have the calf as you promised?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "Ɣää, gatdä, jɛn ɛ duŋdu ni kärɔa. Ɛn yäc ɛni ya̱c."
entries.english_sentence: "Yes, my son, she is all yours. A promise is a promise."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan tëëkɛ kuɔ̱ɔ̱n da̱ŋ rɛw ti määth.Kun kɛl cieŋɛ dɔɔr.
entries.english_sentence: Once upon a time, there lived two rats.One rat lived in the bush.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä kun in dɔ̱ŋ ciɛŋɛ ni ciëŋ.
entries.english_sentence: The other rat lived in a house.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cäŋ kɛl, cu kun in ciɛŋ ni ciëŋ kun in cieŋ dɔɔr jiök i̱, "Ji̱n la cami ni ti jiäk, kä la tɔ̱ci gua̱th mi jiääk kä la lua̱nykɛ ji̱ ɛ nhiaal."
entries.english_sentence: One day, the rat that lived in the house said to the rat that lived in the bush, "You eat badly, sleep badly, and it rains on you.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä kɔn la tɔ̱ɔ̱c nɛy duel kua̱r. Kä la mi̱th nɛy kɛ mi̱i̱th ti ŋuan. Bër kä biɛ lɛ wä nɛn.Cu kun in cieŋ dɔɔr wee i̱, "Ɣän bä me̱t ben ɛn wääri. Cä rɔdä rialikä."
entries.english_sentence: "But, we sleep in chief's houses. We eat many different foods. Come and see.""I will come tonight. I'm ready," said the bush rat.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu gua̱n ciëŋ ŋɔ̱a̱ŋ. Cuɛ wee i̱, "Kɛn kuɔ̱ɔ̱n ti̱ti̱ la camkɛ kuändä ti, ci kɛn ɛ bi nyɔk, bi kɛnɛ nɛn!"Cuɛ kɛ dɛp kɛ kam. Cuɛ thoker la̱th thuok kamä.
entries.english_sentence: Meanwhile, the owner of the house was furious. He cursed, "These rats that eat my food, they will see!"This time, he set a trap with sugar.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kuɔ̱ɔ̱n cop dueel. "Bä kɛn ben mi̱th kɛ kuan tin cuɔmcuɔm tin gɔw tin kɔɔn."Kä kɛn jälkɛ kɛ mi dɔalkɛ to̱o̱k i̱, "Cucu ci̱ci̱ cɛcɛ!"
entries.english_sentence: The rats came in to eat the goodies in the house.They came laughing, "Chuchu chichi cheche!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë cikɛ cop guäth in ca kɛ dɛp thi̱n kɛ thoker, cu kun in ciɛŋ ni ciëŋ wee i̱, "A kɔanä met ɛ ɣän ɛn thoker ɛmɛ. Biɛ kulɛ nɛn ɛn cuomcuom ɛla cam nɛyɛ mɔ."
entries.english_sentence: When they reached the trap the house rat said, "Let me taste this sugar. You see the goodies we eat here."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä ɛ ŋuot /kän kun thoker ni bil, cu kam ɛ käp ɛ kup, tak!Cu kam ɛ kääp cɛ ni widɛ, kä cu wäŋkɛ käny raar ce̱tkɛ dɛy bandhorä.
entries.english_sentence: But before the rat could take the sugar, the trap snapped, PA!The trap caught the rat's head, and his eyes bulged like eggplants.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kun in cieŋ dɔɔr ɛ guic, kä cuɛ ga̱a̱y ɛlɔ̱ŋ.Cuɛ wee i̱, "Ɣëy ɣëë! Mäthdä, kä ɛ mi tetdi la cam kɛ mɔ ɛ bi nyin ran käny raar inɛ mɔ?"
entries.english_sentence: The bush rat just looked, amazed.He said, "E. Heee! My friend, which goodies did you eat that made your eyes pop out like this?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä /ken kun in ciɛŋ ni ciëŋ ɛ luoc.
entries.english_sentence: But the house rat could not reply.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kun in cieŋ dɔɔr kun in ciɛŋ ni ciëŋ ba̱ny piny kä cuɛ wee i̱, "Ɣaa! Nyinkun ti gɔw ɛ ti la camkɛ ɛ bi nyin ran käny raar inɛ mɛ /ka̱nɛ ŋa̱c i̱ dëë me̱t te rɛydiɛn."
entries.english_sentence: The bush rat left the house saying, "Haa! I will not manage these goodies you praise."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Dhɔɔru mi jiääk gɔaa ni jɛn kä dhɔr määthdu mi gɔaa.
entries.english_sentence: Your worst home is better than your neighbour's best home.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Ci gua̱a̱r ɣä naŋ rɛɛk kɛ thurbila mɛ ye̱l in dɔaaŋ.Cu nɛy cuɔ̱ŋ römni duɔ̱pni liɛpkɔ ɣöö ba nɛy lëp nuur in tɔ̱c min nyuoth ɣöö dëë kɔ räth dupda.
entries.english_sentence: My father took me to town in our old blue car.We stopped at a big roundabout for the lights to turn green.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Cua nyami jäl kɛ gëk duɔ̱p nɛn.Jälɛ kɛ bi̱y mi yian mi gɔaa.
entries.english_sentence: I saw a lady walking on the side of the road.She was wearing a beautiful bright orange dress.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Cɛ lɛ̈tdɛ yiɛn kɛ la̱a̱k mi do̱l.
entries.english_sentence: She had a big red belt around her waist.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Rɔmɛ bɛ̈k mi yian mi bilbil kɛ tëtdɛ.
entries.english_sentence: In her hand, she carried a shiny little orange purse.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Jälɛ kɛ wa̱a̱ri ti yia̱ni ti tekɛ thäär ti ba̱rba̱a̱r.
entries.english_sentence: She wore a pair of shiny orange high-heeled shoes.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ cuɔ̱ŋ kä cuɛ miem wecdɛ tin ba̱rba̱a̱r thiap.Caakɛ yiɛn thaariɛn kɛ yieen miemni.
entries.english_sentence: She stopped and touched her long hair.It was held together in the middle with a hairpin.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä mëë ɛ jɛni luonyɛ yien miemkɛ, cu bɛ̈kdɛ pɛ̈ɛ̈n.Cua wee, "Wuu!" kɛ ɣöö ci lɔcdä jiääk kɛ min ci tuɔk kä jɛ.
entries.english_sentence: As she fixed her hairpin, her purse fell down."Ooh," I said feeling bad for her.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu nyal rɔ guoŋ kä kuanyɛ bɛ̈kdɛ.
entries.english_sentence: The lady bent to pick up her purse.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Cua tiɛljieth mi yian mi bäär nɛn guäth in cuothɛ tuur bɛkädɛ.
entries.english_sentence: She cleaned the dust off her purse.I saw long orange earrings.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu nuur in tɔ̱c ben kä cu thurbila tɛth piny.Cua ŋuotkɛ mi la guɛcä jɔkdä.
entries.english_sentence: The lights changed green, and our car drove off.I kept looking behind.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu gua̱a̱r ɣä thiec, "Ɛŋu mi guici?"
entries.english_sentence: "What are you looking at?" my father asked.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ciek in tekɛ bi̱y in yian
entries.nuer_sentence: Cua jɛ jiök i̱, "Guɛcä ni ciek in tekɛ bi̱y ɛ yian in daan."La caarä ni biɛl mi yian kɛ ni̱n diaal ni ciaŋ.
entries.english_sentence: "At the lady in orange," I said.I thought of the colour orange all day.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Lony ci rɛw ɛ näk, cuɛ jiɛɛn wëë maath kɛ pi̱ rɛy puɔ̱ɔ̱l.
entries.english_sentence: Lion is thirsty, so he goes to get a drink of water from the pond.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ cop rɛy pi̱i̱ni kä cuɛ maath kɛ pi̱.
entries.english_sentence: He goes into the water to take a drink.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Min ci Lony maath, ɛ jɛn i̱ bëë raar, cuɛ cuit rɛy tua̱a̱k!
entries.english_sentence: After drinking, Lion tries to get out.He is stuck in the mud!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ gua̱a̱th mi tɔt, cu Gɔɔk ben jälɛ kɛ gëk puɔ̱ɔ̱l.
entries.english_sentence: A moment later, Monkey comes walking by the pond.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Min ci Lony Gɔɔk nɛn, cuɛ jɛ jiök i̱, "Luäk ɣä!"
entries.english_sentence: Lion sees Monkey and calls out, "Help me!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ Lony ka̱m raar rɛy puɔ̱ɔ̱l.Cukɛ lɔ̱ɔ̱ŋ kɛn da̱ŋ rɛw ɛ määth.
entries.english_sentence: Monkey pulls Lion out of the pond.They both rest for a moment under a tree.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ gua̱a̱th in tekɛ lɔ̱ŋä, cu Lony buɔth ɛ näk.Cuɛ rɔɔdɛ riet Gɔɔk, kä cuɛ jɛ jiök i̱, "Ɛn täämɛ bi cam, ci buɔth ɣä näk!"
entries.english_sentence: While he is resting, Lion realises that he is hungry.He turns to Monkey and says, "I am hungry now, so I will eat you!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "Kä ɛŋu cämi ɣä kä lua̱kä ni ji̱?" cu Gɔɔk ɛ thiec.Cɛ ŋɛ̈ɛ̈r kɛ dual.
entries.english_sentence: "Why are you going to eat me after I just saved you?" Monkey asks.He is frightened.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ gua̱a̱th in ruac kɛn cu Wan cop.Cɛ ŋa̱c ɛn ɣöö nɛy ti̱ti̱ tekɛ kɛ riɛk.Cu Wan kɛ thiec, "Ɛŋu ci tuɔɔk ɔ?"
entries.english_sentence: As they are talking, Fox comes walking by.He can see there is a problem."What is wrong?" asks Fox.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä Gɔɔk ro̱tdɛ, cuɛ wee, "Lony cä luäk rɛy puɔ̱ɔ̱l in cɛ cuit thi̱n, kä ɛn täämɛ lɛnɛ lat ni ɣöö camɛ ɣä."Cɛ dual ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛn Gɔɔk /kenɛ ŋa̱c ɛn ɣöö derɛ rɔɔdɛ kän!
entries.english_sentence: Monkey cries, "I saved Lion and now he is going to eat me."Monkey is so scared that he doesn't realise he can save himself!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Wan nhial guic kä cuɛ jiath nɛn, cuɛ Gɔɔk jiök i̱, "Ji̱n guic nhial."Cu Gɔɔk nhial liɛc kä cuɛ jiath nɛn. Kä cuɛ rɔɔdɛ laŋ nhial wi̱c jiaath.Kɛ kɔr kä min cɛ rɔ laŋ wi̱c jiaath.
entries.english_sentence: Fox sees the tree. "Look up to the sky," he tells Monkey.Monkey looks up.He jumps into the tree and climbs to the top.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Wan rɔɔdɛ bar kɛ pɛ̈th kɛ ɣöö dɔ̱ŋ dëë cam ɛ Lony.
entries.english_sentence: Monkey is safe at the top of the tree.Fox quickly turns to run away before Lion can eat him.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan, Rueth kɛnɛ Lɛk kɛ Luth kɛ mäth.Luth ɛ rec mi muɔ̱lmuɔ̱l mi thiɛl maan. La kuëth kɛ jɛ ɛ mäthnikɛ. La kɛn a cɔl i̱ dɔ̱a̱a̱r.
entries.english_sentence: Long ago, Tilapia, Arowana, and Lungfish were friends.Lungfish was easygoing, and some thought he was ugly. His friends bullied him, calling him a fool.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Luth /ca la gakɛ kɛ mäthnikɛ.La jio̱kɛ nikɛ i̱, "Wutni, /ciɛ ɣän dɔ̱a̱a̱r, duŋdä kɔ̱a̱c."
entries.english_sentence: Lungfish would not get angry with his friends.Instead, he would tell them, "Guys, I am not a fool! I am just humble."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, cu ŋuɛ̈tni da̱ŋ diɔ̱k jiɛɛn wäkɛ ja̱l ni peek rööl mi na̱n.
entries.english_sentence: One day, the three friends decided to go on an adventure.They travelled to the far end of their country.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë tekɛ jäl, cukɛ röm kɛ dëëp rɛc. Cu dëëp rɛc käpdiɛn go̱r.Kɛ ɣöö Lɛk ɛ ŋuɛ̈t mi ri̱i̱r, cuɛ dëëp rɛc tin kɔn tɛŋ kä cuɛ leny.
entries.english_sentence: On their journey, they met a fisherman. The fisherman decided to catch them.Because Arowana was an energetic young fish, he managed to escape.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu Luth kään bä kɛ ɣöö tëëkɛ puɔ̱ny mi nyäthnyäth mi la cäät tet nath kä la käcɛ ji̱ tɛ̈rɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Lungfish got away because he has a slippery body.He easily slips from people's hands. He also has a habit of biting his enemies!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä inɔ, /ken Rueth kään, cua käp ɛ dëëp rɛc.Cu duɔth ni ŋuɛ̈tni da̱ŋ rɛw rɛy puɔ̱ɔ̱l mi tɔt, ɛ la Lɛk kɛnɛ Luth.
entries.english_sentence: However, Tilapia did not survive. The fisherman caught him.Now, only the two friends, Arowana and Lungfish, remained. They found themselves in a small pond.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ɛ kɛn i̱ lockɛ wi̱cdiɛn, cukɛ bath.Cukɛ gäk rɛy puɔ̱ɔ̱l in tɔt indaan.Kɛ Mäy, cu pi̱ puɔ̱ɔ̱l indaan wäkɛ mi do̱nkɛ.
entries.english_sentence: When they tried to return to their village, they could not find their way home.They were stuck in the pond!In summer, the pond started to dry up.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë cikɛ jɛ nɛn i̱ do̱n pul, cu Lɛk määthdɛ ni Luth thiec i̱, "Wut in dɔ̱a̱a̱r, ɛŋu mi bi kɔnɛ lɛl ɛn täämɛ mɛ do̱n pul ɛ?"Cu Luth jɛ luɔ̱c jɛ ni määth kɛ duɔɔth i̱, "Bi ramɔ wä cäpä gua̱n."
entries.english_sentence: When the two friends saw this, Arowana asked Lungfish, "What will we do now that the pond is drying up?"Lungfish replied softly with a smile, "Everyone should follow their father's plan."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä Lɛk kui̱cɛ min bɛ la̱t.Cu Luth jɛ tok kɛ mi rialɛ rɔ ikä. Cuɛ kɔ̱a̱a̱k mi lueŋ tɛt kä cuɛ mi̱th tin bɛ cam kɛ Mäy kɛɛliw kuëŋ thi̱n.
entries.english_sentence: Arowana did not know what to do.Lungfish started to prepare for drought. He began to dig a deep hole. He also started storing food.The pond became drier.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci pul do̱n, cu Lɛk li̱w kɛ buɔth kɛnɛ rɛw.Cu Luth wä rɛy kɔ̱kädɛ kä cuɛ thi̱i̱kdɛ ga̱k thi̱n.Mëë ci mi̱thkɛ thuɔ̱k, cuɛ juälɛ cam amäni mëë ci nhiaal dɛ̈m kä ci pul thia̱a̱ŋ kɛ pi̱ ɛ nyɔk.
entries.english_sentence: When the pond dried up, Arowana died.Meanwhile, Lungfish closed himself inside his hole.When he had finished all his food, he ate his own tail.Then it rained again, and the pond filled up.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Luth thi̱i̱kdɛ lɛp kä cuɛ ben raar rɛy kɔ̱kädɛ.Cuɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p wecdiɛn jek kä cuɛ loc wi̱c.Mëë cɛ cop wi̱cdiɛn, cu ji̱ dhɔaariɛn lo̱ckiɛn tɛɛth ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä cua lor kɛ bul mi di̱i̱t.
entries.english_sentence: Lungfish opened the door of his hole and came out.He found his way back to his village.Upon arrival, his people were so happy that they received him with a big celebration.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Ɛ rec indiɛn pɛl ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɔ?
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ca thiec kɛ min ci tuɔɔk, cuɛ kɛ la̱t min ci tuɔɔk kɛɛliw.Cu ji̱ dhɔaariɛn jɛ liak kɛ pɛ̈lɛ. Cu kɛn ɛ lar i̱ ɛ jɛn rec in pɛl ni jɛn rɛy rɛc diaal.Inɔ, /cu raan cany kɛ ta̱a̱ in guic i̱ ni puɔ̱nydɛ.
entries.english_sentence: When asked what happened, Lungfish narrated the whole story to the villagers.He was praised for his wisdom. They called him the wisest fish in the world.They learnt to never underestimate anybody because of their physical appearance or easygoing nature!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan tëëkɛ ley mi cɔal i̱ Wan kɛnɛ diit da̱ŋ rɛw. Kɛl cɔalɛ Tok, cɔal kɛl i̱ Jakɔ̱k.
entries.english_sentence: There once lived an animal called Fox, and two birds called Tok and Sparrow.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl ci Tok dap wi̱c jiaath.Kɛ kɔr ni̱ni ti tɔt cu Wan lɛ wä ja̱l rɛy dɔaar.Cuɛ Tok wä jek cɛ dap wi̱c jiaath.
entries.english_sentence: One day, Fox was walking around the bush.He discovered that Tok had laid eggs in a nest at the top of a tree.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ Tok jiök i̱, "Ɛ ji̱n Tok?"Cu Tok ɛ jiök i̱, "Ɛ jɛn ɣän!"
entries.english_sentence: He said, "Tok, do you have eggs in your nest?"Tok replied, "Yes, I do!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ Tok jiök i̱, "Göörä tuɔɔŋ. Mi /ciɛ jɛn, bä jiathdä jɔp ɛn täämɛ."Cu Tok jɛ moc kɛ tuɔɔŋ kɛl kä cuɛ loc jɔk.
entries.english_sentence: "Give me an egg, or I'm going to cut down this tree right now," said Fox.Tok gave him an egg and Fox went away.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ dɔ̱diɛn ɛ nyɔk, cu Wan rɔ nyɔk kɛ ben kä Tok jälɛ kɛ jio̱p muɔ̱ɔ̱ndɛ.Cuɛ Tok thiec, "Tok, jɔapä jiathdä kiɛ bi ɣä moc tuɔɔŋ?"Cu Tok ɛ lɛni nyɔk kɛ muɔ̱c tuɔɔŋ dɔ̱diɛn.
entries.english_sentence: The next day, Fox returned to Tok."Should I cut down this tree, or will you give me an egg?" asked Fox.Tok gave him an egg.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl cu Jakɔ̱k lɛ ben kä Tok, kä cuɛ Tok bä jek cɛ nuään ɛlɔ̱ŋ.Cuɛ Tok thiec i̱, "Ɛŋu mi ci nuän i̱ nɛmɛ?"
entries.english_sentence: When Sparrow came to visit Tok, she found her friend was very thin."Fox is threatening to cut down my tree with his axe," cried Tok.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Tok ɛ jiök, "Ɣaaaa!"Ca gaatkä thuk ɛ Wan. La bëë ni ciaŋ i̱ go̱o̱rɛ ɣöö bɛ jiath bä jɔp, bä ku moc kɛ tuɔɔŋ kɛl ni ciaŋ."
entries.english_sentence: Sparrow said, "Waaaaaaa!!"She continued, "Don't you know that the axe he is using is not real? That axe is made of mud!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Jakɔ̱k ɛ jiök i̱, "Ɣaaaa!"Kä ɛŋu cɛ jɛ jɔp ɔ? Kui̱ci jɛ ɛn ɣöö /ciɛ jio̱p ɛn jio̱p muɔɔn? Mi wëë wä luny jɔk i̱ go̱o̱rɛ tuɔɔŋ, a jɛ jɔp ɛ."
entries.english_sentence: "If he comes back again and demands an egg, tell him to chop down the tree," said Sparrow.Tok agreed and Sparrow left.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔr kä mëë ci Jakɔ̱k loc jɔk, cu Wan ben kä jɛ go̱o̱rɛ tuɔɔŋ.Cuɛ Tok ben jiök ɛ nyɔk, "Jɔapä jiathdä kiɛ bi ɣä ka̱m tuɔɔŋ?"Cu Tok ɛ jiök i̱, "Ɣää! Guak ɛn wa̱lɛ kuɛ jɔp ɛn jiathdu."
entries.english_sentence: Fox returned and asked, "Will you give me an egg, or should I cut down this tree?"Tok replied, "You can cut down the tree!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Wan ɛ thiec i̱, "Tok, ɛ thuɔ̱k inu /ci tuɔɔŋ bi ŋun? Kɛ ɣöö mi wa̱a̱ jiathdä wä jɔp, bä gaatku cam ni kɛn diaal."
entries.english_sentence: Fox said, "Are you sure that you want me to cut down the tree?Because if I do, I'm going to eat all your eggs."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä ŋotdɛ laar Wan ɛ i̱, "Gɔaa ni ɣöö bi ɣä ka̱m tuɔɔŋ kɛl."Cu Tok ɛ lo̱k kä Wan ɛ thiec i̱, "Kä ɛŋa lär jɛ ji̱ɛn cäp ɛ mɔ?"Cu Tok ɛ jiök i̱, "Ɛ Jakɔ̱k."Cuɛ wee, "Bä jek ɛn Jakɔ̱k."
entries.english_sentence: "You had better give me an egg right now!" concluded Fox.Tok refused. She said, "Sparrow told me that your axe is made of mud."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä niɛ cäŋ ɛmɔ cu Wan kɛnɛ Jakɔ̱k la ji̱ tɛ̈r ti di̱t!
entries.english_sentence: From that day, Sparrow and Fox became the greatest of enemies!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan, tëëkɛ wutni da̱ŋ dhieec ti dɔ̱a̱a̱r ti cieŋ gua̱a̱th kɛl kä nyuak kɛn nyinkiɛn diaal kɛɛl.Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, cukɛ thil mi cam kɛnɛ kä thiɛlɛ kɛ yio̱w. Cukɛ rɔ ciöl duɔl kä cu wut kɛl kɛ thiec i̱, "Kɔn banɛ mi̱eth jek nikä?"
entries.english_sentence: Once upon a time, there were five foolish men living together. They shared everything.One day, they ran out of food. They called a meeting. "Where will our next meal come from?" one of them asked.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ buɔ̱m ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ ɣöö thiɛlɛ kɛ mäthni ti dëë kɛ luäk kiɛ ti dëë kɛ moc kɛ mi cam kɛnɛ.Mëë cikɛ ca̱r ɛ määth, cu ram kɛl kä kɛ wee, "Canɛ jiɛɛn!" Cu ram min rɛwdɛ wee, "Wä kɔn nikä?"
entries.english_sentence: There was no easy answer to this question because they had no money and no friends in the community.After thinking for a few seconds, one of them said "Let's get going!" The second person asked, "Where?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu ram min diɔ̱ɔ̱kdiɛn wee i̱, "Wä kɔn kual." Cu ram min ŋuaandiɛn wee i̱, "Kä ca kɔn bi käp?"Cu dhieecdiɛn wee i̱, "/Cuarɛ diɛɛr. Thiɛlɛ riɛk!"Cu wutni da̱ŋ dhieec jiɛɛn wäkɛ kual kä thuk.
entries.english_sentence: The third person said, "To steal food." The fourth one said, "Won't we get caught?" The fifth person said, "Don't worry about that!"The five men went to the market to steal something to eat.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë cikɛ kuël tok, cua kɛ käp kä cua kɛ naŋ gua̱a̱th luɔ̱k kɛ ɣöö ba gua̱n dui̱rä wä ŋa̱c.
entries.english_sentence: As soon as they started stealing, they were caught!The five men were taken to the police station.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Guäth luɔ̱k, cua kɛ thiec i̱, "Ɛŋa took jɛ mɔ i̱ bi yɛn wä kual?"Cukɛ ruac kɛ mua̱thmua̱th kamnikiɛn kärɔ kä cua kuäär luɔ̱k la̱r ta̱a̱ ëë tuɔɔk kɛ ɣöö bikɛ kual.
entries.english_sentence: During the investigation, the police asked, "Whose idea was it to steal food?"The men started whispering among themselves. Then they told the police how it happened.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu ram min nhiam ɛ loc i̱, "Ɣän cä wee i̱, 'Canɛ jiɛɛn.' /Ka̱ n gua̱a̱th in wä nɛy thi̱n lar."Cu ram min rɛwdɛ wee i̱, "Ɣän thiëëcä ni gua̱a̱th in wä nɛy thi̱n." Cu diɔ̱ɔ̱kdiɛn ɛ lar i̱, "Ɣän nyuɔthä ni gua̱a̱th ëë ci nɛy ɛ mat."
entries.english_sentence: The first person said, "I only suggested leaving, not stealing." The second person said, "I was curious about where we were going."The third person said, "We all agreed to look for food."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu ŋuaandiɛn wee i̱, "Ɣän cä thiec i̱ /ca kɔn bi käp!"Cu dhieecdiɛn wee i̱, "Ɣän laarä ni ɣöö thiɛlɛ riɛk kɛ ɣöö ɛ jɛn min la nɛy a lät ni wän."
entries.english_sentence: The fourth person said, "I warned all of us that we're going to be caught."And the fifth person said, "We all know we are thieves, and that's why I said, 'Don't worry about it'."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci kuäär rieetkiɛn liŋ, cuɛ jɛ ŋa̱c ɛn ɣöö wutni ti̱ti̱ kɛ kuëël.Cu kuäär kɛ jiök i̱, "Gɔaa ɣöö nyuak yɛn ŋɔak kamnikun, duŋdɛ ɣöö /cɛ gɔaa ɛn ɣöö dee yɛn ca̱r mi jiääk mat!"
entries.english_sentence: After hearing this, the police understood that all five men were involved in theft.The police officer concluded, "It is a good idea to share everything, except bad ideas!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Duties of a girl in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: Tëëkɛ ciek Nuäärä mi tekɛ nyier da̱ŋ ŋuaan. Kɛn tekɛ duelgɔ̱rä kä ka̱th in rɛwdɛ kɛnɛ yuni̱bäthɛti̱.Jɛn liakɛ rɔ kɛ kui̱c lätnikiɛn. Jɛn la ti̱mɛ nyieekɛ ciɛŋ ëë ci piith kɛ jɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Mrs Deng has four daughters. They are at high school and university.She is very proud of her daughters. She likes to tell them about her life growing up as a girl.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Duties of a girl in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: Man nyieet cuɛ jɛ la̱r kɛ, "Rɛy ciɛŋnikɔn, mi ci nyal cop kä run wäl, la tekɛ lät ti bɛ la lätdɛ, ce̱tkɛ min te guär, tha̱t, kuëny tɔɔŋni kiɛ kuɛɛr kɛnɛ ŋa̱c ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k."
entries.english_sentence: "In traditional Nuer culture, when a girl reaches the age of ten, she is usually given household chores. The chores include grinding, cooking, collecting firewood, and even milking cows," says Mrs Deng.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Duties of a girl in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: "Ti̱ti̱ kɛ lät ti la ŋäc nyal kɛ ɛn ɣöö bɛ kɛ dhil luäŋ kɛ lätni mi ci ɣɔw baak kɛ runwaŋ amäni mi ci ɣɔw a thiaŋ. Man nyaal la läätdɛ ɛ bum kɛ ɣöö bi nyaadɛ ŋɔak ŋa̱c ɛ puc."
entries.english_sentence: "These are the chores that a girl knows she should do from morning to evening. The mother of a girl must make sure that her daughter knows this work."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Duties of a girl in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: "Ti̱ti̱ kɛ ciɛŋ ti nyooth kɛ ɣöö i̱ te nyal kɛ luth, kɛ luäŋ lätdä, kä ca ŋi̱eec ɛ man kɛ gua̱a̱thdɛ pa̱ny, ɛ mi wä cop dhɔrɛ, bɛ guiir kuakni luäŋ ce̱tkɛ min görkɛ."
entries.english_sentence: "These practices show that a girl is respectful, able to work, and has been taught well by her mother. A married woman must be able to manage her household."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Duties of a girl in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: "Kä mi kui̱c nyal kɛ kɛn lät ti̱ti̱, la bumɛ ɛ tet ɛn ɣöö ba kuɛn, kɛ ɣöö car kɛ jɛ i̱ /cɛ rɔɔdɛ bi wä luäŋ rɛy dhɔaarɛ."
entries.english_sentence: "If a girl does not know how to do these chores, it is hard for her to get married because she would not be able to manage her household."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Duties of a girl in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: "Ti̱ti̱ kɛ kɛn lät nyaal ro̱o̱l Nuäärä," cu ciek indaan ɛ la̱r nyieekɛ."Kɛ ɣöö cä yɛ ŋi̱eec kɛ thuɔ̱k, ɛn täämɛ cia ro̱ŋ kɛ kuën."
entries.english_sentence: "These are the duties of a girl in traditional Nuer culture," says Mrs Deng to her daughters."I have taught you well, you are ready for marriage."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Duties of a girl in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: "Duŋdɛ ɣöö bä ruac ɛmɛ gok inɛ. Kɛ nhiam, bi raan duelgɔ̱rä kɔn thuk ba kulɛ kuɛn. Nɛmɛ ɛ jɛn com in ka̱mä yɛ, kä bia jɛ dhil la̱th lät kɛ ɣöö bia kulɛ gɔw."
entries.english_sentence: Mrs Deng concludes, "But first, you will complete your education, my daughters. That is my duty to you and your duty to yourselves."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: Duties of a girl in Nuer culture
entries.nuer_sentence: "Bia cɔw ti luɔ̱th kɛ rɔ, kä luäŋ kɛ la̱t, kä ca ŋi̱eec ɛ gɔaa ɛ cieŋmanikiɛn jek," cu mandi̱t ɛ la̱r kɛ inɔ, kä dothɛduɔɔth."Ɛ jɛn Mama, cakɔ jɛ liŋ," cu nyieekɛ jɛ loc ɛ wäkɛ kɛ mi buɔmkɛ mandiɛn.
entries.english_sentence: "And find husbands who are respectful, able to work, and have been taught well by their parents," adds Mrs Deng with a smile."Yes, mom, we know!" say her daughters as they hug their mother.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ gua̱a̱th mi ci wä, Ro̱l Nhial kɛnɛ Wi̱i̱ Muɔ̱ɔ̱n te kɛn kɛ dääk, /cikɛ te kɛɛl.Ro̱l Nhial tëë nhial kä Wi̱i̱ Muɔ̱ɔ̱n tëë piny. Ro̱l Nhial ɣɔ̱ cɛ duŋdɛ ɣöö Wi̱i̱ Muɔ̱ɔ̱n köötdɛ. Köötdɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛ cuɛ bɛc ɛn ɣöö dee gaat wutdä da̱ŋ diɔ̱k ɛ ti cieŋ thi̱n.
entries.english_sentence: Long ago, Heaven and Earth were separated. Heaven was up and Earth was down.Heaven was wet and Earth was dry. The Earth was so dry that it was very hard for anything to survive. Three brothers were living there.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn gaat wutdä da̱ŋ diɔ̱k ɛ ti, Mɛŋga ɛ gat in di̱i̱t, Lemun ɛ gat in da̱a̱r, Puɔw-puɔw a gat in kui̱ ni jɛn.Ro̱l Nhial cieŋ ji̱ ciëŋ ti kɔŋ thi̱n bä. Nɛmɛ ɛ Cäŋ in la gua̱n gan kɛnɛ man gan ni Pay kɛ gaatkiɛn ni Kuɛli kɛnɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial.
entries.english_sentence: Mango was the oldest brother, Lemon the middle brother, and Papaya the little brother.Up in the sky lived another family, Sun the father, Moon the mother, and their children Star and Heavenly Cloud.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu gaat wutdä tin kɔn duɔl kɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p in dëë jek ni pi̱. Cu Puɔw-puɔw wee i̱, "Canɛ math ni pi̱ tin te yier."Cu Lemun ɛ gak, "Ëy! /Ci kɔn diaal ɛ dee luäŋ kɛ ɣöö thil kɔn diaal miy ti ba̱rba̱a̱r ti cop kɛ yier."
entries.english_sentence: The three brothers had a meeting about how to get water. Papaya said, "Let us drink water from the river."Lemon rejected that, "No! We can't all use the water from the river. Not all of us have long roots that can reach it."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Mɛŋga wee i̱, "Ɛ ram kɛl kä kɔn lär nyam in cɔalkɛ i̱ Pua̱a̱r Nhial kuën, jɛn ɛ nya mi tekɛ maan kä la thätdɛ kɛ pi̱ ti cuɔmcuɔ̱ɔ̱m."Mi ci ram kɛl ɛ kuɛn derɛ kɔn la thälɛ pi̱ kɛ gua̱a̱th in lot rɔ."
entries.english_sentence: Mango said, "One of us should propose to Heavenly Cloud. She is beautiful and she can cook water."He continued, "If one of us marries her, she will cook water for all of us."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn guäth ɛmɔ cu gaat wutdä da̱ŋ diɔ̱k ɛ matpiny ɛn ɣöö bikɛ kuën la̱r Pua̱a̱r Nhial.Cu Puɔw-puɔw wee i̱, "Ca̱r in ci Mɛŋga ɛ ŋun ɛ ca̱r mi gɔaa. Ɛn täämɛ, kɛ ɣöö ɛ jɛn ji̱n gat in di̱i̱t, ɛ jɛn ji̱n ram in ro̱ŋ kɛ ɣöö bi kuɛɛn."
entries.english_sentence: The three brothers agreed that one of them should propose to Heavenly Cloud.Papaya said to Mango, "Your idea is great! Since you are the eldest son, you are the right one to marry her."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Duŋdɛ ɣöö cu Mɛŋga thiec i̱, "Kä ɛŋu mi banɛ wä ka̱m cieŋ mani puɔ̱rkä ɛla ɣɔ̱k kuën?"Cu Puɔw-puɔw wee i̱, "Kɔn banɛ tuɔ̱ŋ kɔn tin ci dɔŋ kä ci pɛ̈ɛ̈n kuany kä banɛ kɛ waaŋ, banɛ toliɛn thöp ɛla ɣɔ̱k kuën."
entries.english_sentence: Mango asked, "What are we going to pay as a dowry to the family of Heavenly Cloud?"Papaya replied, "We will gather our old and fallen branches and burn them. We will pay their smoke as a dowry."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔrɛ cukɛ wä cuɔ̱ŋ wi̱c pa̱a̱m mi bäär kɛ ɣöö ba Pua̱a̱r Nhial wä la̱r kuën.Cu Jiath Lemun ruac tok wee i̱, "Kɔn cakɔ ben kɛ ɣöö bakɔ Pua̱a̱r Nhial ben la̱r kuën, go̱r nɛy ɣöö bi Ro̱l Nhial kɛnɛ Piny maar."
entries.english_sentence: The brothers went and stood on a high mountain to propose to Heavenly Cloud.Lemon started to talk and said, "We have come to make a  proposal to Heavenly Cloud. We want Heaven and Earth to have a relationship."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ cu Cäŋ in la gua̱n gan jiɛn thiec i̱, "Kä mɔ cia ku ben ɔ, ɛŋu bia yuɔr piny kɛ kui̱c kuën?" Cu Jiath Puɔw-puɔw ɛ loc i̱, "Ɣɔ̱k kuën bikɛ la tuɔl."
entries.english_sentence: Father Sun asked the trees, "Now that you have come, what will you pay as a dowry?""We will pay you our smoke as a dowry," replied Papaya.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Ro̱l Nhial kuën nhɔk, kä cu Pua̱a̱r Nhial ɛ nhɔk bä ɛn ɣöö ba kuɛn ɛ Jiath Mɛŋga duŋdɛ ɣöö cuɛ jɛ la̱th piny ɛn ɣöö bɛ la thätdɛ kɛ nhiaal kɛ gua̱th da̱ŋ rɛw kärɔ̱ min la Ruel kɛnɛ Tɔ̱t.
entries.english_sentence: Heavenly Cloud said she accepted the proposal. Heaven also agreed to the marriage."But I will only cook the rain during two seasons in the year, summer and autumn," said Heavenly Cloud.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn gaat wutdä da̱ŋ diɔ̱k tin kɔn cukɛ ɣɔ̱k kuën nööŋ ce̱tkɛ min ci kɛn ɛ yac, kä cukɛ ɣɔ̱k kuën tɔ̱tɔ̱ waŋ wi̱c pa̱a̱m in bäär.Cu tol wä nhiaal kä cu ji̱ Ro̱l Nhial lo̱ckiɛn tɛɛth mëë cikɛ ɣɔ̱k kuën Pua̱a̱rä Nhial nɛn.
entries.english_sentence: The three brothers paid their dowry as promised. They burned their fallen branches on the mountain.The smoke went up and Heaven rejoiced when they received the dowry for Heavenly Cloud.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn guäth ɛmɔ cua kuën rialikä kam Jiath Mɛŋgakä kɛnɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial. Cu nɛy diaal lo̱ckiɛn tɛɛth, Ro̱l Nhial kɛnɛ Piny cukɛ rɔ mat kɛ tɛ̈th lɔaac.Kɛ kui̱c tɛthkä lɔaac cua ma̱a̱r liŋ gua̱thni diaal, "Bum-bum-bum, bum-bum-bum."
entries.english_sentence: The wedding was arranged between Heavenly Cloud and Mango. Everyone was happy, Heaven and Earth were united with joy.Because of the joy, thunder was heard everywhere. "Bum-bum-bum, bum-bum-bum!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Kuën Jiaath Mɛŋga kɛ Pua̱a̱r Nhial
entries.book_title_english: Wedding between Mango and Heavenly Cloud
entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ cu Pua̱a̱r Nhial nhiaal in nhiam, cu thal kä cu Piny ɣɔ̱c cu tok.Ɛ tookɛ niɛ guäth ɛmɔ ɛ wä nhiam cu Pua̱a̱r Nhial ya̱cdɛ cu rɔam thi̱n ɛn ɣöö bɛ nhiaal a thaalɛ kɛ gua̱a̱th da̱ŋ rɛw, ɛla Ruel kɛnɛ Tɔ̱t.
entries.english_sentence: The first rain was cooked by Heavenly Cloud and Earth began to be wet.From then until now, Heavenly Cloud kept her vow to cook only during two seasons, summer and autumn.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nɛy ti ŋuan rɛy wec ɛmɛ la cieŋkɛ canä mëëdan.
entries.english_sentence: Many people in this village were living in poverty.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kuääriɛn ni Koang cuɛ kɛ com i̱, "Görɛ ria̱ŋ piny muɔ̱ɔ̱n." Duŋdɛ ɣöö /kenɛ cop lɔcdiɛn, kä /ka̱n rie̱e̱tkɛ käp.
entries.english_sentence: Chief Kyemba, their leader, advised them, "Look for the wealth in the soil."But they did not understand and did not pay attention to his words.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ tekɛ dhɔl mi duŋ tiit mi cɔalkɛ i̱ Ko̱r mi cieŋ rɛy wec ɛmɛ. Ko̱r la kääpɛ diit ti ŋuan. Jɛn la camɛ dit ni kɛɛliwdɛ. Jɛn räthɛ ni mi̱th cueny kɛnɛ ci̱i̱nkɛ.
entries.english_sentence: A small boy called Mutaka lived in this village.Mutaka caught a lot of birds. He used to eat the whole bird. He even ate the liver and intestines.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cäŋ kɛl Ko̱r cuɛ guk käp wi̱i̱ jiaath. Mëë ci guk ɛ nɛn ca käp, cuɛ wak kɛ jɔw, "Mäthdä, pälni ɣä i̱kä, ɣän tee kɛ mi ro̱ŋ kɛ ɣöö dee ŋa̱c mi bä la̱r ji."
entries.english_sentence: One day Mutaka caught a dove in a tree.When the dove saw that Mutaka had him, it cried out, "My friend, leave me and I tell you what you need to know."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ko̱r cuɛ wee, "Lärni jɛ ɣä. Kɛ kɔrɛ bä ji̱ ku cam!"
entries.english_sentence: Mutaka said, "Tell me. Then I will eat you!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu guk ruac kä biɛlɛ min lɔw wäkɛ mi luɔɔcɛ rɔ kɛ mi yiel-luaal. "Jak ni ɣä kä wä wi̱i̱ jiaath ɛ mi, kɛ kɔrɛ bä ji̱ la̱t ti ŋuan."
entries.english_sentence: The dove spoke while changing its colour from grey to purple."Let me go to that tree over there, and then I will tell you more."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Ko̱r guk päl kä barɛ rɔ wi̱i̱ jiaath. Mëë cɛ cop ɛn wi̱ni, cuɛ dɔl ni Ko̱r. Cu guk ciöt, "Ria̱ŋ tëë rɛydäää!"
entries.english_sentence: Mutaka let the dove go and it flew to the tree.When it reached there, it laughed at Mutaka. "Wealth is in meee!" called the dove.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ko̱r cuɛ thiec, "Ɛŋu mi latdi?" Cu guk ɛ loc i̱, "Rɛydä ɛ da̱a̱p." "Jin ci dɔ̱r ɛn ɣöö ci ɣä pa̱l wä. Ci ria̱ŋ mi di̱i̱t pa̱l wä." Cu guk ca̱r Köör ya̱r.
entries.english_sentence: Mutaka asked, "What are you saying?""Inside me is gold!" replied the bird. "You were stupid to release me. You have missed a lot of wealth," the dove tormented Mutaka.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu dit ŋɔaani ti ce̱tkɛ da̱a̱pni yuɔr piny. Cuɛ räth wi̱i̱ jiaath mi bäär. Cu Ko̱r cu coth ni piny ge̱kä jiaath in dan.
entries.english_sentence: Then the bird passed out droppings that looked like gold. It flew to a taller tree.Mutaka started to scratch the ground around the tree.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ ji̱ wec cɔl, "Bia kɛ ɣä kɛɛl, kɔndiaal banɛ ria̱ŋ wä wät piny."
entries.english_sentence: He called out to the villagers, "Come with me, we can all scratch for wealth in the ground."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu määni walɛ, Ko̱r kɛnɛ ji wecdiɛn ŋotkɛ wa̱tkɛ piny kɛ gör da̱a̱pä.
entries.english_sentence: To this day, Mutaka and the villagers are scratching the ground looking for gold.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä Guk rɔmɛ ni kiet thi̱n wi̱i̱ jiaath i̱, "Ria̱ŋ tëë rɛydäää!"
entries.english_sentence: The dove continues to sing in the tree that, "Wealth is in meee!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu gua̱n gatdä tɛth piny kɛnɛ gatdɛ kɛ muuliɛn wä kɛn ja̱l gua̱a̱th mi na̱n.Mëë te kɛn dup, cu tha̱a̱ŋ nath kɛ thiec kɛ mɔ /ci kɛn ko̱t jɔk muɔ̱l kɛ jɛ mɔ.
entries.english_sentence: A father, his son and their donkey started a long journey.On the way, some people asked them why they didn't ride the donkey.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu gua̱n gatdä gatdɛ jiök i̱ ko̱tni jɔk muɔ̱l bä ja̱l kɛ piny.Cu kɛn wä kɛ wä nhiam inɔ kɛ gua̱a̱th mi tɔt.
entries.english_sentence: The father invited his son to ride the donkey while he walked.They continued like this for a while.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu nɛy tin kɔ̱ŋ tëë ci röm kɛ kɛ ruac wäkɛ i̱, "Guic dho̱l ɛ jiääk ɛmɛ ko̱tdɛ jɔk muɔ̱l ku gua̱n lɛ ja̱l kɛ ciök."
entries.english_sentence: Then, other people they met remarked, "Look at this rude boy riding a donkey while his father is walking!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ ɣöö inɔ, cu gat käny piny kä cu gua̱n kɔt jɔk muɔ̱l.Cu kɛn wä kɛ wä nhiam kɛ ja̱l.
entries.english_sentence: As a result, the son jumped down and his father rode the donkey.They continued their journey.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔr gua̱th, cu nɛy ti kɔ̱ŋ wee, "Nɛ̈nɛ wut ɛ jiääk ɛmɔ cɛ kɔt jɔk muɔ̱l ku gatdɛ lɛ ja̱l kɛ ciök."
entries.english_sentence: After some time, other people said, "Look at this rude father riding a donkey while his son is walking!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu gua̱n gatdä kɛnɛ gat ɛ car i̱ bi kɛn da̱ŋ rɛw kɔt jɔk muɔ̱l kɛɛl.
entries.english_sentence: So the father and son decided to ride the donkey together.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔr gua̱th mi tɔt, cu tha̱a̱ŋ nath wee i̱, "Nɛ̈nɛ nɛy ti kue̱c kɛ ca̱r ti! Bi kɛn muul näk."
entries.english_sentence: But a few minutes later, some people remarked, "Look at these rude people! There are going to kill the donkey.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ jɔak, cu gua̱n gatdä kɛnɛ gat ɛ ŋa̱c thiɛlɛ gua̱a̱th mi bi kɛn ca̱r nath la̱ny thi̱n.Cu kɛnɛ mat i̱ bi kɛn la̱t ni min guic kɛnɛ i̱ lot rɔ.
entries.english_sentence: Finally, father and son understood that they could not escape from people's remarks.They decided to use their own minds to do the right thing.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Run ti ŋuan tëë ci wä, ya̱a̱k ci buɔth kɛ näk. Kɛ ɣöö tëë piny kɛ rɛɛth, cu mäni böwni, kɛnɛ rɔɔm kä cua ɣɔ̱k ɣöth gua̱thni kɔ̱kiɛn. Ya̱a̱k cukɛ duɔth ni baaŋ ɛ thiɛlɛ mi camkɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Many years ago, hyenas were starving. Because of a famine, even goats, sheep and cows migrated to other places.Hyenas had nothing to eat. They gathered in one place to discuss the issue.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Yak kɛl rɛydiɛn cuɛ wee i̱, "Rɛy ciɛŋädan, kɔn la cam kɔnɛ ɛni mi ri̱ŋ. Nɛnɛ jɛ, kɛn pua̱a̱r tɔ̱tɔ̱ riŋkɛ."
entries.english_sentence: One of the hyenas said, "In our culture, we eat anything that is fleeing. Look, these clouds are fleeing."This hyena believed that the clouds were migrating to another place. He said, "Let's eat them."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ pɛ̈th ɛlɔ̱ŋ, kɛn ya̱a̱k diaal cua guic ni nhial kä cuɛ pua̱a̱r nɛn jälkɛ nhial.
entries.english_sentence: Immediately, all the hyenas looked up and saw the clouds moving in the sky.One of the youngest hyenas asked, "How do we reach the clouds? They are very far away from the ground."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn yak in di̱i̱tdiɛn cuɛ wee, "Ɛ yak in bum ni jɛn cuŋ piny kä bi ramɔ kɔt jɔɔk raamɔ kamnikɔn kɛ̈l kɛ̈ɛ̈li. Kɔn banɛ kɔt amäni ni ɣöö kɔn canɛ cop ni rɛy pua̱a̱ri."
entries.english_sentence: The oldest hyena said, "Let the strongest hyena stand on the ground and then let the rest of us stand on each other's backs. We will climb on one another's backs until we reach the clouds."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn cua mat piny kä cuɛ köt tok jio̱knikiɛn kɛ̈l kɛ̈ɛ̈l.
entries.english_sentence: They agreed and started climbing up on one another's backs.Soon, there were no more hyenas left remaining on the ground except the strongest one.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔrɛ mëë ci yak in jɔakdiɛn kɔt, ɛn yak in te piny cuɛ car ni ɣöö ya̱a̱k tin kɔ̱kiɛn cikɛ mi̱eth ku thuŋ tok.
entries.english_sentence: After the last hyena climbed up, the hyena on the ground thought that the others had started eating.He asked, "Why don't you give me some of the food you're eating?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cieŋni mëë, kɛn ya̱a̱k /kenkɛ cop rɛy pua̱a̱ri.
entries.english_sentence: However, the hyenas did not reach the clouds.They didn't find any food and so they had nothing to give to the strongest hyena standing on the ground.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn yak in bum ni jɛn cuɛ cio̱kdɛ luaŋ kä cuɛ rɔ riet kui̱c caam. Duɔthkiɛn tin kɔ̱ŋ cukɛ pɛn piny kɛ kui̱c cuëëc ni kɛndiaal.
entries.english_sentence: The strongest hyena became impatient and moved to the left side. All the others came falling down to the right side.As a result, even today all hyenas limp on their right side.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan rɛy kakä mi tɔt mi thieek kɛ wec.
entries.english_sentence: Once upon a time, there was a little farm near a little village.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Tëë kɛ dɔw manpalɛ̈k mi cɔal i̱ Nyabo̱o̱rä mi cieŋ thi̱n.
entries.english_sentence: There lived a little chicken called Daisy.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ wee i̱, "Mi wa̱a̱ wä di̱t, bä la pa̱a̱rä rɛy pua̱a̱ri kɛ gɔ̱kä."
entries.english_sentence: "When I grow up, I want to fly high, high into the sky," Daisy said.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä manpalɛ̈kni tin kɔ̱ŋ /ci kɛn ɛ ŋäth ɛn ɣöö i̱ derɛ la thuɔ̱k. La dɔal kɛ jɛ ɛ kɛn.
entries.english_sentence: But all the other chickens laughed at her.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kɛnɛ jiök i̱, "Ɛ ji̱n gua̱n kacä mi jiääk, /cakɔ rɔ bi nyɔk kɛ ŋar kɛ ji kɛɛl."
entries.english_sentence: "You are so weird," they said. "We won't play with you anymore."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu man ɛ jiök i̱, "Dee kɔn gɔ̱k kɔn diaal ɣär kä dee kɔn kɛ tɛ̈ŋ ɛ pätpät duŋdɛ ɣöö bumɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛn ɣöö dee manpalɛ̈k päär kɛ gɔ̱kɛ ce̱tkɛ diit tin kɔ̱ŋ."
entries.english_sentence: "Daisy, we can all flap our wings but it's very difficult for chickens to fly," Mama told her.Daisy wouldn't give up.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä /kenɛ ŋɔa̱ŋ, la ŋi̱i̱cɛ rɔ kɛ ɣöö derɛ päär.La ɣɔ̱nɛ jɛ ni ciaŋ i̱ derɛ päär kɛ gɔ̱kɛ ɛ pätpät duŋdɛ ɣöö /kenɛ rɔ me̱t luäŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Every day she practiced by herself, flapping her wings.Flap, flap, flap, she would flap her wings but she couldn't lift off the ground. She imagined herself flying high into the sky.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä min tëë ŋi̱i̱cä, cuɛ ca̱a̱r i̱ derɛ cu pär nhial a derɛ manpalɛ̈kni tin kɔ̱ŋ la guicɛ piny.Cuɛ wee i̱ a dëë kɛ leny amäni kɛy kɛnɛ jiëyni, ɛ dee kɛ la wee, "Ɛ manpalɛ̈k mi te di ɛn nɛ päär kɛ gɔ̱kɛ mɛ!"
entries.english_sentence: She imagined herself flying high and looking at the chickens below.She imagined flying past the sparrows and the swallows. "Wow! A chicken that can fly!" The birds would say.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛ pätpät ni ciaŋ, ɣɔ̱nɛ jɛ i̱ derɛ päär kɛ gɔ̱kɛ.
entries.english_sentence: So Flap, flap, flap, every day Daisy would flap her wings.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: La kacɛ rɔ i̱ riŋɛ nhial kä la wä luny ni jɛn piny ɛ nyɔk.
entries.english_sentence: She would lift off the ground but fall down again.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu lɔcdɛ jiek kä cuɛ wie. Cuɛ man jiök i̱, "Nɛy tin la wee i̱ /cä bi me̱t päär tekɛ kɛ cuɔ̱ŋ, ɣän /cä bi me̱t päär ɛpuc."
entries.english_sentence: "I'm never going to fly!" Daisy cried to Mama. "The others are right."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu man ɛ jiök i̱, "Cɛ ramɔ cak kɛ cäkdɛ, tha̱a̱ŋ manpalɛ̈kni /ci kɛn ɛ go̱r ɛn ɣöö dee kɛ päär ce̱tkɛ ji̱. Ɣɔ̱n ni duŋdu."
entries.english_sentence: "Daisy, you are different from the other chickens. They don't want to fly but you do! You can do it," Mama said.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ruɔ̱n cuɛ kɔt wi̱i̱ duëël manpalɛ̈kni kä cuɛ gɔ̱kɛ tɛ̈ŋ ɛ pätpät.Cuɛ pär rɛy jiɔam kä cuɛ gɔ̱kɛ ɣa̱a̱r kä cuɛ kɛ tɛ̈ŋ ɛ pätpät…
entries.english_sentence: The following day Daisy climbed to the top of the chicken coop and flap, flap, flap, she flapped her wings.She flew into the air and flapped her wings and flapped her wings and ...
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "Ayiööööw……!"
entries.english_sentence: BAM!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu manpalɛ̈kni tin kɔ̱ŋ rɛ̈ɛ̈t kɛ to̱k ɛlɔ̱ŋ.Cu kɛ wee min läär nɛy ɛ ji̱! Thilɛ manpalɛ̈k mi dee päär ɛ bɛ wä nhial.
entries.english_sentence: The other chickens laughed out loud."Ha ha ha! We told you! Chickens can't fly!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä mëë ruɔ̱ndɛ, cu Nyabo̱o̱rä cak päär ni jɛn ɛlɔ̱ŋ. Cuɛ wä ni wi̱i̱ luaak.Ɛ pätpät i̱ nɛ cuɛ päär kɛ gɔ̱kɛ.
entries.english_sentence: But the next day Daisy climbed even higher, right up to the top of the hut.Flap, flap, flap, Daisy flapped her wings.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ päär rɛy jiɔam, kä cuɛ gɔ̱kɛ tɛ̈ŋ ɛ pätpät.
entries.english_sentence: She flew into the air and flapped her wings and flapped her wings and flapped her wings and...
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ ŋot kɛ mi la ɣɔ̱nɛ jɛ i̱ bɛ pär ni nhial. Kä cu jiɔm gɔ̱knikɛ rɔ rep ɛlɔ̱ŋ.Kä cuɛ jor ni nhial ɛpuc. Cu kɛy kɛnɛ jiëyni wee i̱, "Ɣa̱y, ɛ manpalɛ̈k mi päär nhial kɛ gɔ̱kɛ!"
entries.english_sentence: She kept flying! The wind beneath her wings grew stronger and she flew higher and higher!The sparrows and the swallows said, "Amazing! A flying chicken!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu manpalɛ̈kni tin kɔn go̱o̱r ni ɣöö dee kɛ päär ce̱tni kɛ jɛ bä.
entries.english_sentence: And the other chickens wanted to be just like her.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kɛ wee i̱, "Ɛ ji̱n rami gäy naath, lö Nyabo̱o̱rä!"
entries.english_sentence: They said, "Oh Daisy, you're amazing!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ gua̱a̱th ëëdan, tëë nyier da̱ŋ rɛw ti cieŋ Nyabuɔ̱ny kɛnɛ Nyabuay. Ci ciëŋmanikiɛn li̱w. Cieŋkɛ dhɔr mi thiɛl nhiaal kä thiɛl bɛl. Mi ci kɛn wä go̱r kɛn kuän la ramɔ wä ni gua̱a̱th mi na̱n bɛ kulɛ wä jek.
entries.english_sentence: Once upon a time, there lived two sisters, Nelima and Nambuya. Their parents were dead.They lived on bare land. There was neither rain nor crops. Whoever wanted food had to go a long distance to find it.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuɔ̱ny ɛ nyam mi muɔ̱l, bitdɛ kä luääk. Nyiman ni Nyabuay ɛ gua̱n liakä /cɛ com ɛn la̱rkɛ jɛ liŋ. Kä /cɛ diɛɛr kɛ tha̱a̱ŋ nath.
entries.english_sentence: Nelima was a humble, quiet and helpful girl.Her sister Nambuya was proud and did not listen to advice. She did not care about other people.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, cu nyier tin guɔ̱ɔ̱r da̱ŋ rɛw thiɛl mi cam kɛnɛ. Bikɛ dhil gör kɛ kuän. Inɔ Nyabuɔ̱ny kɛnɛ Nyabuay cukɛ däk piny wä kɛn gööli.
entries.english_sentence: One day, the two sisters had nothing to eat. They would have to look for food.So Nelima and Nambuya went off in different directions.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn gua̱thɔ, tëë kɛ ciek mi di̱i̱t mi cɔali Nyagɔa. Ŋa̱th kɛ jɛ i̱ dera muuc riäŋä. Nyagɔa tëë kɛ dhɔp kä ci puɔ̱nydɛ thia̱a̱ŋ kɛ buɔ̱ɔ̱t.
entries.english_sentence: Meanwhile, there lived an old woman called Netasile. She was believed to be a giver of riches.Netasile had leprosy and her body was full of sores.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyabuay rët kɛ gëk Nyagɔa. Cu Nyagɔa Nyabuay cɔl, "Nyadä mal puɔ̱nydu? Bi ni gua̱a̱th indiɛn? Kä wi̱i̱ nikä?"
entries.english_sentence: Nambuya came across Netasile.Netasile said to Nambuya, "My daughter, how are you? Where do you come from? Where are you going?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuay cuɛ thiecni diaal tin kɔn luɔc. Inɔ cu Nyagɔa ɛ jiök, "Bër luäk ɣä kɛ wädä dhɔɔrä bä ji̱ wä la̱r min bi wä la̱t."
entries.english_sentence: Nambuya answered all the questions.Then Netasile said, "Come help me to go to my house and I will tell you what to do."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuay cuɛ gaak kɛ ciek. Cuɛ wee i̱ "Thia̱k ni ɣöö dëë li̱w kä ɣöö dëë buɔ̱ɔ̱tku wä thiap." Cu Nyagɔa biɛt cuɛ gue̱c ni Nyabuay ja̱l malä.
entries.english_sentence: Nambuya was rude to Netasile. She said, "I would rather die than touch those sores of yours."Netasile kept quiet and wished Nambuya a safe journey.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuay cuɛ ja̱l kɛ gua̱a̱th mi bäär.  Cuɛ cop gua̱a̱th mi tekɛ thɔ̱ɔ̱l, kɔ̱lkɔ̱li, makuac thɔ̱a̱l kɛnɛ muɔɔl piɛny ti kɔ̱ŋ. Ci puɔ̱nydɛ cuuc kä ci buɔth ɛ näk. Mëë cɛ nyuur lɔ̱ŋɛ, cuɛ niɛɛn. Cu muɔɔl piɛny ɛ tuok ka̱ckɛ jɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Nambuya walked for a long time. She reached a place where there were snakes, millipedes, caterpillars and other insects.She was very tired and weak from hunger. She sat down to rest and fell asleep. The insects began to bite her.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rɛy ja̱lɛ, Nyabuɔ̱ny cuɛ ben kä jɛn ciek ɛn di̱i̱t. Cu lɔcdɛ tɛɛth kɛ ɣöö cɛ Nyagɔa nɛn, ɛŋadiɛn ram ɛn nhiam ëë kɔn kɛ jek kɛ tuk ja̱lɛ. Nyagɔa cɛ thiec jɛn ëë cɛ thiecni Nyabuay.
entries.english_sentence: On her journey, Nelima came across Netasile. She was happy to see her because she was the first person she met since starting her journey.Netasile asked the same questions as she asked Nambuya.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuɔ̱ny cɛ nhɔk bɛ Nyagɔa luäk. "Ci la̱t ɛn ca lo̱k ɛ nɛy tin kɔ̱ŋ la̱t," laarɛ ciek ɛn di̱i̱t. Cuɛ Nyabuɔ̱ny jiök locni cieŋ. Thɔ̱ŋɔ bi tin diaal tin go̱o̱ri̱ jek.
entries.english_sentence: Nelima agreed to help Netasile. "You have done what others failed to do," said Netasile.She told Nelima to go back home. There she would find everything she wanted.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyabuɔ̱ny ci lɔcdɛ tɛɛth ɛlɔ̱ŋ cuɛ tɛ̈th lɔaacdɛ la̱r ciek ɛn di̱i̱t. Cuɛ riŋ locɛ cieŋ cuɛ duel mi jädi̱t jek kɛ kɔakɛ diaal rɛydɛ, kɛ kuan ti ŋuan. Cuɛ ria̱ŋ. Duŋ ni ɣöö Nyabuɔ̱ny paarɛ nyiman ɛn ci yiëëdɛ jiɛɛn, Nyabuay.
entries.english_sentence: Nelima was very grateful and thanked Netasile.She ran back home and found a new house with everything in it, and a lot of food. She was now rich.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cɛ la̱r rɔɔdɛ, "Kɛl mi /ken luek liŋ ɛ jɛn ɣöö bɛ wä guut ni thook gua̱r."
entries.english_sentence: But Nelima mourned the loss of her sister, Nambuya.She said to herself, "One who did not listen to advice ended up in an elephant's mouth."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ŋuot Nyaluaak kɛ kuɛ̈, la man a tɔ̱ɔ̱c kɛ bi̱ri̱c mi gɔaa.Ɛn bi̱ri̱c ɛmɔ takɛ waydɛ ɛn Nyaluaak kɛ ga̱a̱p nöör.
entries.english_sentence: When Akai was a little girl, her mother used to put her to sleep on a beautiful mat.Akai's aunt made this special mat from palm leaves.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn bi̱ri̱c ɛmɔ tëëkɛ biɛɛl ti ŋuaan.Tëëkɛ biɛl mi diŋ kɛnɛ biɛl mi tɔ̱c la̱l kɛ biɛl mi tɔ̱c juayni. Jɛn tëëkɛ dääk kɛ bi̱ri̱c tin kɔ̱ŋ tin tekɛ man rɛy duëël ɛ.
entries.english_sentence: The mat had bright pink, blue and green colours.It was different from other mats that Akai's mother had in the hut.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn wec ëë tekɛ thin ɛ wec mi leth ɛlɔ̱ŋ kä tëëkɛ pääm. Kä tëëkɛ jiɛth kɛnɛ thɔ̱ɔ̱l kɛ makaari ti ŋuan.Duŋdɛ ɣöö /cɛ la dualɛ ɛn Nyaluaak kɛ kɛn mɔɔl piɛny diaal ɛ tɔ̱.
entries.english_sentence: The land around Akai's home was very dry, hot and full of stones. There were many scorpions, spiders and snakes too.But Akai was never in danger of being bitten by these dangerous creatures.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu man wee, "Ɛn bi̱ri̱cä mɛmɛ gaŋɛ jɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ mi dee jɛ kac."
entries.english_sentence: Her mother said, "Her special mat protects Akai from any harm."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn Nyaluaak ɛ gat mi pɛlpɛl. Ŋäcɛ jɛ amäni gua̱a̱th puɔ̱ɔ̱l in janyjany min thiäk kɛ dhɔɔriɛn.
entries.english_sentence: Akai was a clever child.She discovered where the nearest shallow well was.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyaluaak ŋäcɛ jɛ amäni dhɔr mandɔŋdɛ bä.Jɛn ni ciaaŋ laa wëë rueeth kɛ cak thɔ̱a̱rɔ̱a̱a̱l kɛɛl kɛ mandɔɔŋdɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Akai also knew where her grandmother's manyatta was located.She often went to drink camel milk with her grandmother.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, ɛ jɛn i̱ wëë mandɔɔŋdɛ gui̱l dhɔɔrɛ, kä cuɛ bath rɛy päämni. Cuɛ dual ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: One day, Akai was not so lucky. She left to go to her grandmother's manyatta, but she got lost in the hills.Akai was afraid.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ nyuur thaar jiaath mi thep kä cuɛ te thi̱n lipɛ rami mi dee jɛ luäk, kɛ pɛ̈th cuɛ niɛɛn kä cuɛ läk läkikä.
entries.english_sentence: She sat under an edome tree and waited for help.Soon she fell asleep and had a dream.
