entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ rɔɔdɛ jek tɔ̱cɛ rɛy bi̱ri̱cä min gɔaa. Cuɛ ciek mi di̱t mi cäätkɛ mandɔɔŋdɛ nɛn guic jɛ piny. Doothɛ duɔɔth kä kämɛ jɛ cak thɔ̱a̱rɔ̱a̱a̱l kɛ liɛɛr. Niɛ gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ cuɛ tetkɛ riny kɛ käpdɛ kɛ cak, kä cuɛ cu ke̱e̱r.
entries.english_sentence: This is what Akai dreamed: She was lying on her special mat. A woman who looked like her grandmother was watching over her. The old woman smiled and gave her a bowl of camel milk. Just when Akai stretched out her hand to take the milk, she woke up.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ wäŋkɛ lɛp ni määth.Mëë cɛ nhial guic, cuɛ dit mi tɔt mi tɔ̱cla̱l nɛn tëë kaarä jiaath nhial.
entries.english_sentence: Akai opened her eyes slowly.When she looked up, she saw a small blue bird on a branch above her.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci Nyaluaak rɔ jiɛc, ɛn dit ɛ tɔt ɛ tɔ̱cla̱l ɛmɔ cuɛ gɔ̱kɛ tɛ̈ŋ kä cuɛ Nyaluaak böth dup.Cu Nyaluaak ɛ guɔ̱ɔ̱r.
entries.english_sentence: When Akai got up, the small blue bird flapped its wings and led the way for Akai.She followed the bird.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyaluaak cuɛ cop gua̱a̱th mi tekɛ dup ti ŋuan ti däk piny gööli, cu dit ɛ tɔ̱cla̱l ɛ tɔt ɛmɔ ko̱l yuɔr piny mi ce̱tkɛ bi̱ri̱c Nyaluaak.
entries.english_sentence: Akai came to a place where the path went in two different directions.The blue bird dropped a piece of a mat that was like Akai's own mat.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë cɛ bi̱ri̱c ɛmɔ kuany piny, Nyaluaak cuɛ ci̱ök ti ce̱tkɛ mi man kɔn ja̱l kɛ jɛ.Kɛ pɛ̈th jɛn cuɛ wa̱l in janyjany nɛn ɛ thia̱kɛ kɛ gua̱a̱th ëë laa kɛn pi̱w ɛ jɔm thi̱n.
entries.english_sentence: Picking up the piece of mat, Akai saw footprints that she knew were her mother's.Soon she saw the shallow well from where they fetched water.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ciëŋmani Nyaluaak cuɔ diit kɛt kä duthkɛ kɛ ɣöö loor kɛnɛ.Kɛn cua ŋuɔ̱t dɛl, cua ri̱ŋ bul kä tɛth lo̱ckiɛn kɛ ɣöö ci nyaadiɛn lunyjɔk kɛ mal.
entries.english_sentence: Akai's family sang and danced to welcome her home.They slaughtered a goat, roasted the meat and celebrated their child's safe return.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyaluaak cuɛ nyuur rɛy bi̱ri̱cä dɛ min gɔaa ɛ camɛ ri̱i̱ŋdɛ min ca buɔ̱lɛ ni kɛ tɛ̈th lɔaac.
entries.english_sentence: Akai sat on her special mat and enjoyed eating a big piece of roast meat.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän /ka̱n wa̱a̱ri met la̱th. Mi nɛ̈ɛ̈nä gaat la̱thkɛ wa̱a̱ri ti gɔw, bä kɛ guic kä.
entries.english_sentence: I had never worn shoes before.When I saw children wearing nice shoes, I would look at them with longing.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Maar cuɛ lar, "Jin bi tekɛ wa̱a̱ri ti ŋuan ni waalɛ lipni kɛ!"Tha̱a̱ŋ gua̱thni /ci ɣän ɛ a ŋääth. "Ni waalɛ ɛ nɛy? Ɣän cua̱ jɛ thiec kɛ cäŋ kɛl."
entries.english_sentence: My mother would say, "You will have many pairs in the future, just wait!"Sometimes I did not believe her. "When is the future?" I asked her one day.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu gua̱th wä ɛ cu thia̱k ni da̱p gatdä Kuɔth. Kä cia raan wä guäth ko̱kä kä lunyɛ jɔk kɛ ki̱i̱th mi te rɛy kɛ ti pay kɔk."Ma! Bi kɔn wä i̱ nɛy kä thuk ko̱kä?" cua̱ maar thiec.
entries.english_sentence: Time passed and it was nearly Christmas. Everybody was busy going to the market and coming back with bags of new things."Mother, are we going to the market?" I asked her.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛ ŋot cäŋ däpä gatdä Kuɔth, cu maar ɣä ker nikɛ runwaŋ ɛlɔ̱ŋ mi /ken met tuɔɔk.Cuɛ ɣä thiec mi dee ki̱th ko̱kä min la naŋɛ gua̱th ko̱kä ni ciaŋ gɔn.
entries.english_sentence: The day before Christmas, my mother woke me up earlier than usual.She asked me to fetch the big shopping basket she always carried to the market.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä guäth ko̱kä mi ɣööŋ, te ni diëëth ti ŋuan kɛnɛ gaatkiɛn thi̱n.Kɛn tekɛ ko̱kä bieyni kɛnɛ kuan.
entries.english_sentence: At the open-air market there, were many parents with their children.They were buying new clothes and stocking up on food.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu nɛy rɛt ni jɛ gua̱a̱th ëë te wa̱a̱ri ti gööl ti ŋuan thi̱n.Wäŋkä cukɛ nha̱a̱ny kɛ nënkä ti biɛlbiɛɛl. La guɛ̈nyä ni wa̱a̱ri ti ca car bërɔ kɛ bërɔ.
entries.english_sentence: We went straight to where there were many different types of shoes.My eyes were wide with amazement. I gaped at row after row of neatly arranged shoes.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔr kä min cä gua̱th wa̱a̱ri ti ŋuan ɣɔ̱a̱n, cuɔ cuɔ̱ŋ kä wa̱a̱ri ti ca̱a̱r ti bär. Kɛ jɛn wäär ɛmɔ, /ka̱n niɛn.Cu lɔcdä tɛɛth caarä ɣöö kɛ wa̱a̱ri ti pay kɔk kä bä rɔ gɔ̱k kɛ rɛy dhɔaar.
entries.english_sentence: After trying on many pairs, I settled for black lace-up shoes. I couldn't sleep that night.I was so excited thinking of how I would wear my new shoes and show off to every child in the village.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔrɛ, ɣän cuɔ rɔ jiɛc wi̱i̱ dhaŋä kä kuëŋä wa̱a̱rikä.Ɣän ja̱lä ni määth rɛy duëël kɛ kɔr kä min cä thuɔk kɛ ja̱l cua̱ wa̱a̱ri luɔc rɛy thundukä.Cuɔ loc tɔɔc, dundɛ ɣöö /ca̱ nin.
entries.english_sentence: After a while, I got out of bed and put on the shoes. I walked gently around the room and then put the shoes back into the box.I lay down again, but I couldn't sleep.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän cua̱ ji̱ɛɛn ni nyɔk kɛ ɣɔ̱n wa̱a̱ri min rɛwdɛ.Cua̱ ka̱a̱th kuëëny wiɛlä rɛy duëël cua̱ wa̱a̱ri luɔc tɔ̱wädiɛn.
entries.english_sentence: I got up and tried on the shoes a second time.I strutted around the room for a while and then put them back.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän cua̱ tɔɔc ɛ nyɔk kä ɣɔ̱a̱nä nien. Duŋdɛ ɣöö ɣän cuɔrɔ nyɔk kɛ jiɛɛn kɛ jiɛɛn in diɔ̱ɔ̱kdiɛn. Cua̱ wa̱a̱ri la̱th kä ka̱yä wiɛlä rɛy duëël.Cua̱rɔ jek ci puɔ̱nydä cuuc. Ɣän cua̱ loc wi̱i̱ dhaŋä ni nyɔk.
entries.english_sentence: I lay down once more and tried to sleep. But I got up a third time. I put on the shoes and jumped around the room.Then I felt tired. I decided to get back into bed.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Bakädɛ, cu maar ɣä ker. Kä cuɛ thiec, "Ɛŋu mi nɛ̈ɛ̈nä mɔ?"
entries.english_sentence: The following morning, I was woken by my mother. "What is this I see?" she asked.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɣän la̱thä wa̱a̱rikä tin pay kɔk ni rɛy dhaŋä.
entries.english_sentence: I was wearing my new shoes in bed!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ni walkä, cɛ kɔn tekɛ nya mi te thi̱n mi cɔal ci̱ötdɛ Nyɛwec. Nyɛwec ɛ nya mi wi̱c ruac ɛlɔ̱ŋ. Caŋ ni mëë ci manɛ luek i̱ /cu la ruac i̱ ɛlɔ̱ŋ, Nyɛwec /kenɛ liŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Long time ago, there lived a girl whose name was Kalabushe. Kalabushe was a very talkative girl.Although her mother warned her not to talk too much, Kalabushe did not listen.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Manlen Nyɛwec ciɛŋɛ ni kui̱c lo̱o̱ lä, kä kui̱c in dɔ̱diɛn te dhɔr Nyɛwec ni thi̱n. Kɛ cäŋ kɛl cuɛ puɔ̱nydɛ moc kɛ juey, cuɛ thiɛl ram mi te kutdɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Kalabushe's aunt lived across the valley on the other side of Kalabushe's village.One day she fell ill. She had nobody to take care of her.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Man Nyɛwec tëë rɛy la̱t mi di̱i̱t. Ni kɛ thiaŋ wa̱r cua Nyɛwec ka̱m kuän mi no̱ŋɛ manlendɛ min tekɛ juey.
entries.english_sentence: Kalabushe's mother was very busy.It was late in the evening when she gave Kalabushe food to take to her sick aunt.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë jälɛ, cuɛ röm kɛ lɛt ran, lɛt ɛmɔ cɛ kɔnɛ ley cuɛ rɔɔdɛ kulɛ loc ni raan.
entries.english_sentence: On the way, Kalabushe met Sinson.Sinson was a hyena who had changed into a person.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Lɛt cuɛ Nyɛwec thiec i̱, "Ɛ ŋu mi kapi?" Cuɛ loc i̱, "Min kapä ɛ ri̱ŋ, kɛ tuɔŋ, kɛnɛ cak."Nyɛwec cuɛ lar bä, "I̱ naŋä ni kuän maalen mi tekɛ juey." Cu ley mɔ thokdɛ bɛl, kɛ ɣöö ŋuäcɛ ri̱ŋ ëë kap Nyɛwec ɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Sinson asked Kalabushe, "What are you carrying?"Kalabushe answered, "I am carrying meat, eggs and milk."Kalabushe's mother had warned her not to say what she was carrying.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyɛwec cuɛ lar bä i̱, "Naŋä ni kuän maalen mi tekɛ juey." Cu ley mɔ thokdɛ bɛl, kɛ ɣöö ŋuäcɛ ri̱ŋ ëë kap Nyɛwec ɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Kalabushe also said, "I am taking the food to my sick aunt."Sinson licked his lips at the thought of the meat that Kalabushe was carrying.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Lɛt cuɛ riŋ nhiam kɛ pɛ̈th kä cu kɔn cop ni jɛn dhɔr manlen Nyɛwec.
entries.english_sentence: Sinson quickly ran ahead of Kalabushe to her aunt's house.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ manlen Nyɛwec roc kä kɛ kɔrɛ cuɛ rɔɔdɛ kuɔ̱m piny kɛ pa̱ta̱n.
entries.english_sentence: He swallowed Kalabushe's aunt and then covered himself with her blanket.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci Nyɛwec cop, duel ɛ nëë bitdɛ lik. Jɛn cuɛ räth ni rɛy duëël, kä cɔalɛ manlendɛ, "Ji̱n ɛ ni maalen?"
entries.english_sentence: When Kalabushe arrived, the house was very quiet.She went inside and called out, "Aunt, where are you?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyɛwec /kenɛ jɔw manlendɛ liŋ. Cuɛ pali rɛy duëël in dɔ̱diɛn mëë ci manlendɛ tɔ̱ɔ̱c thi̱n. Jɛn cuɛ ga̱a̱c mëë cɛ ram mi ci rɔ buɔ̱r piny kɛ pa̱ta̱n mi di̱i̱t.
entries.english_sentence: Kalabushe did not hear her aunt's voice. She went to the inner room where her aunt slept.She was surprised when she saw someone covered with a big blanket.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyɛwec thiec i̱, "Maalen ɛŋu ci ji̱thku di̱t ɛ walɛ mɔ?"Cu lɛt wee, "Ɛ ɣöö bä ji̱ kulɛ liŋ ɛ gɔaa."
entries.english_sentence: Kalabushe asked, "Aunt, why are your ears so big today?"Sinson replied from under the big blanket, "So that I can hear you well."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyɛwec cuɛ thiecɛ nyɔk, "Maalen ɛŋu ci wäŋku di̱t ɛlɔ̱ŋ inɔmɔ?"Lɛt cuɛ loc i̱, "Ɛ ɣöö bä ji̱ kulɛ nɛn a gɔaa."
entries.english_sentence: Kalabushe asked again, "Aunt, why are your eyes so big today?"Sinson answered, "So I can see you well."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyɛwec thiec in jɔak ku thiec, "Maalen ɛŋu ci thokdu di̱t ɛlɔ̱ŋ inɛ ɛ walɛ?"Cu lɛt ɛ loc i̱, "Ɛ ɣöö bä ji̱ kulɛ cam!" Kä cuɛ rɔ yuɔ̱r wi̱c laŋrɛbä kiɛ dhaŋä cuɛ Nyɛwec roc.
entries.english_sentence: Kalabushe finally asked, "Aunt, why is your mouth so big today?"Sinson replied, "So I can eat you up!" He jumped from the bed and swallowed Kalabushe.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyɛwec cuɛ ŋot rɔmɛ ruac thi̱n amäni mëë tëë jiic lɛ̈t. Jɛn cuɛ thieecni ti nyin ŋuan thiëc.
entries.english_sentence: Kalabushe kept talking even when she was inside Sinson's stomach.She asked many questions.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ jɔakdɛ, cu lɛt ŋɔa̱a̱ŋ kɛn thiecni Nyɛwec ti ŋuan, kä lɛt cuɛ guic ni bɛ ŋuɔ̱li jɛ raar.
entries.english_sentence: In the end, Sinson was so tired of Kalabushe's many questions that he decided to spit her out.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cua Nyɛwec kɛnɛ manlendɛ luäk ɛ ji̱ wecdiɛn.Niɛ cäŋ ɛmɔ, /ken Nyɛwec rɔ nyɔk kɛ ruac ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ rööl.
entries.english_sentence: Kalabushe and her aunt were rescued by the villagers.From that day, Kalabushe did not talk too much to strangers.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan, rɛy ciëŋ dhɔr mi cɔal i̱ Rupca̱a̱r, tekɛ wut mi cɔali̱ Gatluaak.Gatluaak nhɔkɛ mi̱eth ɛlɔ̱ŋ. Jɛn la nhɔkɛ ni ɣöö bɛ camni ri̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: A long time ago, in the village of Nyamani, there lived a man known as Kiundu.Kiundu liked to eat very much. He especially liked to eat meat.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, cu kuäär wec nɛy diaal cɔal buul kuën gatdɛ.
entries.english_sentence: One day, the chief of the village invited all the villagers to his son's wedding.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔrɛ, cu Gatluaak nɛy ti kɔ̱kiɛn liŋ ruackɛ kɛ kui kuën dɔ̱diɛn. Jɛn thia̱kɛ kɛ wec mi cɔaal kɛ jɛ i̱ Wecluaal."Buɔ̱l da̱ŋ rɛw kɛ cäŋ kɛl kɛn diaal." Cu Gatluaak ku ca̱a̱r.
entries.english_sentence: Then Kiundu heard people talking about another wedding party. It was in a nearby village called Katumbi."Two parties on the same day!" Kiundu thought.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Gatluak cuɛ ca̱r kärɔadɛ, "Ɣän bä wä thi̱n gua̱thni kiɛndiaal. Ɣän kɛ nhiam bä wä Wicluaal, kä kɛ kɔrɛ bä kulɛ wä Rupca̱a̱r."
entries.english_sentence: "I must attend both parties," Kiundu said to himself. "I will first walk to Katumbi and then come back to Nyamani."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Gatluaak ke̱e̱r nikɛ runwaŋ kä cuɛ wä Wicluaal. Jɛn mëë cɛ cop cuɛ kuan nɛn ŋotdɛ kualɛ riali̱kɛ ikä. Gatluaak mɛk ni ɣöö."Ɣän bä wä Rupca̱a̱r kɛ nhiam, bä kulɛ wä lunyjɔk wa̱nɛmɛ ni yɔɔ."
entries.english_sentence: Kiundu woke up early in the morning and walked to Katumbi village. When he arrived he saw that the cooks were still preparing the food."I will go back to Nyamani and return here later," Kiundu decided.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Gatluaak cuɛ loc Rupca̱a̱r kɛ ŋa̱thdɛ i̱ dɔ̱ŋ bɛ ri̱ŋ jek cɛ tuak. Jɛn niɛ wa̱nɔ ci buɔthɛ näk ɛlɔ̱ŋ.Duŋni ɣöö mëë cɛ cop, cuɛ naath jek ŋotkɛ rialkɛ ni kuan i̱kä.
entries.english_sentence: Kiundu walked back to Nyamani hoping to find the meat ready. He was now hungry.But when he arrived, people there were also still preparing the food.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Gatluaak cuɛ ca̱r, "Ɣän min jianä mindan Wicluaal kualɛ tok ni tha̱t. Diɛwä jɛ i̱ cikɛ tuak kɛn kuaan ɛn täämɛ."Gatluaak cuɛ loc Wicluaal bä. Jɛn niɛ wa̱nɔ ci buɔthɛ näk ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: "When I left Katumbi they were starting to cook," he thought. "The food must be ready now."So Kiundu walked back to Katumbi. He was now very hungry.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Niɛ gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ cu Gatluaak rɔ wä jek ni Wi̱cluaal ɛ jekɛ naath cikɛ mi̱th. Ja̱a̱l wakɛ mi thöpkɛ ni kaw kɛnɛ kueen muc.Gatluaak /cuɛ thilɛ muc mi derɛ thöp. Jɛn mëë go̱o̱rɛ ɛ mi̱eth kärɔa.
entries.english_sentence: By the time Kiundu got to Katumbi, people had already eaten. Guests were giving presents to the bride and the groom.Kiundu did not have a gift to give. He only wanted to eat.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Gatluaak cu lɔcdɛ jiääk ɛ nëë ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ kui̱c kä ɣöö cɛ kuän dak. Jɛn cuɛ mɛkni ɣöö bɛ loc Rupca̱a̱r.Jɛn cucɛ kä näk buɔthɛ kä cuɛ jal ni niɛy-niɛy ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Kiundu was most disappointed about missing the food. He decided to walk back to Nyamani village.He was hungry and tired and walked very slowly.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn mëë cɛ cop Rupca̱a̱r, cuɛ naath jek tekɛ ki̱tdä kä räwkɛ. Kɛn ca mi̱th diaal thuŋ cam ni wän kiɛ mindan!
entries.english_sentence: When he arrived at Nyamani village, people were singing and dancing.They had already eaten all the food!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn mëë cuɛ liŋ i̱ thilɛ ɣɔw kuän, Gatluaak cuɛ muɔn. Kɛ ɣöö Jɛn cɛ kuan ŋa̱a̱ri̱ diaal dak.Jɛn mëë cɛ ɣɔ̱r, cuɛ madidɛ mi tɔt jek rɛy yo̱mä!
entries.english_sentence: When he heard that there was no food, Kiundu fainted. He had missed meat from both parties.When he recovered, he got some porridge in a small cup!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Gatluaak cuɛ loc cieŋ ɛ nyɔk, kä ŋotdɛ näk buɔthɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Kiundu walked home again, still hungry.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nɛmɛ ɛ Nyagɔaa. Jɛn tëëkɛ run bärɔw.Kɛ thokdɛ, ɛ jɛn Thok Nath, lot ciötdɛ ni 'mi gɔaa'.
entries.english_sentence: This is Khalai. She is seven years old.In her language, Lubukusu, her name means 'the good one.'
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyagɔaa keer kä cuɛ ruac kɛ jiath lëmuunä."Jiath lëmuunä pithni ɛ di̱t kä mockɔ dɛy ti ŋuan ti ci lɔɔr kiɛ ti buɔɔr."
entries.english_sentence: Khalai wakes up and talks to the orange tree."Please orange tree, grow big and give us lots of ripe oranges."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyagɔaa jälɛ wëë duel-gɔrkä. Rɛy duɔ̱p, cuɛ ruac kɛ juaac."Juaac, piɛthɛ ɛ la ti tɔ̱ɔ̱c kä /cuarɛ kööt."
entries.english_sentence: Khalai walks to school. On the way, she talks to the grass."Please grass, grow greener and don't dry up."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyagɔaa gaakni nɛn."Yɛn gaakni, ɣɔ̱cdun rɔamɛ jɛ thi̱n kɛ ɣöö bä yɛ kulɛ la̱th rɛy mi̱emnikä."
entries.english_sentence: Khalai sees flowers."Please flowers, keep blooming so I can put you in my hair."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyagɔaa cuɛ ruac kɛ jiath mi te duel-gɔ̱rkä."Jiath, pithni kɛ tuɔ̱ŋ ti di̱t kɛ ɣöö bi nɛy kulɛ kuen ti̱epdu."
entries.english_sentence: Khalai talks to the tree at her school."Please tree, put out big branches so we can read under your shade."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyagɔaa ruac kɛ kal jiɛn ti ɣɔ̱ɔ̱c mi te duel-gɔrkädɛ."Liɛmä ji̱, pithni ɛ bum kɛ ɣöö bi nɛy gaŋ kä nɛy ti jiäk."
entries.english_sentence: Khalai talks to the hedge round her school."Please, grow strong and protect us from bad people."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci Nyagɔaa luny cieŋ, cuɛ jiath lemuunä ben gui̱l.Cuɛ jiath thiec, "/Ken dɛyku ni lɔɔr?"
entries.english_sentence: When Khalai returns home, she visits the orange tree."Are your oranges ripe yet?" Khalai asks the tree.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "Dɛy ŋotkɛ kɛ tɔ̱ɔ̱c," cu Nyagɔaa jɛ nɛn.Nyagɔaa cuɛ jɛ lar i̱, "Bä ji̱ ben gui̱l i̱ ruun lö jiath lɛmuunä. Mi lotdɛ rɔ, bɛ tekɛ dɔw mi ci ciɛk kɛ kui̱dä."
entries.english_sentence: "The oranges are still green," sighs Khalai."I will see you tomorrow orange tree," says Khalai. "Perhaps then, you will have a ripe orange for me!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan tëëkɛ wec mi te wi̱i̱ yiëër.Tëëkɛ nyam mi tɔt mi cieŋ thi̱n mi cɔal i̱ Nyaluaal.
entries.english_sentence: There was a village near a lake.There lived a young girl. Her name was Atieno.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä gua̱n Nyaluaal ɛ wut mi deep rɛc mi ci kɛ̈kdɛ juor rɛy wecdiɛn. Tëëkɛ rieydɛ mi tɔt mi la dep kɛ jɛ.Nyaluaal la nhɔkɛ ɣöö wëë dɛɛp kɛ gua̱n kɛɛl.
entries.english_sentence: Atieno's father was a famous fisherman. He had his own little fishing canoe.Atieno enjoyed going fishing with her father.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyaluaal la nhɔkɛ ɣöö guicɛ dhɔɔl mi ŋarkɛ kurɛ ciökni.Cuɛ dhɔɔl jiök i̱ a ŋarä kɛɛl kɛ yɛ.Kä cu dhɔɔl ɛ dɔl. Cu kɛnɛ jiök i̱, "Wër ŋari kɛɛl kɛ nyieri kɛ kumdakuany."
entries.english_sentence: Atieno loved to watch the boys play football."Let me play with you," she begged them one day.The boys laughed at her, "Go and play hide and seek with girls. "
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu nyieri jɛ ji̱ök i̱, "Ji̱n ciöku bärkɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ." Kä cuɛ gaak kɛ nyieri.Cuɛ rɔɔdɛ kuum ŋarädiɛn, mi ci ɣɔw baak la wëë döny rɛy thɔlä ca̱ŋ.Cu cäŋ cua̱ määthdɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Girls said to Atieno, "Your legs are too long." Atieno was sad.Each morning, Atieno danced alone with the sun.The sun became her friend.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl /ken cäŋ lɛ̈p. Kä /ken tuut manpalɛ̈kni rööt. /Ken diit wiee. Kä /ken gaat wä duelgɔ̱rä, amäni gua̱n Nyaluaal /kenɛ wä dɛɛp kɛ rɛc.Cu Nyaluaal lɔcdɛ jiäk. Cuɛ thiec i̱, "Kä määthdä ni cäŋ ja nikä? Kä ɛ ŋu mɛ ci ɣɔw cuɔl inɛ mɛ?"
entries.english_sentence: One day, the sun did not rise. Cocks did not crow. Birds did not sing. Children did not go to school. Even her father did not go fishing.Atieno was sad. "Where is my friend, the sun? Why is it so dark today?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyaluaal gaat tin kɔ̱ŋ jiök i̱ lɔcdä cɛ jiääk ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛn walɛ. Kä cu nyiiŋ ɛ dɔl, "Cu kɛn ɛ jiök i̱ määthdu ni cäŋ jɛ mɔn ci li̱w ɣɔ, cɛ ji̱ ba̱ny piny."Kä cuɛ loc i̱, "/Kenɛ ɣä ba̱ny piny ɛn määthdä ni cäŋ kä /kenɛ li̱w."
entries.english_sentence: Atieno told the other children how sad she was. But they laughed at her, "Perhaps your friend the sun, is dead. Or perhaps it ran away from you."Atieno said, "The sun is my friend. It cannot die."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyaluaal lɔcdɛ jiääk ɛlɔ̱ŋ, cuɛ riŋ dueel.Cuɛ kurɛ däman kuɛt ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Atieno was so sad that she ran to the house.She kicked her brother's ball very hard.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ ca̱r kɛ gua̱a̱th mi tɔt, "Kä cuɛ we ɣän bä ŋar kɛ jɛn kurɛ nɛmɛ amäni mi ci mäthdä ni cäŋ luny jɔk."Cuɛ kurɛ käp kä cuɛ riŋ raar kɛ jɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Atieno thought, "I will play with this ball until my friend, the sun returns."She picked up the ball and ran out with it.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyaluaal cuɛ kurɛ la̱th piny. Cuɛ wee, "Bä ŋar ce̱tkɛ kɛn dhɔɔl tɔ̱tɔ̱."Kä cuɛ kurɛ dɛ kuɛt. Cuɛ kuɛ̈t nhial kä cu kurɛ räth ni rɛy puɔ̱ɔ̱ri.
entries.english_sentence: Atieno put the ball on the ground. She thought, "I can play just like those boys."She kicked the ball hard. It went up and up into the cloudy sky.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu nyiiŋ diaal ɛ guiɛc nhial. Kä cu kurɛ bath rɛy pua̱a̱ri ti tekɛ wuɔ̱ɔ̱n.Kä cu nɛy dial biɛt ɛ bi pinydɛ wä lik.
entries.english_sentence: Everybody stared up. The ball disappeared into the thick clouds.There was total silence.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ gua̱a̱th mi tɔt cu wuɔ̱ɔ̱n indaan thiɛl, kä cu cäŋ jɔɔc. Cu ti diaal luɔc gua̱a̱th ni kiɛn.Kä cu naath luoc lätkiɛn tin la la̱tkɛ ɛ kɛn.
entries.english_sentence: Suddenly, the thick clouds cleared. The sun appeared. Life returned to the village once again.Everybody prepared to do what they always did.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä /ken Nyaluaal ɛ ŋäth ɛn ɣöö ci cäŋ luny jɔk rɛy dhɔaariɛn. Duŋni ɣöö min di̱t ni jɛn ɛ ɣöö ci cäŋ ku thuŋ luny jɔk rɛy ciëŋädɛ ce̱tkɛ ta̱a̱ dɛ min wän.Cuɛ nyiiŋ tin kɔn jiök i̱, "Määthdä ni cäŋ cɛ luny jɔk!"
entries.english_sentence: Atieno could not believe that the sun was back in the village. But most of all, the sun was back in her life.She told the children, "My friend, the sun is back!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔr runi tëë ci wä, Cäŋ kɛnɛ Pi̱ cikɛ kɔnɛ mäth. Kɛn cieŋkɛ wi̱i̱ muɔ̱ɔ̱n kɛɛl.
entries.english_sentence: Many years ago, Sun and Water were great friends. Both lived on earth together.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cäŋ la gui̱i̱lɛ Pi̱ ni ciaŋ ɛlɔ̱ŋ, ɛni ɣöö /ken Pi̱ Cäŋ met gui̱l.
entries.english_sentence: Sun used to visit Water very often, but Water never went to visit Sun.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Pi̱ cua loc i̱ ɛ kui̱c kä ɣöö dhɔr Ca̱ŋ kuiyɛ."Ɣän mi cakɔ ben kɔnɛ ji̱ gɔaalä, dee nɛy yɛ lɔak raar," jɛn cuɛ lat.
entries.english_sentence: At last Sun asked Water why he never came to visit.Water replied that Sun's house was too small. "If I come with my family we will drive you out," he said.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu Pi̱ wee i̱, "Mi gööri ɣöö bä ji̱ gui̱l, lätni gua̱a̱th mi di̱i̱t. Ɣän ta̱a̱ kɛ nɛy ti ŋuan, kä kɛn, ba duël tɔ̱ɔ̱yä ti ŋuan go̱r."
entries.english_sentence: Then Water said, "If you wish me to visit you, build a very large compound. My people are very many, and take up a lot of room."Sun promised to build a very big compound.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cäŋ cuɛ loc dhɔɔrɛ kä ciekdɛ, Pay, cuɛ lor ni kɛ duɔɔth. Cäŋ cuɛ la̱r Pay ɛn min cɛ yac rɔ kä cɛ la̱t Pi̱.
entries.english_sentence: Sun returned home to his wife, Moon, who greeted him with a broad smile. Sun told Moon what he had promised Water.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ruɔ̱ndɛ, jɛn cuɛ tok lätdɛ cieŋ mi di̱i̱t kɛ kui̱ rɔmä määthä diɛn thi̱n.
entries.english_sentence: The next day he started building a huge compound in which to entertain his friend.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Niɛ wa̱nɔ mëë ci ciëŋ thuɔ̱k kɛ lätni, cuɛ Pi̱ thiec kɛ ɣöö dëë gui̱l.
entries.english_sentence: As soon as the compound was completed, he asked Water to come and visit them.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci Pi̱ cop, jɛn Cäŋ cuɛ thiec ɛn ɣöö mi bɛ thiɛl riɛk kɛ cothdɛ rɛc.Cu Cäŋ ɛ loc, "Ji̱öö kiɛ ɣää, bia rɛc, määthadiɛn."
entries.english_sentence: When Water arrived, he asked Sun whether it would be safe for him to enter."Yes, come in, my friend," Sun answered.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Pi̱ cua ri̱i̱ŋ rɛc tok.Ɛ na̱a̱m kɛ jɛ ɛ nyäŋ, rɛc, guëëk, kuɛt, thɔ̱ɔ̱l, luëëk, näär-muɔ̱ɔ̱ni, mieeri kɛnɛ ley yiëër diaal.
entries.english_sentence: Water began to flow in.He was accompanied by crocodiles, fish, frogs, snakes, snails, flukes, turtles, and all the water animals.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ pɛ̈th cu Pi̱ peek muɔ̱ɔ̱li. Jɛn cuɛ Cäŋ thiec i̱, "Ŋotdɛ thiɛlɛ riɛk."Cu Cäŋ ɛ nyɔk kɛ luɔ̱c, "Ɣää." Pi̱ cukɛ cu ben rɛc ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Very soon Water was knee-deep. He asked Sun if it was still safe."Yes," Sun again answered. So more of water's people  came in.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Pi̱ cukɛ räth ni gua̱a̱th mi cop ŋuäk nath. Jɛn cuɛ Cäŋ thiec, "Dee nɛy ben rɛc ɛ ŋuan?"Cu Cäŋ ɛ loc, "Ɣää!"Pi̱ cukɛ ben rɛc, amäni mëë Cäŋ kɛnɛ cukɛ rɔ wä jek ni wi̱i̱ duëël kiɛ nikä kum duëël.
entries.english_sentence: Water reached the level of the top of a person's head. He asked Sun, "Can more of my people come in?" Sun and Moon both answered, "Yes."Water flowed on, until Sun and Moon had to perch themselves on the top of the roof.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cäŋ kɛnɛ Pay cua kɛ kuɔ̱k ɣöö cukɛ copni nhial. Kɛn cua cu ciɛŋ ni nhial niɛ wa̱nɔ.
entries.english_sentence: Water's people continued to rush in. Very soon they reached the top of the roof.Sun and Moon were forced to go up into the sky. They have remained in the sky ever since.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rɛy Ruɔ̱ɔ̱p Nyaandit, tëëkɛ gɔɔk mi cieŋ kɛ jiääk lɔaac.Kɛ gua̱a̱th mi cɛ wee diethɛ, la li̱w dɛykɛ.
entries.english_sentence: In Miwa Forest, there lived a monkey who was always sad.This was because every time she had a baby, it died.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu tëkdɛ bɛ̈c ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛn gɔɔk kɛ ɣöö la li̱w dɛykɛ ni ciaŋ. La yuorɛ rɔdɛ nhial kä bɛ rɔdɛ lɛ nyɔk kɛ yuor piny.Bɛ rɔdɛ yuɔr tuuŋ jiaath ɛmɛ kä kɛ kɔrɛ bɛ rɔdɛ lɛ nyɔk kɛ yuɔr kä min dɔ̱ŋ kä wie ɛ i̱, "Kwi! Kwi! Kwi!"
entries.english_sentence: The pain of losing her babies made Monkey jump up and down.She would jump to one branch, then to another, and cry out, "Kwi! Kwi! Kwi!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: La tëëkɛ jiɛ̈th lɔaac mi cɛ gɔak tin kɔ̱ŋkiɛn nɛn kɛ dɛykiɛn.
entries.english_sentence: Monkey was sadder when she saw other monkeys with their babies.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ nyuur tuuŋ jiaath.Kɛ kɔr ni̱ni cu jiɛ̈th lɔaacdɛ wekɛ mi rebɛ ni rɔ ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: The sad monkey sat on a branch.Days passed and she cried more and more.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ gua̱a̱th cuɛ dieth kɛ dɔw ɛ nyɔk.Cuɛ go̱r ɛn ɣöö bɛ dɔwdɛ naŋ dup kɛ ɣöö ba lɛ wä nɛn ɛ nɛy tin jäl dup kɛ ɣöö ba lɛ wä nɛn kä dɔ̱ŋ dëë jɛ poth.
entries.english_sentence: Then she gave birth again. She decided to take the baby to the path.She wanted people passing by, to see the baby and wish it well.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Gɔɔk cuɛ dɔw dee la̱th däär duɔ̱p. Niɛ gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ, tekɛ kääk mi loc cieŋ.Jɛn cuɛ dɔw gɔak nɛn tɔ̱ɔ̱cä gekä duɔ̱p.
entries.english_sentence: Monkey put her baby on the path. At that time, a hunter was returning home.He saw the baby monkey lying on the side of the path.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kääk dɔw naŋ dhɔɔrɛ. Mëë ci kääk cop cieŋ, cu gaatkɛ da̱ŋ diɔ̱k ti tɔ dhɔɔl dɔw gɔak käp.
entries.english_sentence: The hunter carried the baby monkey to his house.When the hunter reached home, his three sons wanted to hold the baby monkey.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu dhɔɔl ki̱et:Yɔrɛ nhial!Yɔrɛ jɛ piny!Yuɔ̱rɛ jɛ ɣä!Yuɔ̱rɛ jɛ jɛ!Jɛn dɔw gɔak la yuɔ̱r kɛ jɛ ram kɛnɛ ramɔ.
entries.english_sentence: The boys sang:Throw it up!Throw it down!Throw it to me!Throw it to him!The baby monkey was thrown from one child to the other.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Man dɔw gɔak cɛ rɔ tɔ̱w wi̱i̱ jiaath kä guicɛ kɛ.Jɛn dualɛ i̱ dɔ̱ŋ bi dɔwdɛ li̱w, ce̱tkɛ tëë kɔn.
entries.english_sentence: Mother Monkey hid in a tree and watched them.She was afraid that this baby would also die, like the others.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔrɛ cu ciek kääkä gaatkɛ nɛn ŋarkɛ kɛ dɔw gɔak ɛ duŋ tiit ɛmɔ.Jɛn cuɛ jɛ lar, "Tiɛtdɛ jɛ! Nöŋɛ jɛ wa̱nɛmɛ! Bia pa̱l pɛ̈ɛ̈n!"
entries.english_sentence: Then the hunter's wife saw her children playing with the little monkey.She said, "Be careful! Bring it here. You will drop it!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn cuɛ dɔw gɔak kuɔ̱l puɔ̱ɔ̱nydɛ, kä cuɛ jɛ poth.
entries.english_sentence: She took the baby monkey in her arms, and blessed it.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn ciek kääkä cuɛ dɔw gɔak la̱th piny. Man gɔak cuɛ dɔwdɛ naŋ kä cuɛ cu wä ni rɛy ruɔ̱ɔ̱p.Niɛ gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ kän man gɔak dɔwdɛ rɔ lɛ nyɔk kɛ lia̱a̱.
entries.english_sentence: The hunter's wife put the baby monkey down. Mother Monkey picked the baby up and disappeared into the forest.Mother Monkey never lost another baby from then on.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyadak kɛnɛ cieŋmani cieŋkɛ kä Juba, ɛ rɛk mi la but ji̱kɛ cuŋä kɛ la̱t rɛy Jinub Thuda̱n. Nyadak të kä kilɛ̈th 3.Jɛn tëëkɛ lɔc mi gɔaa kä pɛlɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Fana and her family live in Debre Birhan, a busy town in Ethiopia. Fana is a Grade 3 student.She is good-hearted and wise.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyadak nhɔkɛ ley. Jɛn tëëkɛ nyaaw, kɛ manpalɛ̈kni da̱ŋ rɛw, kɛ dɛl kɛnɛ guuk.Jɛn naŋɛ pek mi bäär kɛɛl kɛ ley, mi̱thɛ kɛ, kä ŋarɛ kɛ kɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Fana loves animals. She has a cat, two hens, a goat and a dove.She spends time with these animals, feeding them, and playing with them.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cäŋ kɛl, Nyadak wëë kɛ mi ŋarɛ rɛy duëlgɔ̱rä kɛnɛ mäthnikɛ.Jɛn cuɛ nɛn ɛn ɣöö tëkɛ tha̱ŋ gan ti bökɛ guɔ̱kni kɛ pääm. Cuɛ rɔɔdɛ thiec i̱, "Ɛŋu mi bökɛ guɔ̱kni mɔ?"
entries.english_sentence: One day, Fana was playing in the school yard with her friends.She noticed some children throwing stones at doves. "Why are they hurting the doves?" she asked herself.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ ŋar päl kä cuɛ riŋ kä gaat tin bökɛ guɔ̱kni kɛ dööl kiɛ pääm.Kɛ nhiam ken mäthnikɛ jɛ liŋ ɛn min ci tuɔɔk, cu kɛn ɛ guɔ̱ɔ̱r.Cuɛ yɔal i̱, "Pa̱lɛ yori päämni!"
entries.english_sentence: She stopped playing and ran towards the children who were throwing stones. At first her friends didn't understand what was happening, then they followed her."Stop throwing stones!" shouted Fana.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn gaat ɛ tɔ̱ cuarɔ̱ bar.Nyadak cuɛ guɔ̱kni da̱ŋ rɛw tin ca moc buɔ̱ɔ̱t käp. Cɛ buɔ̱ɔ̱t nɛn gɔ̱knikiɛn.Cuɛ guɔ̱kni da̱ŋ rɛw tin kɔn naŋ cieŋ kɛ ɣöö bɛ kɛ wä tit.
entries.english_sentence: The other children ran away.Fana caught the two injured doves. She saw wounds on their wings.She decided to take the two doves home to look after them.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn cuɛ guɔ̱kni mi̱eeth. Kɛ thiaŋ jɛn cuɛ la̱r diëëthkɛ ɛn ɣöö cɛ guɔ̱kni kän.
entries.english_sentence: She fed the doves. In the evening she told her family about how she saved the doves.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ runwaŋ, Nyadak kɛnɛ diëëthkɛ cukɛ wä duel wal leyni kɛ ɣöö ba guɔ̱kni wä moc kɛ wal.Kɛ kɔr ni̱ni ti tɔt, cu guɔ̱kni buɔ̱ɔ̱tkiɛn puɔl. Cu Nyadak lɔcdɛ tɛɛth ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: In the morning, Fana and her parents went to the clinic and got medicine for the doves.After a few days, the doves' wounds healed. Fana felt very happy.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyadak ni ciaŋ la lätdɛ jɛ mäthnikɛ ɛn ɣöö, "Ɣän nhɔakɛ ley. Ley luäkɛ kɔn kɛ mäthnikɔn. Kɛ kui̱c ɛmɔ bi kɔn kɛ dhil gaŋ kä banɛ kɛ yop."
entries.english_sentence: Fana always tells her friends, "I love animals. Animals help us and they are our friends. We must protect and preserve them."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan Kuoth kɛnɛ Guak kɛ mäth ti di̱t.Cäŋ kɛl cukɛ wä gör ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k wec mi na̱n kɛ wecdiɛn. Cu Guak Kuoth jiök i̱, "Bi kɔn rɔ gön pi̱."Cu Kuoth ɛ loc i̱, "Ban pi̱ wä jek nhiam."
entries.english_sentence: Long ago, Fox and God were friends. One day, they went to look for cows at a village far away from home. Fox said to his friend, "We should take water with us."God said, "No, we will get water there."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rɛy ja̱liɛn, cu Guak rɛw ɛ näk. Cuɛ Kuoth jiök i̱, "Ci rɛw ɣä näk, göörä pi̱."Cu Kuoth ɛ jiök i̱, "Ti̱c juaac ɛ tɔ̱, bi pi̱ jek thi̱n." Cu Guak juaac ti̱c, cu pi̱ ben raar kä cukɛ maath.
entries.english_sentence: On their way, Fox was thirsty. He said, "God, I want water. I am thirsty."God replied, "Pull out those grasses next to the road, you will get water." Fox pulled out the grasses and water came from the ground. They drank.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë cikɛ cop wec ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k, cu kɛn ɣɔ̱k rɛw naŋ kä cu kɛn kɛ yian kɛ dep.Mëë ci ji̱ ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k kɛ nɛn, cua jɛn riŋdiɛn guɔ̱ɔ̱rkɛ kɛ.Cu Guak Kuoth jiök i̱, "Ci naath ben, ba kɔn käp."Cu Kuoth ɛ loc i̱, "/Cu dual."
entries.english_sentence: They reached the village and went to the cattle camp. They took two cows, tied them with ropes, and quickly left.But the cattle owners saw them and ran after them. Fox cried, "God, people are coming after us. They will catch us!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci naath thia̱k, cuɛ Guak moc diɛɛr mi di̱i̱t.Cuɛ Kuoth nyɔk kɛ jiök i̱, "Ci naath cop." Cu Kuoth ɛ loc i̱, "/Cu diɛɛr."Mëë ci ji̱ ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k thia̱k kɛ kɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ, cu Guak yɔal ɛlɔ̱ŋ i̱, "Kuoth! Ba kɔn käp ɛn täämɛ!"
entries.english_sentence: As the people approached, Fox became more worried. "God! People are coming closer," cried Fox. "Don't worry," God responded.When the cattle owners were very close, Fox cried out, "Help, God! They will catch us now!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Kuoth wee, "Käp dep yaaŋdu kɛnɛ yiat cio̱kädä min di̱i̱t." Cu Guak kɛ käp.Cu Kuoth wi̱cdɛ yiath piny kä cu piny rɔ lɛp. Cukɛ coth piny amäni ɣɔ̱k kɛɛl.Cukɛ bath waaŋ nath kä cukɛ wä päl raar ni dhɔɔriɛn. Cu Guak lät tɔ̱tɔ̱ tit.
entries.english_sentence: God said, "Hold my toe and the rope of your cow." Fox did so. God put his forehead on the ground, and the earth opened up. God dived into the ground with his cow, and Fox followed.The earth closed behind them. They came up in their village.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ dɔ̱diɛn, cu Guak määthdɛ ni Nyoŋgol jiök i̱, "Määthdä! Ban wä gör ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k."Cu Nyoŋgol ɛ nhɔk nikä kɛɛl, kä cua jɛn tɛthdiɛn piny lockɛ wi̱c ëëdan.Cu Nyoŋgol wee, "Ban rɔ gön pi̱." Kä cu Guak ɛ loc i̱, "Ɣey! Ban pi̱ wä jek däärɔ."
entries.english_sentence: The next day, Fox called his friend, Vulture. Fox said, "My friend! Let's go and look for cows."Vulture agreed and said, "We should take water with us." Fox replied, "We will get water on the way."They left home for the same cattle camp as the day before.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rɛy ja̱liɛn, cu rɛw kɛ näk, kä cukɛ cop guäth ëëdan.Cu Nyoŋgol Guak jiök i̱, "Ci rɛw ɣä näk."Cu Guak Nyoŋgol jiök i̱, "Ti̱c juaac ɛ tɔ̱ bi pi̱ jek thi̱n."
entries.english_sentence: On their way, they both began to feel thirsty. They reached the same spot next to the grasses. "I am very thirsty," complained Vulture.Fox said to Vulture. "Pull out those grasses, you will find water."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyoŋgol juaac ti̱c, duŋdɛ ni ɣöö thiɛlɛ pi̱ ti cu ben raar.Cu Guak rɔ mat ni ti̱cä, kä cuɛ ŋot thiɛlɛ pi̱.Cukɛ pi̱ wä go̱r guäth mi dɔ̱diɛn.
entries.english_sentence: Vulture pulled out the grasses, but there was no water. Fox pulled out more grasses, but still there was no water.So, they had to look for water in other places.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë cikɛ cop wec ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k, cukɛ ɣɔ̱k da̱ŋ rɛw naŋ. Cukɛ kɛ yian kɛ dep. Mëë ci ji̱ ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k kɛ nɛn, cua jɛn riŋdiɛn kɔɔriɛn.Cu Nyoŋgol naath nɛn kɔɔriɛn kɛ kɛtni. Cuɛ wee i̱, "Guak! Naath ɛ bëëni."Cu Guak ɛ loc i̱, "/Cu dual."
entries.english_sentence: Fox and Vulture finally reached the cattle camp and took two cows. The cattle owners saw them and ran after them.Vulture saw the people following them with sticks. He said "Fox! People are coming." "Don't be afraid," replied Fox.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci naath thia̱k, cu Nyoŋgol diɛɛr ɛlɔ̱ŋ. Cuɛ wee, "Guak! Ci naath thia̱k kɛ kɔn."Cu Guak wee, "/Cu diɛɛr. Käp dep yaaŋdu kɛnɛ yiatdä min di̱i̱t."Cu Nyoŋgol kɛ käp.
entries.english_sentence: The cattle owners got closer. Vulture cried, "Fox! People will catch us now!"Fox said, "Hold my toe and the rope of your cow." Vulture did so.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Guak wi̱cdɛ yiath piny mi bi piny rɔ lɛp bɛ, duŋdɛ ɣöö /kenɛ rɔ lɛp.Cuɛ yiath piny nikä ti nyin ŋuan. /Ci piny rɔ lɛp.Cu Guak Nyoŋgol jiök i̱, "Päl yiatdä."Cuɛ päl kä cua jɛn barɛ kɛ rɔ.
entries.english_sentence: Fox placed his head on the ground to open it. But the ground didn't open up. Fox tried many times, but nothing happened."Let go of my toe!" Fox shouted at Vulture. Fox ran away, leaving Vulture with the two cows.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Niɛ wanɔ mɔ, cu ji̱ ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k ben, cua jɛn käp Nyoŋgol, dua̱ckɛ jɛ wi̱i̱dɛ kɛnɛ ŋuäkdɛ.Nɔmɔ ɛ jɛn jak Nyoŋgol kä thiɛl mi̱em wec kɛnɛ ŋuäkdɛ amäni wa̱lɛ.
entries.english_sentence: The cattle owners caught Vulture and beat him. Vulture was so frightened that all his feathers fell out. Eventually, most of the vulture's feathers grew back, but not all of them.Until today, this is the reason that vultures are bald on their heads and necks.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan tëëkɛ wut mi mat bär kɛnɛ dhök, cɔalɛ Duŋdi̱i̱t. Jen lenyɛ nɛy diaal tëë cieŋ rɛy wecdiɛn kɛ di̱t.Kɛ di̱tdɛ nɔmɔ, mi ca nɛn dual gaat kɛ jɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Once upon a time, there was a giant man who was bigger than everyone in his village. This man's name was Dungdit.Dungdit was so big that small children in the village were afraid of him.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rɛy wecdiɛn ɛn Duŋdi̱i̱t, lätdɛ lät tin la̱tkɛ thi̱n, ce̱tkɛ min te puɔ̱r ka̱a̱kni, kɛ dëp rɛc, kɛ ja̱l ciökni mi di̱i̱t.Jɛn rɛy la̱tdɛ, matdɛ pɛ̈th kɛnɛ kët mi di̱i̱t. Ɛn pɛ̈th la̱t ɛ di̱i̱t ɛmɔ, la thukɛ lätkɛ ɛ ŋot nɛy diaal.
entries.english_sentence: Dungdit liked hunting, fishing, and farming. He liked trekking for miles around his village.He worked quickly and enthusiastically. He sang songs as he worked, and always finished his work before others finished theirs.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ ɣöö bärɛ kä dho̱kɛ, /cɛ riäŋ. La rëpkɛ jɛ, ɛ ji̱ dhɔaariɛn kɛnɛ mäthnikɛ, kɛ tha̱a̱ŋ kuan. Duŋdɛ ɣöö cäŋ ca rep /cɛ ro̱ŋ bä.Mi jekɛ rɔ /kenɛ ria̱ŋ, bɛ cu mac ni naath.
entries.english_sentence: This giant was always hungry. He was rarely satisfied by the food he ate. His friends and family shared their food with him, but his stomach didn't easily get full.Sometimes Dungdit was so hungry that he stole food from his friends and family!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Jɛn cuɛ bɛ̈c ɛlɔ̱ŋ, kɛ ɣöö /ci kuän ro̱ŋ.Cuɛ räthni mi̱th dɛɛni jiɛɛn, amäni ciök jiɛɛn tin tɛ̈tkɛ piny.Kɛ kɔrɛ mëë cɛ mi̱ethdiɛn tok, cu puɔ̱nydɛ buɔ̱m, kä cuɛ pual, ɛ cu lɔcdɛ tɛɛth ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: In his village, people ate mostly millet with fish or meat. To satisfy his hunger, the giant began to try new types of food. He tried fruits and vegetables. He tried berries, leaves, roots, and stems from edible plants.Dungdit added fruits and vegetables to his diet. He became stronger, happier, and healthier.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci puɔ̱nydɛ gɔaa, cuɛ wi̱c naath yi̱c kɛ min dho̱k kɛ jɛ.Cukɛ jɛ thiec, "Duŋdi̱i̱t ɛ leeŋu cämi mɔ?"Cuɛ loc i̱, "Ɣän camä ni ji̱th jiɛɛn kɛnɛ dɛy amäni ciökiɛn."
entries.english_sentence: Because of his new diet, Dungdit grew even bigger and stronger.People in the village told him, "You look good!" And they asked, "What have you been eating recently?""I have been eating leaves, tubers, fruits, and vegetables," he answered.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Niɛ gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ, cu naath mi̱eth dɛɛni jiɛɛn kɛnɛ rɛc dɔp, cu buɔ̱m kɛnɛ pual pua̱a̱ny nath rɔdiɛn rep, kä cuɛ lo̱ckiɛn jakä tɛth.
entries.english_sentence: Soon, everyone in the village was eating a balanced diet with vegetables, fruits, millet, and fish.Everyone became healthier, stronger, and happier.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë cikɛ rɔ dol, cu kɛn ɛ jiök i̱, "Duŋdi̱i̱t, käni mun ɛmɛ ɛla kaakdu."Cua nyɔk kɛ lär i̱, "Bakɔ ji̱ mockɛ la̱a̱t kɛ kui̱ lätnikun."
entries.english_sentence: The people of the village gave Dungdit a plot of land so that he could farm fruit and vegetables. They helped him with the daily activities.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu ram kɛl rɛydiɛn ɛ jiök i̱, "Duŋdi̱i̱t, ci duɔ̱ɔ̱p teekä mi ro̱ŋ rialikä kɛ kui̱da." Kɛ ɣöö nɔ, ba ji̱ jakä kuäär rɛy wecdan ɛmɛ, kä bi ŋot go̱ r i̱ nɛy ikä, kɛ buɔ̱m kɛnɛ luäŋ la̱tdu min di̱i̱t.Cu naath dit kit kɛ rɔal wäkɛ i̱, "Bi jääny kɛ tëk kuäära min di̱i̱t, ni Duŋdi̱i̱t!"
entries.english_sentence: The villagers said to Dungdit, "You have positively changed our lives, we want to change your life! We want you to be our leader, and to explore more things that can improve our lives."The people sang and shouted, "Long live our great, generous, giant leader!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ run tëë wal, cu Guɛk kɛnɛ Nyaaw Nyami̱er rɛk kɛ kuën.Nyal nhɔkɛ ni Guɛk duŋdɛ ɣöö gua̱n nyaal nhɔkɛ ni Nyaaw.
entries.english_sentence: Once upon a time, Frog and Cat both wanted to marry Turtle's daughter.Turtle's daughter loved Frog, but her father preferred Cat.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci gua̱n nyaal ɛ ŋa̱c i̱ nhɔk nyaadɛ ni Guɛk, cuɛ ca̱p la̱t.Cuɛ nyadɛ jiök i̱, "Ŋuɛ̈tni da̱ŋ rɛw ti̱ti̱ bi kɛnɛ ŋɔc kä ramɔ bi raan lenyɔ bɛ ji̱ kuɛn."
entries.english_sentence: When Turtle learned that his daughter loved Frog, he came up with a plan."These two gentlemen will race each other, and the winner will marry you," he told his daughter.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Mi̱eer ɛ la̱r Guɛk kɛnɛ Nyaaw bä i̱ bi kɛn kööŋ kɛ wuɔ̱ɔ̱r. Ramɔ bi raan lenyɔ, ɛ jɛn bi nyaadɛ kuɛn ɔ.Cu Guɛk ɛ thiec mi derɛ nhɔk i̱ bi kööŋ ni kɛn kɛ kët kɛnɛ Nyaaw, duŋdɛ ɣöö cu Mi̱eer ɛ lo̱k.
entries.english_sentence: Turtle told Frog and Cat about the race.The frog suggested swimming instead of running, but the turtle refused.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyaaw läär ɛmɔ wä la̱r mäthnikɛ. Cu lɔcdiɛn tɛɛth ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ ɣöö ŋäc kɛnɛ i̱ Guɛk la yuurɛ ni rɔ.Cu kɛn cäŋ ko̱o̱ŋä lip baaŋ ɛ /ken kɛn rɔ rialikä.
entries.english_sentence: Cat shared this news with his friends. They were happy because they knew that frogs cannot run. They only leap.The cats waited for the day of the competition, but did not prepare themselves for the race.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Guɛk duɔl kɛnɛ mäthnikɛ.Cuɛ kɛ jiök i̱, "Mi̱eer cɛ ɣä lo̱k. Ɛ jɛn i̱ bi nɛy ŋɔc ni jɛ kɔnɛ Nyaaw. Ramɔ bi raan lenyɔ bɛ nyaadɛ kuɛn."
entries.english_sentence: The betrothed frog also met with his friends to tell them the news.He said, "Turtle turned down my proposal. He said that Cat and I must run a race, and the winner will marry his daughter."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu määthdɛ kɛl ɛ loc kɛ pɛ̈th wee i̱, "Ɛŋu /ciɛ lär Mi̱eerɔ derɛ jak ni ji̱ kä ket kɛnɛ Nyaaw. Biɛ läny kɛ ɣöö Nyaaw dualɛ kɛ pi̱."Cu Guɛk ɛ loc i̱, "Cä la̱r jɛ i̱ dee kööŋ ni nɛy kɛ kët kä cɛ lo̱k. Cɛ ti diaal lo̱k."Cu kɛn guic ɛla ti cɛ wi̱cdiɛn yi̱c.
entries.english_sentence: One of his friends quickly suggested, "Why don't you tell the turtle to let you and the cat swim? You will win because cats fear water."The betrothed frog responded, "I suggested a swimming competition, but he refused."Frog's friends were frustrated.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu määthdɛ mi dɔ̱ŋ wee i̱, "Nɔmɔ ɛ mi thia̱kthia̱k. Mi wä kɔn rɔ mat kɛɛl, bi nyaamɔ kuɛn ɛ ji̱n ɛ cäŋ ni mɔ Nyaaw bum ni jɛn ɔ, di̱t ni jɛn kä puɔl ni jɛn kä ji̱ mɔ. Canɛ ca̱r kɛ ca̱a̱p tin deri jɛ leny kɛ kɛ."
entries.english_sentence: Another frog said, "This is an easy problem to solve. If we are united, you will marry Turtle's daughter."Cat is stronger, bigger, and faster than you. But together, we can think of strategies to win this race."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Guɛk mi dɔ̱ŋ wee i̱, "Nɔmɔ ɛ ca̱r mi gɔaa. Kɛ ɣöö cäät kɔn, bi ram kɛl wuɔ̱ɔ̱r tok kɛnɛ Nyaaw. /Cɛ jɛ bi ŋic."Bi Guëëk tin kɔ̱ŋ rɔ tɔ̱w rɛy juaacni ɛ thieek kɛ gëk duɔ̱p. Bi Cɔwnyaal wä cuɔ̱ŋ jɔkcieŋ. Bi määthdan ni Kun lät ɛla ram min bi ta̱a̱ in ko̱o̱ŋ kɛ naath guic."
entries.english_sentence: "Frogs look alike, so we can take turns in the race and the cat won't notice," suggested a different frog."One frog will start. Other frogs will hide in the grass by the road, and we will swap during the race."The betrothed frog will hide in Turtle's backyard."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci Kun tha̱pa̱a̱r koth, cu Guɛk in nhiam wuɔ̱ɔ̱r tok kɛnɛ Nyaaw. Kɛ gua̱a̱th mi tɔt, cuɛ wak i̱, "Tɔrɔt! Tɔrɔt! Tɔrɔt!"Cu Guɛk mi dɔ̱ŋ rɔ yuɔr nhiam Nyaawä kä cuɛ wak i̱, "Tɔrɔt! Tɔrɔt! Tɔrɔt!" Cu Guɛk mi dɔ̱ŋ rɔ nyɔk kɛ yuɔr nhiam Nyaawä, cuɛ wak i̱, "Tɔrɔt! Tɔrɔt! Tɔrɔt!"
entries.english_sentence: Rat was the judge. She blew the whistle to begin the race.The cat ran ahead. After a short distance, the frog cried, "Croak, croak, croak." Another frog jumped out in front of the cat, crying, "Croak, croak, croak."Cat ran faster. But the frogs continued to take turns.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyaaw wi̱cdɛ nyuɔɔn kä cuɛ cuuc.Kɛ jɔak cu Guɛk in kuen rɔ yuɔr rɛy kal gua̱nthudɛ kɛ pɛ̈th kä cuɛ wak i̱, "Tɔrɔt! Tɔrɔt! Tɔrɔt!"
entries.english_sentence: The cat was confused. He felt exhausted as he ran towards the turtles' compound.The betrothed frog suddenly leapt ahead of the cat, beating him into the compound.Frog cried, "Croak, croak, croak!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Kun wee i̱, "Ci Guɛk Nyaaw leny."Cu Nyaaw ɛ gak, "Ɣän /ci ɣän ɛ ŋɔc kɔnɛ Guɛk kɛl. Ci kɛn ɣä wen. Ci kɛn ɣä wen."
entries.english_sentence: Rat declared, "Frog won the contest against Cat."The cat complained, "I am sure I did not run with only one frog. They tricked me. They tricked me!"But the rat would not listen to the cat's complaints.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kun /kenɛ min latkɛ ɛ Nyaaw liŋ. Ɛ tookɛ niɛ cäŋ ɛmɔ, cu Kun kɛnɛ Nyaaw cieŋ ɛla ji̱ tɛ̈r.Cu Mi̱eer kɛnɛ Guɛk ɛ mäth ti nhɔakɛ rɔ.Cu kɛn a ji̱ cieŋ kä cukɛ cieŋ kɛ tɛ̈th lɔaac.
entries.english_sentence: From that day on, the rat and the cat became enemies.The turtle and the frog became good friends.They got married, became a family, and lived happily ever after.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Luth ɛ rec in col ce̱tnikɛ yiec cukä. Colɛ ɛ cui̱c kä ɛ nyäthnyäth. Ta̱a̱dɛ ce̱tdɛ kɛ thɔ̱l min cɔal i̱ nyääl. Ku duŋdɛ ɣöö camkɛ jɛ. Kui̱ cɔ̱wkɛ kɛ ɣöö di̱t ni ri̱i̱ŋdɛ.Tëëkɛ räl ti tɔt ti cɔalkɛ gɛl. Mi ci raan kɛ cam, la thiecɛ ni gɛ̈l mi dɔ̱diɛn kɛ ɣöö comkɛ ɛ yum. Ɛn luth ciɛŋɛ yieer duŋdɛ ɣöö mi ci ɣɔw rueel, la delɛ piny.
entries.english_sentence: A lungfish is black or brown and slippery to touch. Its meat is delicious!Lungfishes live in rivers. In the dry season they can burrow underground when there is not enough water.Unlike other types of fish, the lungfish can breathe air.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Rɛy ri̱cäda, thilɛ ram mi leny gua̱a̱r kɛ mi̱eth luuthni kuɛ la ɣöö pa̱a̱rkɔ ɛ juc.Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, cu gua̱a̱r ɣɔ̱k yial laak. /Ka̱ duɔth luɛŋ kɛ ɣöö nhɔakä ta̱a̱ gekä gua̱a̱r ɛlɔ̱ŋ.Mëë cakɔ cop paan, cu gua̱a̱r jɔkdɛ cat kɛ ɣöö luaaŋɛ puɔ̱nydɛ kɛ ŋuëk kakä. Cuɔ ɣɔ̱kɔ ku la liacä lɛɛr kamä min te gua̱a̱r pur waŋdɛ.
entries.english_sentence: One day, my father went to graze our cattle. I did not want to remain at home because I love to spend time with my father.When we arrived at the pasture, my father relaxed under a cedar tree as he was tired. I looked after the cattle.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Tëëkɛ pul mi thieek kɛ gua̱a̱th la̱k ɣɔ̱ɔ̱k. Kamdiɛn kɛnɛ thuc mi te raar cɛ do̱o̱n. Ci luth ɛmɔ dël thi̱n. Cuɔ jɔw liŋ ɛ bat wee, "Ɣub!"Cuɔ dhɔŋ ni ɣöö ɛ ruathda mi yiek ni jɛn, duŋdɛ ɣöö ɛ jɔw luɔ̱ɔ̱th. "Ɣub!" ɛ nyɔk. Cuɔ wee, "Nyaŋgari! Ɛ jɔw luɔ̱ɔ̱th mi del piny!"
entries.english_sentence: There is a pool next to the pasture. I heard a sound coming from the pool. "Hub!"At first, I thought it was one of our calves burping!"Hub!" I heard it again, coming from the mud. "Wow! What a sound! Could it be a lungfish?" I wondered.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɔ jɛ nyɔk kɛ käm tiit. Gua̱a̱r tëë juupä waŋdɛ thaar thëëp. Cuɔ gua̱a̱r nɛn ri̱i̱ŋ. Cuɛ ɣä thiec i̱, "Kä tɛ lotdä in mith ɛ jɔw luɔ̱ɔ̱th?" Cuɔ wee, "Mɔn!"Cu gua̱a̱r jɛ caar a /cɛ jɛ jek. Cuɛ kuɔm kä cuɛ wee i̱, "/Ciɛ kui̱c ɛn luth la ɣubɛ kä locɛ biɛt?" Cuɔkɔ li̱ep kä /kerɛ met ɣuup ɛ tɛk.
entries.english_sentence: My father had also heard the sound. He ran over to me."Where did that sound come from?" he asked. My father looked around but did not find the fish.He complained, "Lungfishes can 'hub' and then go silent again."We waited, but the fish did not 'hub'.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ nyaŋthiaŋ, cuɔkɔ ɣɔ̱kɔ yiëël ciëŋrɛy.Cuɔ ɣɔ̱kɔ yian, yaŋɔ kɛ depdɛ, tuutdɔ kɛ depdɛ, jiɛthɔ kɛ ŋuäkɔ, cukɔ kɛ lo̱cdɛ.Gua̱a̱r tëë to̱ŋ gɔali.
entries.english_sentence: At dusk we returned home with our cattle.I tied up each cow, bull, and ox with rope. I knotted the rope around the pole.My father lit the dung fire in the fireplace.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci ɣɔw baak, cuɔkɔ ɣɔ̱k naŋ laak. Cu gua̱a̱r jɔkdɛ cat thaar thëëpdɛ. Cuɔ ɣɔ̱k la liacä lɛɛr.Kɛ jɛn cäŋ ɛmɔ, cuɔ tuɔk ba̱a̱r kɛɛl kɛ rɔɔdä. "Bä dhil kɛ näk ɛn luth indaan. /Cɛ jɛ bi met put ɛn wa̱lɛ," ŋɛ̈rä kɛ lɔcdä.
entries.english_sentence: In the morning, we took our cattle to graze again. My father relaxed while I looked after the cattle.That day, I took a bowl with me. "I am sending this lungfish's spirit to heaven today!" I said to myself.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ja̱ lä ɛ cärcär. Cuɔ tuɔk indaan yɔ̱t."Ɣub! Ɣub!" cuɛ wak. Cuɔ mua̱c, "Lapdho̱r-mi-cɔ̱tbɛ̱̈ɛ̱̈! Cɛ jɔɔc!"Cuɔ jɛ liac thar thuɔ̱ɔ̱c mi te cueecdä kä cɔalä gua̱a̱r. Cuɔ jɛ yiɛth. Cuɛ bithdä töl taŋ. Cu gua̱a̱r ri̱i̱ŋ kɛ bithdɛ. Cuɛ jɛ yiɛth kä cu luth li̱w.
entries.english_sentence: Walking around, I hit the bowl I was carrying. It made a sound like the lungfish."Hub!" said the lungfish in the mud. I called to my father, "It is here!"I threw my spear into the mud, but it broke. My father ran over quickly and speared the fish.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɔkɔ jɛ guëëth raar ɛ dhɔ̱w. Cu lɔc gua̱a̱r tɛɛth kɛ ɣöö cɛ duɔɔth in la go̱o̱rɛ jek. Cuɔkɔ wä cäŋ. Cuɛ cua jɛn cäŋ tɛthä lɔaac cieŋda.Cu gua̱a̱r cuɔ̱ɔ̱l luɔ̱ɔ̱th guëëth raar kä cuɛ jɛ ka̱m dɔw jio̱kda. Cuɔkɔ käpdɛ cam kɔnɛ dämaar min ca bul rɛy tɔŋä.Cu gua̱a̱r ɣä ku nhɔk ɛ yum.
entries.english_sentence: My father carefully removed the lungfish from its hole in the mud. We went home and roasted it on the fire.My father enjoyed the meat, while my younger brother and I ate the tail. Our dog got the fish's colon.It was a happy day for our family.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan tëëkɛ wut mi gɔaa mi ŋäc ŋɔak ɛlɔ̱ŋ. Cɔal ciötdɛ i̱ Mayian. Tëëkɛ thäk mi ke̱r. Thäk cio̱tdädɛ ɛ Mayiankertuut. Mayiankertuut tëëkɛ gɔl mi di̱i̱t kä tëëkɛ ɣɔ̱k ti ŋuan bä.
entries.english_sentence: There once lived a noble wiseman. His name was Mayian.He had a favourite black and white ox. His ox-name was Mayiankertuut.He had a big family and many cattle too.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Tëëkɛ lëët ti ci jiɛɛn ro̱o̱liɛn, kä cukɛ ben Ro̱o̱lnath kɛ gör kä mi camkɛ. Wutlɛ̈t kɛl jälɛ kɛ ciekdɛ mi paydap, kä ci buɔth kɛ näk kɛ ɣöö thilɛ mi̱eth mi camkɛ.
entries.english_sentence: At that time, a family of ogres came to Nuerland looking for food.The ogre's wife was breastfeeding their twin babies.The ogres were starving because they had nothing to eat.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Ci Mayiankertuut ɣɔ̱ɔ̱kɛ luɔny laak. Mëë ci lëët ɣɔ̱k nɛn, cukɛ kɛ joc, kä cukɛ thäk Mayiankertuut mi ke̱r käp. Cua liŋ ni go̱lo̱ŋ lo̱thädɛ ni wi̱c, mëë ca yuɔr piny, kä cuɔ cam.
entries.english_sentence: Mayian had untied his cattle for grazing.When the ogres saw the cattle, they chased them, and caught Mayian's black and white ox.Its ox-bell was heard ringing from far away. The ogres killed the ox and began eating it.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu ŋuɛ̈tni ri̱i̱ŋ kɛ wuɔ̱ɔ̱r mi di̱i̱t. Riŋkɛ guäth in ca thäk cam thi̱n. Cukɛ wutlɛ̈t kɛnɛ ciekdɛ min paydap nɛn ɛ tekɛ mi̱th tha̱a̱k. Cukɛ lëët yiath kä görkɛ näkdiɛn. Cu Mayiankertuut cop kɛ pɛ̈th, jälɛ kɛ ko̱t kɛnɛ wëthdɛ mi di̱i̱t.
entries.english_sentence: Young people from the village came sprinting to get the cattle.They saw the ogres eating the ox. They threw spears at the ogres and tried to kill them.Mayiankertuut arrived. He was holding a shield and weapons.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ rɔɔdɛ ka̱m mua̱a̱l, kä cuɛ mutdɛ guath kä mua̱a̱yɛ. Cuɛ cieklɛ̈t mi ci dap kɛ cuɛ̈ɛ̈k dhɔɔli da̱ŋ rɛw nɛn. Cu Mayiankertuut ŋuɛ̈tni ka̱p cuɔ̱ŋ, kä cuɛ wutlɛ̈t kɛnɛ mangɔaalɛ pën näk. Cuɛ ŋuɛ̈tni jiök, "Pa̱lɛ kɛ! Ɛ kɛ camkɛ thääkdä, ɛ buɔth dapä. Wutni, bär ni ciaŋ."
entries.english_sentence: Mayiankertuut knelt and saw the mother ogre breastfeeding her twins.He stopped the youths from killing them.He said, "Leave them, let them eat my ox. It's the hunger of a breastfeeding mother! The better life is ahead of us."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu ŋuɛ̈tni lui̱k Mayiankertuut liŋ. Cu Mayiankertuut kɛ jiök, "Wuɔcɛ löthdɛ kɛnɛ dhuɔɔrkɛ. Naŋɛ kɛ wi̱c. Pa̱lɛ ri̱i̱ŋdɛ, ɛ camkɛ ɛ kɛn." Cu lëët lo̱ckiɛn tɛɛth ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ min ca la̱t ɛ Mayiankertuut.
entries.english_sentence: The youths heard the advice of Mayiankertuut. He told them, "Collect the ox-bell and tassels. Take them to the cattle camp. Leave the meat for the ogres to eat."The ogres were joyful because of what Mayian had done.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ kɔr runi, cu Mayiankertuut kɛnɛ wutni da̱ŋ dhieec wä ja̱l. Wäkɛ gör kɛ miy ro̱o̱l mi na̱n. Mëë cikɛ cop ro̱o̱l ɛmɔ, cu nhiaal mi di̱i̱t dɛ̈m, kä cukɛ wä caak luaak.
entries.english_sentence: After some years, Mayian and five men travelled to a far away land, in search of giraffes.As they arrived, it started raining heavily. They ran to a cattle byre and slept there.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn luak ɛmɔ ɛ luak lɛ̈t. Cukɛ niɛɛn thi̱n. Cu lɛt min mɔ gua̱n luaak jiɛɛn kɛ wäär, wëë lëët tin kɔ̱ŋ wä la̱rlär. Cuɛ kɛ jiök, "Tëëkɛ wutni da̱ŋ bäkɛl ti ci Kuoth kɛ nöŋ kɔn, bia, banɛ kɛ ben puur ni kaakdä."
entries.english_sentence: That cattle byre belonged to an ogre!The ogre left that night to inform the other ogres.He told them, "In my byre, there are six men whom God brought to us. Come and cultivate my field. Afterward, we will eat them."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu lëët lunh kɛ runwaŋ. Cukɛ thääk dha̱a̱ri tha̱t ti di̱t, ti ci thia̱ŋ kɛ pi̱ lɔap maac, ti dëë ben ciithni naath. Kɛ kɔrɛ dëëkɛ cu cam. Kä rɛy lëëtni tëë ci ben, lɛt kɛl rɛydiɛn ɛ jɛn lɛt ëë caam thäk Mayiankertuut. Jɛn ca kɔŋ kän kɛnɛ gaatkɛ ɛ Mayiankertuut.
entries.english_sentence: The ogres arrived very early in the morning.They filled big bowls with boiling water, preparing to eat the men.Among the ogres who came, was the one who ate Mayian's ox. Mayian saved him and his family long ago.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ cunh rɛy luaak lɛ̈t min puɔ̱rkɛ kaakdɛ. Ɛ ŋot keekɛ ni puur, cuɛ Mayiankertuut ŋic. Cuɛ wee, "Ɣa̱la̱! Ɛ ji̱n Mayiankertuut?" Cu Mayiankertuut ɛ loc, "Ne̱rɔ dheeŋ!"
entries.english_sentence: The ogre who Mayian had saved entered the cattle byre of the owner of the field.He recognised Mayiankertuut and exclaimed, "Are you Mayiankertuut?""Yes, I am!" replied Mayian.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: "Ɣɔ̱ɔ̱n! Ɛn ram min cɔalkɛ ni kɔ ɛn ɣöö ba ben puur ni kak, ɛ ji̱n Mayiankertuut?" cuɛ thiec ɛ dɔlɛ to̱k."Juää!" cu Mayiankertuut ɛ loc. "Mayiankertuut bër raar! Kɛ yɛn da̱ŋdi?" cuɛ jɛ thiec. "Kɛ kɔn da̱ŋ bäkɛl," cu Mayiankertuut ɛ loc. Cu lɛt ɛmɔ lëët thiec, "Tëëkɛ ram mi kui̱c cuɛ̈ɛ̈kä tin kɔn?" Cu wutlɛ̈t in puɔ̱rkɛ kaakdɛ ɛ loc, "Ɣëc, thilɛ ram mi kui̱ckɛ."
entries.english_sentence: "So, you are the one we were told to eat after cultivating the field," the ogre smiled.The ogre asked the other ogres, "Is there anyone who doesn't know my twins?""No, there is none," said the owner of the field.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu wutlɛ̈t lëët la̱t cäät, kä latdɛ jɛ, "Wut ɛmɛ mëëdan cakɔ thääkdɛ mi nhɔkɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ cam kɔnɛ ciekdä. Mëë ci ŋuɛ̈tni wecdiɛn ri̱i̱ŋ kɛ ɣöö bakɔ ben näk, cuɛ kɔ gaŋ. Duŋ mi thil ni jɛn, ɣän kɔnɛ ciekdä kɛ cuɛ̈ɛ̈kä tin kɔn /cakɔ dee tëk."
entries.english_sentence: The ogre narrated his story, "Long ago, my wife and I ate the favourite ox of this man. When the youths of his village came to kill us, he protected us.Without the help of this man, my twins, my wife, and I, would be dead."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu lɛt Mayiankertuut kɛnɛ dämani ka̱m raar rɛy luaak. Cuɛ kɛ naŋ ni cieeŋdɛ. Mëë cikɛ cop cieeŋdɛ, cukɛ kɛ moc kɛ kuan kɛ took kɛ tuɔ̱ŋ ti /ka̱n me̱t cam.
entries.english_sentence: The ogres freed Mayian and the other five men.The ogre who Mayian had saved invited them to his home.The men were served food on new plates and given spoons which had never been used before.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Cukɛ niɛɛn kɛ muɔŋ kɛɛl kɛ lëët. Cu wutlɛ̈t kɛ thiec, "Kä kɛ ŋuuni kɛn tin bia ben go̱r Ro̱o̱lëëtni?" Cukɛ wee, "Kɔn bakɔ ben go̱r ni miy. Kɛn miy kɛ nyin wutdä. La̱thkɛ kɛ ŋuääk kɛnɛ tet."
entries.english_sentence: The men and the ogres spent the night chatting.The ogre asked them, "What brought you to Ogreland?"They replied, "We came looking for giraffe tails. We use them to make necklaces and bracelets.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ruɔ̱ndɛ, cu wutlɛ̈t kɛnɛ gaatkɛ wä kak kɛ guëc. Cukɛ miy ti ŋuan nöŋ Mayiankertuut kɛnɛ mäthnikɛ. Mëë ci gua̱a̱th ben, cu Mayiankertuut wutlɛ̈t jiök, "Kɔn bakɔ loc Ro̱o̱lnath." Ɛn wutlɛ̈t kɛnɛ gaatkɛ cukɛ Mayiankertuut nam kɛnɛ mäthnikɛ, ɛ cukɛ cop ni Ro̱o̱lnath kɛ mal.
entries.english_sentence: Early in the morning, the ogre and his children went hunting for giraffes. They brought many giraffe tails to Mayiankertuut and his friends.When Mayian was ready to leave, the ogre and his children accompanied them to Nuerland.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title_english: A better life is ahead of us
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë cikɛ cop, cukɛ ciaŋ mi gɔaa mëë ca wä cieeŋnikɛ ɛ lëët wä la̱r naath. Kɛn lëët tëë ci Mayiankertuut kɛ gaŋ mëë ca thääkdɛ cam, kɛ kɛn tin tëë ca Mayiankertuut kɛnɛ mäthnikɛ kän. Ɛ jɛn, ci riet Mayiankertuut mëë laarɛ ben ɛla thuɔ̱k. Ɛn ɣöö, "Bär ni ciaŋ." Cɛ duɔth ɛla ka̱a̱ŋ mi larkɛ ɛ naath ɛn ɣöö ci Mayian wee, "Bär ni ciaŋ."
entries.english_sentence: When they arrived home, they told everyone about the hospitality of the ogres. These were the same ogres that Mayiankertuut protected long ago, which saved Mayian and his friends today.Always remember, a better life is ahead of us. That is to say, 'What goes around, comes around.'
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan tëëkɛ ji̱ dhɔaar ti cieŋ wi̱c mi na̱n kɛ rɛk. Kä wec ɛmɔ tëëkɛ rup mi tekɛ ley.Tëëkɛ dho̱l mi cɔal i̱ Dɛŋ kɛnɛ nyiman mi cɔal i̱ Nyakuiy. Cieŋkɛ kɛɛl kɛ mandiɛn.Ca kɛ ŋi̱eec kɛ ɣöö bi kɛn a gaat ti gɔw ti cieŋ kɛ tɛ̈th lɔaac.
entries.english_sentence: Once upon a time, there lived a family in a village far from the city. The village was surrounded by a forest with many animals.A boy called Deng and his sister Nyekuiy lived in the village with their mother.They were taught how to be good children, and how to live happily.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Dɛŋ la ŋarɛ rɛy ɣɔ̱ɔ̱ kiɛn kä ŋäcɛ nyiön deet.Kä cuɛ ka̱k leyni ŋa̱c bä, kä la wëë mac yieer kɛ kuɛt.Kɛ cäŋ kɛl cuɛ bath. Kä cu man diɛɛr kɛ gua̱a̱th in cɛ wä thi̱nɔ. Cua go̱ r gua̱thni ti ŋuan kä /ka̱ n jɛ jek.
