entries.english_sentence: Deng played near their cow yards and learned to milk goats.He learned to hunt animals, and to fish in the river to catch turtles.One day, Deng's mother could not find him anywhere. She was worried. The family looked for him everywhere but did not find him.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ jɔɔc kɛ thiaŋ, jälɛ kɛ wi̱c thiel. Cu man ɛ thiec i̱, "Ci wä nikä kä ɛŋu rɔmi mɔ?"Cuɛ jɛ loc i̱, "Ci nɛy wä kak kɔnɛ dhɔɔl."Kä man diɛɛrɛ kɛ ɣöö ka̱k leyni dɔaar bɛcɛ. Cuɛ jiök i̱, "/Cu rɔ nyɔk kɛ wä kak rɛy ruɔ̱ɔ̱p."
entries.english_sentence: Deng finally came home that night. He was carrying an antelope's head. His mother asked him, "Where have you been? What are you carrying?""I went hunting wild animals with the village boys," replied Deng. His mother was concerned because hunting wild animals can be dangerous. "Don't hunt in the forest again," she told Deng.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä /kenɛ ruac man liŋ. La rɔɔdɛ a kualɛ ruup ɛ nyɔk. Cu man rɔ moc kɛ kɛɛt i̱ duäcɛ jɛ kɛ ɣöö /cɛ lui̱k liŋ. Mëë cɛ kɛɛt nɛn tetdä man, cuɛ rɔ bar. Cuɛ rɔ wä tɔ̱w wi̱c jiaath. Cu man ɛ go̱r kä /kenɛ gua̱a̱thdɛ jek.Cu Nyakuiy jɛ cɔl kä cuɛ jɛ jiök i̱, "Deŋ, Mama thiɛlɛ jɛ, ku ben piny ban ben mi̱th kɛ kuän." Cuɛ ben piny.
entries.english_sentence: His mother took a stick to beat him for not listening to her. Deng saw the stick and ran. He hid up a tree and his mother could not find him.Nyekuiy called to her brother, "Deng, Mama isn't around, come home and eat with me!" The boy came down to eat.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu man jɛ nɛn kä cuɛ jɛ jiök i̱, "Thukni kɛ mi̱eth bi kɔn tekɛ ruac."Mëë ci kɛ thuɔ̱k kɛ mi̱eth, cu riŋ ni jɛn guäth ŋarä kä cuɛ jɛ wä rɛ̈t käk ɛ nyɔk.Cuɛ man wi̱cdɛ gäy kɛ ciaaŋdɛ. Kä cuɛ jɛ go̱r i̱ bɛ jɛ naŋ rɛɛk duelgɔ̱rä. Cuɛ ca̱r kɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p in dee gatdɛ ruac ɛmɔ liŋ kɛ jɛ kɛ kui̱c kä ɣöö derɛ nhɔk.
entries.english_sentence: "Deng, I want to talk to you after your meal," said his mother.But after eating, Deng ran out to play and then went hunting again.His mother was concerned about his behaviour. "He should go to school in the city. How can I explain this to Deng so that he accepts the idea?" she wondered.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ wargak gɔ̱a̱r däman ni Bidiit mi cieŋ rɛɛk. Kɛ kɔr gua̱th cu Bidiit wargak ɛ mɔ loc. Larɛ jɛ i̱ bɛ ben ja̱l wi̱c.Cu Dɛŋ kɛnɛ Nyakuiy lo̱ckiɛn tɛɛth kɛ ɣöö bikɛ ben jëk kɛ nääriɛn min bëë rɛɛk.Kä kɛ kɔr path cu nääriɛn cop.
entries.english_sentence: Mother wrote a letter to her brother, Bidiit, in the city. After some time, she received a letter in return from Bidiit. He told her that he was coming to visit them in the village.The children were excited to meet their uncle from the city.Bidiit arrived one month later.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu mandiɛn kɛ jiök i̱, "Gaatkä, ci näärun ben."Cu Nyakuiy wee i̱, "Can wä jëk kɛ nääran, Dɛŋ." Kä cua to̱k dɔl ɛ kɛn kä cukɛ riŋ kut nääriɛn ni Bidiit.Cu nääriɛn ni Bidiit kɛ jiök i̱, "Kɛ yɛn gaat ti gɔw." Cu mandiɛn ɛ lar i̱, "Diɛwä jɛ bɛ la tɛ̈th lɔaac i̱ bia wä cieŋ rɛɛk kɛ näärun kɛɛl."
entries.english_sentence: "My children, your uncle has arrived," said mother."Let's meet our uncle," Nyekuiy told Deng. They both laughed as they ran towards Bidiit."You are beautiful children," said Uncle Bidiit. "I think that you will be happy living in the city with your uncle!" said mother to her children.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Bidiit kɛ jiök i̱, "Bä yɛ naŋ rɛɛk kä bia wä gɔ̱a̱r."Kɛ kɔr päthni da̱ŋ ŋuaan bi babuur ben kä bä yɛ kööt rɛydɛ."Mi wia wä cop rɛɛk, bä yɛ kök jio̱o̱kthiɛliɛkni bä."
entries.english_sentence: "I will take you to the city and you can go to school," said Uncle Bidiit.He continued, "In a few months' time, there is a ship coming up the river past the village. I will buy tickets for you."He added, "When you come to the city, I will buy bicycles for you!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu gaat lo̱ckiɛn tɛɛth ɛ bi tɛ̈th lɔaac kɛ dee pën mi̱eth kɛ cäŋ ɛmɔ.Kɛ kɔr juɔkni da̱ŋ rɛw cu Bidiit ni̱n lɔŋädɛ thuuk. Kä cuɛ loc rɛɛk.Kɛ kɔr päthni da̱ŋ ŋuaan cu babuur ben loorɛ Nyakuiy kɛnɛ Dɛŋ. Cu mandiɛn kɛ la̱th rɛy babuurä kä cukɛ rɔ nër mal.
entries.english_sentence: The children were so happy that they couldn't eat that day.Two weeks later, Uncle Bidiit's holiday was over, and he returned to the city.After four months, the ship finally arrived to take Nyekuiy and Deng to the city. Their mother put them on the ship and waved goodbye.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu babuur gaat ja̱a̱l kɛ nin bärɔw kɛ rɛy yiëër.A wä babuur kɛ wä, Dɛŋ kɛnɛ Nyakuiy guɛckɛ juaac riŋkɛ.Cu kɛn tekɛ tɛ̈th lɔaac kɛ ɣöö wäkɛ duelgɔ̱rä.Cu kɛnɛ go̱o̱ri̱ bikɛ gɔ̱r ni ŋuɔt kiɛ ki̱i̱m duëlwal.
entries.english_sentence: The ship carried the children on a seven-day journey along the river.Deng and Nyekuiy watched the wind in the grass as the ship moved through the water.They were joyful that they were going to school. They dreamed of one day studying law or medical science.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci babuur cop rɛɛk, cukɛ nääriɛn jek lipädiɛn thok waath babuuri.Cu Dɛŋ dɛy jiɛɛn ka̱m raar kä kämɛ kɛ gaat näärɛ. Cukɛ thiec kɛ duɔɔth i̱, "Kɛ ŋuuni?"Cu Dɛŋ kɛ loc i̱, "Kɛ dɛy jiɛɛn rɛy cieŋ. Comkɛ."
entries.english_sentence: When the ship arrived in the city, Uncle Bidiit was at the dock waiting for the children.Deng took out some fruits and gave them to his uncle's children as they met. They asked with smiles, "What is this fruit?"Deng replied, "They are village fruits, very sweet!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Bi näära kɔ naŋ rɛɛk kɛ babuur
entries.book_title_english: Our uncle will take us to the city by ship
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Nyakuiy kɛnɛ Dɛŋ cieŋ rɛɛk kɛ nääriɛn kɛɛl kɛ run.Cukɛ lät ɛ bum duelgɔ̱rädiɛn amäni mëë cikɛ thuɔ̱k kɛ gɔ̱a̱r.Mëë cikɛ rɔ jek lät, cu kɛn mandiɛn luäk.
entries.english_sentence: Nyekuiy and Deng lived in the city with their Uncle Bidiit for many years.They worked hard at school and went to study at university.When they got jobs, they supported their mother.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan tëëkɛ wut mi cɔal i̱ Macoc. Cɛ wä rɛy ruɔ̱ɔ̱p, ɛ jɛn i̱ wëë jɔp kɛ jiɛn ti lätdɛ luaakdɛ.Mëë wëëkɛ, cuɛ pöör ram mi ci li̱w ni wal wä jek.
entries.english_sentence: Once there was a man named Macoc who went to the forest to cut wood. He was building a byre to keep his cattle in.While he was in the forest, he came across the skull of a person who must have died a long time ago.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu Macoc pöör indaan kuɛt kɛ cio̱o̱kdɛ kä cuɛ wee i̱, "Ji̱n pöör ɛmɛ, ci ji̱ ku näk niɛ lɛpdu ɛ lual ɔ."Kä cu pöör indaan jɛ jiök i̱, "Amäni ji̱n bä, bi ji̱ lɛ näk niɛ lɛpdu ɛ lual ɔ bä."Kä cu Macoc ga̱a̱c, kä cuɛ dual ɛlɔ̱ŋ, kä cuɛ jɛ ŋɔac wi̱c kɛ pɛ̈th mi di̱i̱t ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛlɔ̱ŋ.
entries.english_sentence: Macoc kicked the skull and said to it, "You, is it not your tongue that killed you?"The skull responded to Macoc, "You will be killed by your tongue too!"Macoc got a fright and ran back to the village.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cuɛ cop cieŋ a lathɛ jɛ. Kä cuɛ thiec i̱, "Macoc ɛŋu ci tuɔɔk kä ji̱ mɔ?"Cuɛ wee i̱, "Tëëkɛ mi di̱i̱t mi ci tuɔɔk min cä wä rɛy ruɔ̱ɔ̱p. Ɣän cä wa̱ jɔp kɛ jiɛn ti la̱tdä ni luaakdä, cua pöör ram mi ci li̱w wä jek piny, kä mëë cä jɛ kuɛt kɛ cio̱o̱kdä, kä jiökä jɛ i̱, 'Ji̱n pöör ɛmɛ, ci ji̱ näk niɛ lɛpdu ɛ lual ɛmɔ?' "
entries.english_sentence: He was shaking with fear when he arrived. The villagers asked Macoc what had happened.He replied, "Something strange happened to me in the forest. I came across a dry skull. I kicked the skull, saying, 'You, is it not your tongue that killed you?'"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cuɛ ɣä jiök i̱, "Amäni ji̱n bä, bi ji̱ näk niɛ lɛpdu ɛ lual ɛmɔ bä. Kä cua rɔ cu bar kä ri̱eeŋä ni cieŋ, kɛ ɣöö bä min ci tuɔɔk ben la̱r naath."
entries.english_sentence: Macoc continued, "And the skull replied, 'You will be killed by your tongue too!'When this happened to me in the forest, I was very frightened. I had to come home without cutting the wood for which I went."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ca ruac ɛmɔ liŋ ɛ naath, cukɛ gääc ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛlɔ̱ŋ. Kɛ ɣöö thilɛ pöör mi ci li̱w, mi dee ruac.
entries.english_sentence: Macoc's revelation shocked everybody because no one could believe what he said.But he insisted that the story was true.Macoc said, "If you people do not believe me, I am ready to accompany you to the forest where I found the dry skull."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu naath wee i̱, "Wut ɛmɛ cɔal i̱ Macoc ɔ, jɛn tekɛ kac mi diit ɛlɔ̱ŋ."Kä cu Macoc naath jiök i̱, "Ɛ puc, ɛ puc. Nɔmɔ cɛ tuɔɔk."
entries.english_sentence: After a long argument, people advised Macoc to tell his story to the village chief.They all went to the chief together.When Macoc arrived at the house of the chief, he was asked to repeat his story, and he did.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ wee i̱, "Mi ɛ yɛn i̱ kacä jɛ, ɣän bä yɛ naŋ guäth in tëë thi̱n."Kä cua jiök i̱, "Ji̱n wër lätni ruac ɛmɔ kuäär wec."
entries.english_sentence: The chief called for more people to come to listen to Macoc's strange story.When these people came, Macoc was asked to repeat what he had said to the others.When these people heard Macoc's story, they too were shocked.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu kuäär wec indaan Macoc jiök i̱, "Ji̱n bi naath naŋ guäthdɛ ɛn pöör ɛ ruac ɔ."Kä cuɛ Macoc jiök i̱, "Kä mi wä ruacdu nɔmɔ wä la kac ɛŋu mi ba lät kä ji̱?"
entries.english_sentence: As a result, the chief asked Macoc to accompany the people to the forest where he claimed he saw the talking skull.The chief asked Macoc, "If your story turns out to be a lie, what should the people do to you?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Macoc wee i̱, "Yɛn bia ɣän näk!"Cu nɛy diaal mat kä ɣöö ba Macoc näk mi /ken pöör ruac.
entries.english_sentence: Macoc replied, "Let them kill me if I am lying!"So, the chief sent the people off to the forest together with Macoc.They agreed that if the skull did not talk, the people would kill Macoc.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci naath cop rɛy ruɔ̱ɔ̱p kɛ Macoc kɛɛl, cuɛ pöör indaan wä jek ɛ thuɔ̱k.Cu Macoc ɛ kuɛt kɛ cio̱kdɛ kä jio̱kɛ jɛ i̱, "Ji̱n pöör ɛmɛ, cu ji̱ ku näk niɛ lɛpdu ɛ lual ɛmɔ?" Cu pöör indaan biɛt ɛ lik.Cu Macoc jɛ nyɔk kɛ kuɛt kä cuɛ wee i̱, "Ji̱n pöör ɛmɛ, ci ji̱ näk niɛ lɛpdu?" Kä cu pöör indaan biɛt ɛ lik.
entries.english_sentence: The people arrived in the forest, and Macoc found the dry skull.He kicked the skull saying, "You, is it not your tongue that killed you?"But the skull was silent.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Macoc pöör kuɛt nikä diɔ̱ɔ̱k, ŋotdɛ thilɛ mi ci pöör ɛ loc.Kɛ kɔrɛ cu naath wee, "Wut ɛmɛ ɛ gua̱n kacä, cɛ kɔn kaŋ amäni kuäär wec. Banɛ jɛ näk kɛ ɣöö thilɛ ram mi dɔ̱ŋ mi bi kac mi di̱i̱t mi ce̱tkɛ mɛmɛ nyɔk kɛ ka̱c."Cua Macoc cu näk.
entries.english_sentence: Macoc kicked the skull again, and again.The skull did not say a word. The people became very angry with Macoc because he had lied to them and to the chief.They killed Macoc in the forest.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ca Macoc näk, cu pöör indan ɛ jiök i̱, "Ɣän /ka̱ nɛ la̱t ji̱ i̱ amäni ji̱n bä bi ji̱ näk niɛ lɛpdu ɛ lual ɛmɔ."Kä min ci naath ruac ɛmɔ liŋ, cukɛ ga̱a̱c ɛlɔ̱ŋ kɛ ɣöö ca Macoc näk baaŋ.
entries.english_sentence: After Macoc was dead, the skull said to him, "Didn't I tell you that you too would be killed by that tongue of yours?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan tekɛ wutni da̱ŋ rɛw ti thieek dho̱o̱rkiɛn. Wut kɛl tëëkɛ yaŋ, kä wut ɛ dɔ̱diɛn thiɛlɛ yaŋ.Kɛ ruɔ̱n kɛl, cu ɣɔw tekɛ buɔth mi di̱i̱t, kä ŋot bɛl ɛ /kenkɛ ni ciɛk. Kɛ jɛn gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ, ci mi̱th diaal thuɔ̱k, ci duɔ̱th ni ɣɔ̱k.
entries.english_sentence: Once upon a time, there were two men who were neighbours. One man had a cow and the other had none.That year, a great famine hit the entire village. The harvest wasn't yet ripe for picking. There was nothing to eat. People were left with just their cows.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci buɔth di̱t, cu wut in tekɛ yaŋ yaaŋdɛ näk kɛ ɣöö bi ji̱ gɔaalɛ jɛ cam. Kä /kenɛ gua̱n thieekädɛ min thiɛl yaŋ moc kɛnɛ ji̱ gɔaalɛ.Cu wut in ca dak wä guäth in ci wut ɛmɔ yaaŋdɛ jiaŋ thi̱n, "Cuɛ waw yaaŋ in ca yiäk wä jek. Kä cuɛ wä naŋ, cua wä cam kɛnɛ ji̱ gɔaalɛ. Cukɛ tëk kɛ waw ɛmɔ amäni mëë ci bɛlkiɛn ciɛk."
entries.english_sentence: When famine struck, the man who had a cow decided to slaughter it for his family to eat. He didn't offer any of the meat to his neighbour.His neighbour decided to look around the place where the cow had been slaughtered. He found the remains of the cow's chyme and ate it with his family. They survived until the harvest was ready.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci bɛl ciɛk, cu wut ëë thiɛl yaŋ kaakdɛ ciɛk kɛ bɛl ti ŋuan, kä /ken kak wutdä mëë tekɛ yaŋ ciɛk.Mëë ca bɛl ŋɛr, cu wut ëë thiɛl yaŋ tekɛ jiöŋni da̱ŋ diɔ̱k, kä cu wut ëë tekɛ yaŋ thiɛl jio̱ŋ. Cuɛ wut in tekɛ bɛl lëp luk kä makämɛ. Cua luk gua̱thni ti ŋuan, kä nyaanɛ naath amäni mëë cikɛ ben kä kuäär ɛmɛ.
entries.english_sentence: When the harvest was ready, the man without a cow had a surplus harvest, but the other man had nothing.The man who had killed his cow decided to take the man who had a surplus to court. They went through many courts and couldn't find a solution, until they came before a judge at the highest court.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu wutni da̱ŋ rɛw tɔ̱tɔ̱ nyuur nhiam kua̱r. Cu kuäär kɛ thiec kɛ ɣöö bikɛ min bee kɛ kɛ wi̱c makämɛkä kuɛɛn.Cu wut in gɔɔny raan kɛ luk ɛ tuok, "Wal ruel mëë te ɣɔw kɛ buɔth, wut ɛmɛ thilɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱r. Cikɛ dee li̱w kɛnɛ ji̱ gɔaalɛ kɛ buɔth. Mëë cä yaaŋdä näk, cuɛ wawdɛ wä naŋ. Cua wä cam kɛnɛ ji̱ gɔaalɛ. Mi thiɛl ni yaaŋdä dee kɛ li̱w kɛ buɔth kɛnɛ ji̱ gɔaalɛ."
entries.english_sentence: The judge asked each man to present his case before the court.The man who had killed his cow started, "During the famine, this man had nothing. His family were starving. When I killed my cow, he took the chyme from the carcass for his family to eat. If it wasn't for me, his family would have died of hunger."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu wut ɛmɔ jɛ ŋok, "Ɣän göörä ɣöö bɛ waw yaaŋdä col. Bi nɛy bɛlkɛ da̱a̱k kɔnɛ jɛ."Cu kuäär wut in dɔ̱ŋ thiec kɛ ɣöö bɛ cuɔ̱ɔ̱ŋdɛ kuɛn. Cu wut ɛmɔ jɛ lar i̱, "Ɛ thuɔ̱k, cä waw yaaŋ wutdä nɛmɛ naŋ ɛ puc, duŋdɛ ɣöö wä kuany ni mi cɛ yiäk."
entries.english_sentence: The man concluded, "I want reparations so that my family and I can have a share of the grain from his abundant harvest."The judge asked the other man to make his statement. The man said, "It's true, I took the cow's chyme, but only after my neighbour had discarded it."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kuäär ji̱ makämɛkä moc kɛ rieet kɛ ɣöö ba ram in tekɛ cuɔ̱ɔ̱ŋ lar.Cukɛ guɛ̈l. Cu tha̱a̱ŋ nath jɛ lar ɛn ɣöö derɛ cuɔ̱ɔ̱ŋ wutdä min ca waw yaaŋdɛ cam, kɛ ɣöö mi thiɛl ni yaaŋdɛ, dëë wut ɛmɔ kɛnɛ ji̱ gɔaalɛ yɔ̱c ɛ buɔth. Cu tha̱a̱ŋ nath wee i̱, "Derɛ cuɔ̱ɔ̱ŋ wutdä min ci waw yaaŋ ran cam, kɛ ɣöö wä kuany ni mi ca yiäk. Lo̱kɛ ni ɣöö dee kɛ li̱w."
entries.english_sentence: The judge invited the jury to speak about who they believed had a right to reparations.Some thought the first man had a right. If it weren't for his cow, the other man's family would have died.Others thought the second man had a right. Nobody normally eats chyme. He did it to survive.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cuɛ kuäär wi̱cdɛ gäy kɛ min derɛ lat. Kɛn wutni da̱ŋ rɛw diaal tekɛ kɛ cuŋ gua̱thnikiɛn.Cu kuäär wee, "Ba kap jɔk ɛn luk ɛmɛ, ba lɛ nyɔk kɛ guec iruun."Kä /ken kuäär ɛ ŋa̱c ɛn ɣöö te gaat kɛ cuŋä jɔɔk luɔ̱k makämɛkä liɛŋkɛ min lat kɛ.
entries.english_sentence: The judge didn't know what decision to make. Each man was right in his own way.The judge decided to adjourn the court and resume it the next day.The judge didn't know that his children were in the crowd listening to the court case.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ jɛn thiaŋ ɛmɔ, cu kuäär ko̱lɛ nöŋ raar duëël. Cuɛ ben tɔ̱ɔ̱c raar kɛ ɣöö ci duel leeth.Te gaatkɛ ŋarä kutdɛ. Cu gat kɛl gaat tin kɔ̱ŋ jiök i̱ "Canɛ ŋar kɛ luk. Ɛ ɣän kuäär makämɛkä."Cu kuäär ji̱thdɛ pa̱l piny.
entries.english_sentence: That evening, the judge came home very tired. He decided to rest outside in the open air, because it was too hot inside the house.His children were playing close by. He heard one of his sons say, "Let's play a game of court. I'll be the judge!"The judge's ears perked up.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu ram kɛl kä dhɔɔl wee, "Kɛ kɔn wutni tin luk mindan, ɛŋa mɔ deri lar i̱ tekɛ cuɔ̱ɔ̱ŋ?" Te kuäär li̱ŋ.Cu dho̱l in la kuäär makämɛkä jɛ loc, gua̱thnikiɛn diaal tekɛ kɛ cuŋ duŋdɛ ɣöö /ci wut in tekɛ bɛl waw yaaŋ wutdä nɔmɔ bi col kɛ bɛl. Ɛn wut ɛmɔ bɛ lip ni ɣöö ba bɛl wutdä nɔmɔ kɔ̱m bɛ jil bɛɛl kɛ wä naŋ kɛ gua̱a̱th waaw yaaŋdɛ.
entries.english_sentence: One child asked, "Which man from today's hearing would you say had a right?" The judge was listening.The boy playing judge exclaimed, "Both men have a right, but the man with a surplus harvest does not owe the other man any of his grain. The man with the cow should wait for the wheat to be hulled. Then, he can take the husks as payback."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kuäär dhɔɔl jiök i̱, "Kuɛ̈ɛ̈ wä tɔ̱ɔ̱c, ci̱ ɣɔw la wäär." Ci /kenɛ min ca lat ɛ kɛn li̱ŋ.Kɛ runwaŋ cuɛ wutni da̱ŋ rɛw tëë pan cɔal wi̱i̱ makämɛ. Cukɛ lɛni kuën ɛ nyɔk.Cu kuäär ji̱ makämɛkä nyɔk kɛ muɔ̱c kɛ rieet ɛ nyɔk kɛ ɣöö ba gua̱n cuuŋä lɛy, kä cukɛ ŋot kɛ mi guɛ̈l kɛ.
entries.english_sentence: It was getting late, and soon the judge told his children to go to sleep. He pretended that he hadn't heard them playing.The next day, he called the two men back to the court. Both men made their statements a second time. The jury members shared their views again, but they still disagreed about who had a right to reparations.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kuäär rietdɛ ku lar, "Cuɛ wä kɛn wutni da̱ŋ rɛw tekɛ kɛ cuɔ̱ɔ̱ŋ gua̱ thnikiɛn diaal, duŋdɛ ɣöö /ca waw yaaŋ wutdä nɔmɔ bi col kɛ bɛl."Ji̱n wut in tekɛ yaŋ bi lip ni ɣöö ba bɛl wutdä nɛmɔ kɔn kɔ̱m. Bi jil bɛɛlkɛ wä naŋ kɛ gua̱a̱th waaw yaaŋdu."
entries.english_sentence: Finally, the judge made his ruling. He said, "Both men have a right, but the man with three bins full of wheat does not owe the other man any part of his grain.The man who had a cow should wait for the other man's wheat to be hulled, then he can take the husks as payback for the cow's chyme."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu wutni da̱ŋ rɛw tin kɔn ŋɛ̈ɛ̈r, kä cu nɛy diaal mat kɛ min ca lar ɛ kuäär.Cu kuäär kɛ jiök i̱, "Luɔcɛ dho̱rikun kä ɛ lo̱ckun /ci jiäk kamnikun. Ɛn luk cɛ thuɔ̱k ɛn täämɛ. Bia tekɛ mal."
entries.english_sentence: The two men were surprised, but everyone agreed with the judge's resolution.The judge concluded, "Go back to your homes, and stop holding grudges. The case is now resolved. Peace be upon you."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Mäthni ti ci bila ji̱ tɛ̈r
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ gua̱a̱th mi ci wä, tëë kɛ mäthni ti cieŋ kɛɛl, ɛ Yak kɛnɛ Pɛlpɛl.Yak ɛ puur ka̱a̱kni mi di̱i̱t. La kerɛ nikɛ runwaŋ kä bɛ wä lät rɛy kakädɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Once upon a time, there lived two friends, Hyena and Hare.Hyena was a hardworking farmer. He woke up early every morning and went to work in his field.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Mäthni ti ci bila ji̱ tɛ̈r
entries.nuer_sentence: Pɛlpɛl la kerɛ nikɛ cäŋdäär.Jɛn la ŋa̱a̱ mɛ kä ri̱i̱nyɛ rɔɔdɛ. Kɛ kɔrɛ bɛ kulɛ wä gör kua̱n.
entries.english_sentence: Hare woke up when it was already broad daylight.He would yawn and stretch. Then he would go looking for food.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Mäthni ti ci bila ji̱ tɛ̈r
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ runwaŋ ni ciaŋ, la mocɛ rɔɔdɛ kä kuay rɛy tue̱cä kiɛ yiirä Yakä. Kɛ kɔrɛ bɛ wä rɛy kakä kɛ pɛ̈l kacä ce̱tkɛ mi cɛ lät.La dɔpɛ ni mac mi kɛɛlɛ kɛ kuay. Thiɛlɛ mi la luäŋɛ kɛ lätni, ɛ ni kël bɛɛl kärɔadɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Most mornings, Hare would take some seeds from Hyena's granary. Then he went to his field and pretended to work.He would light a fire and roast the seeds. He did nothing, except eat roasted seeds.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Mäthni ti ci bila ji̱ tɛ̈r
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ gua̱th ŋër, Pɛlpɛl la jiɛnɛ kɛ ɣöö bɛ rɔa̱a̱th bɛɛl mäthdɛ wä kual.Jɛn la naŋɛ kɛ rɛy tue̱cdɛ kiɛ yiirɛ.
entries.english_sentence: At harvest time, Hare went and stole his friend's ripe maize.He carried it to his own granary.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Mäthni ti ci bila ji̱ tɛ̈r
entries.nuer_sentence: Yak cuɛ wi̱cdɛ yi̱c kɛ kuël kuaynikɛ.Pɛlpɛl cuɛ loc i̱, "Dɔ̱ŋ kɛ ji̱ thi̱eekädan tɔ kualkɛ bɛlku tɔ. Kɛn tekɛ cucä näk buɔth kɛ ɣöö /ca la̱t luäŋ."
entries.english_sentence: Hyena complained about the stolen crops.Hare answered, "Maybe the neighbours stole your maize. They are suffering from famine because they are lazy."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Mäthni ti ci bila ji̱ tɛ̈r
entries.nuer_sentence: Yak cuɛ jääny caarɛ riɛkdɛ. Cuɛ ben nhial kɛ ca̱r. Cuɛ luaac kuɛth pua̱nyni jiɛɛn.Jɛn cuɛ kak gekdɛ kɛɛliw thiäŋ kɛ luaac ti dɔapdɔaap. Ɛn kueel ba käp ɛ luaac.
entries.english_sentence: Hyena thought about this problem for a long time. He came up with an idea.He collected gum from the trees. He put that sticky gum around the whole field. The thief would get stuck in the gum.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Mäthni ti ci bila ji̱ tɛ̈r
entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ wäär, cu Pɛlpɛl jiɛɛn wë manytaapni kual rɛy kakä Yakä.Ɛ ŋot /kenɛ ni cop rɛy kakä cuɛ ɣɔw guic kɛɛliw mi puɔlɛ.
entries.english_sentence: During the night, Hare went to Hyena's field to steal more maize.Before entering the field he looked around to see if it was safe.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Mäthni ti ci bila ji̱ tɛ̈r
entries.nuer_sentence: Pɛlpɛl /kenɛ luaac tin ca go̱lni kak ɛ Yak nɛn.Pɛlpɛl cuɛ cuɔ̱ŋ rɛy luacä kä cuɛ dɔp thi̱n. Cuɛ rɔaal kɛ gör lua̱k.
entries.english_sentence: Hare did not see the gum that Hyena had put around the field.Hare stood in the gum and was stuck. He started shouting for help.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Mäthni ti ci bila ji̱ tɛ̈r
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Yak rɔal liŋ kä ri̱i̱ŋɛ raar kɛ ɣöö bɛ kueel ben käp. Jɛn /kenɛ ŋäth kɛ waŋdɛ i̱, dɔ̱ŋ ɛ jɛn määthdɛ ni Pɛlpɛl min ci dɔp rɛy luacä.Niɛ gua̱th ɛmɔ, cu Yak duɔ̱pdɛ kuany kä cu Pɛlpɛl wä kɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p dɔ̱diɛn. Cuɛ cua̱ jɛn tuk däkä määthädiɛn piny.
entries.english_sentence: Hyena heard the shouts and ran out to catch the thief.He could not believe his eyes. It was his friend Hare who was stuck in the gum!
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan, nyaawni kɛnɛ kuɔ̱ ɔ̱ n kɛ mäth. Kɛn la ŋarkɛ kä lätkɛ kɛɛl.Nyaawni cikɛ kuɛɛn kä kuɔ̱ ɔ̱ n, kä kuɔ̱ ɔ̱ n cikɛ kuɛɛn kɛ nyaawni, cieŋkɛ kɛ tɛ̈ th lɔaac.
entries.english_sentence: A long time ago, the cats and the mice were friends. They worked together and played together.Cats married mice and mice married cats and they were happy.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Duŋdɛ ɣöö, kɛ kɔrɛ, kɛn kuɔ̱ɔ̱n cukɛ diɛɛr. "Tha̱a̱ŋ ji̱ maarädan cikɛ bath. Kɛn a nikä?" "Ɣän cä jääny /ka̱n näärä met nɛn," cu kun kɛl ɛ lar."Kä /ka̱n maalen met nɛn," cua lat ɛ kun dɔ̱diɛn. "Nyimaar /cɛ lɛ ŋot thi̱n," ɛ  kun in diɔ̱ɔ̱kdiɛn. "Kä dämaar tëë nikä?" latdɛ kun in ŋuaandiɛn.
entries.english_sentence: But over time, the mice became worried. "Some of our relatives have disappeared," they said. "Where are they?" "I haven't seen my uncle for a long time," one mouse said."And I haven't seen my aunt," said another mouse. "My sister isn't here anymore," a third mouse said. "And where's my brother?" said a fourth mouse.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä cu kun in dɔaaŋ wi̱cdɛ tiŋ ɛ gui̱cɛ kɛ gak.Jɛn cuɛ wee, "Ɣän tëëkɛ läär jiɛthä lɔaac mi la̱rä yɛ. Kɛn nyaawni ti̱ti̱ camkɛ kɔn. Kɔn banɛ rɔ dhil tit. Cikɛ thia̱k kɛ ca̱mdan kɔndiaal."
entries.english_sentence: An old mouse shook his head. He looked sad."I have bad news for you, my friends," he said. "The cats are eating us. We must be very careful. Soon they will eat us all."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn kuɔ̱ɔ̱n cukɛ dual ɛlɔ̱ŋ.Cu mani gan gaatkiɛn jiök i̱, "Yɛn tiɛtdɛ rɔ. /Cuarɛ wä raar. Kɛn nyaawni ba yɛ ka̱p."
entries.english_sentence: The mice were very frightened.The mothers said to their children, "Don't go outside. Be careful. The cats will catch you."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn kuɔ̱ɔ̱n diaal cuarɔ̱ ku pay tit.Cukɛ cua̱ te rɛy kɔ̱a̱knikiɛn. Kɛn /ca wä raar lɛ go̱r.
entries.english_sentence: All the mice were careful now.They stayed inside their holes. They did not like to go outside.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Niɛ gua̱a̱th ɛmɔ, kɛn nyaawni diɛɛrkɛ bä. Cukɛ wee i̱, "Kä kuɔ̱ɔ̱n diaal cikɛ wä ni? Buɔth näkɛ kɔn. Kä/thilɛ mi canɛ jek mi dëë kulɛ cam."Cu nyaaw in di̱i̱t wee, "Ɣäni ca rɔ̱ tɔ̱w kɛ kɔn. Banɛ kɛ kulɛ käp i̱di?"
entries.english_sentence: Now, the cats were worried too. "Where have all the mice gone?" they said. "We're hungry. We haven't got anything to eat.""They're hiding from us," a big cat said. "How can we catch them?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Nyaaw dɔ̱diɛn cuɛ wee, "Kɔn wanɛ wä, kɛ gui̱l mi banɛ riali bul ikä. Kɔn banɛ kɛ wä thiec i̱ nyam kɛl kä yɛ ba kuɛnɛ gat kɛl kä nɛy. Kɛ ɣöö bi ri̱ŋ mi di̱i̱t te thi̱n bikɛ ben raar kɛn diaal. Kɔn banɛ kɛ cu käp niɛ gua̱a̱th mɔ ni kɛn diaal. Kɛn bikɛ cua̱ ri̱ŋkɔn ti ro̱ŋ kɛ kɔn!"Cu nyaawni dial tin kɔ̱kiɛn wee, "Ɛ ca̱r mi gɔaa ɛlɔ̱ŋ."
entries.english_sentence: "I've got an idea," another cat said. "Let's go and visit the mice and arrange a wedding. We'll ask for one of their daughters to marry one of our sons.There'll be a feast and they'll all be together in one place. We can catch them all at the same time. It will be a great feast for us!"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛ nyɔk bä, cu nyaawni di̱tkiɛn jäkä kuɔ̱ɔ̱n.Cua kuɔ̱ɔ̱n jiök i̱, "Muɔcɛ nɛy kɛ nyal mi kuɛɛn nɛyɛ kä nyieekun. Kɔn go̱o̱r nɛy ɣöö ba ciek kɛl kä gaatkɔ."
entries.english_sentence: "That's a very good idea," said all the other cats.So, the cats sent their elders to the mice."Give us one of your daughters," they said. "We want a wife for one of our sons."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kä kuɔ̱ɔ̱n cukɛ ŋɛ̈ɛ̈r ɛlɔ̱ŋ. Cukɛ wee i̱, "Kɔn /ci nɛy yɛ ŋäth. Go̱o̱r yɛni ɣöö bia nɛy cam."Kä cu nyaawni ɛ loc i̱, "Ɣëy! Ɣëy! Kɔn lot nɛy ni jɛ ɛ puc ɛ puc ɛn gör määthädun. Jɛn ɛ thuɔ̱k, kɛ gua̱a̱th ci wä, tha̱a̱ŋda ca tha̱a̱ŋdun cam. Duŋni ɣöö ɛn tämɛ ba̱kɔ yi̱k päl. Kɔn /ca̱kɔ yɛ bi cam ɛ nyɔk."
entries.english_sentence: The mice were very surprised. "We don't trust you," they said. "You only want to eat us.""No! No!" answered the cats. "We're very honest and sincere and want to be your friends. It's true, a long time ago some of us ate some of you. But we must forget that now. We'll never eat you again."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kuɔ̱ɔ̱n nyaawni di̱el guec. Kä nyaawni cua duɔɔth doth.Cu kuɔ̱ɔ̱n wee, "Gɔaa, ci kɔn mat. Kɔn ba̱kɔ gatdun kɛl thöp nyaada kɛl."
entries.english_sentence: The mice looked at the cats. The cats were all smiling."All right," the mice said. "We agree. We will give one of our daughters to one of your sons."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu nyaawni loc cieŋ kɛ tɛ̈th lɔaac.Cukɛ wee i̱, "Bi gɔɔydɛ ba̱l ni cäŋ buɔ̱ɔ̱l," ɛ wäkɛ mi bɛ̈lkɛ thukiɛn.
entries.english_sentence: The cats went home happily."The wedding day will be wonderful," they said,  licking their lips.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu cäŋ buɔ̱ɔ̱l cop. Kɛn kuɔ̱ɔ̱n cukɛ ŋot diɛɛrkɛ. "Ta̱yɛ thieekä ɣo̱tni," cua la̱r gaatkiɛn."Guicɛ jɛ, nyaawni ka bëëni. Mi wäkɛ gɔw kɛ kɔn, banɛ gɔw kɛ kɛ bä. Duŋni ɣöö mi wa ca̱mdan ɣɔ̱n, banɛ rɔ̱dan cu guir."
entries.english_sentence: The wedding day came. The mice were still very worried. "Stay near your holes," they said to their children."Look, the cats are coming. If they're nice to us, we'll be nice to them. But if they try to eat us, we'll be ready."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu nyaawni duɔ̱pdiɛn kuany.Ɛ wäkɛ mi kɛ̈tkɛ dit buɔ̱ɔ̱l.
entries.english_sentence: The cats came down the road.They were singing a wedding song.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Dɔaaŋ kuɔ̱n cuɛ ŋuɛ̈t kɛl thiec i̱, "Liŋ yɛn dit ɛ kiit kɛnɛ mɔ?"Cu kun in duŋ tiit wee, "Ɣää. Kɛn tekɛ ki̱i̱tdä, 'Ka̱pɛ kɛ kä camɛ kɛ. Ka̱pɛ kɛ kä camɛ kɛ!'"
entries.english_sentence: "Can you hear the words of the song?" an old mouse asked a young one.The young mouse said, "Yes. They are singing, 'Catch them and eat them. Catch them and eat them!'"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu kun in di̱i̱t wee, "Kɔn banɛ kiet bä."Jɛn cuɛ kiet tok, "Riɛŋɛ, kuɔ̱ɔ̱n, riɛŋɛ! Riɛŋɛ, kuɔ̱ɔ̱n, riɛŋɛ!"Kɛn kuɔ̱ɔ̱n diaal cuarɔ̱ yuɔr ɣo̱tnikiɛn kä cukɛ läny.
entries.english_sentence: "Then we must sing too," said the old mouse.He began to sing, "Run, mice, run! Run, mice, run!"All the mice jumped into their holes and escaped.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛn nyaawni cukɛ cop kä thiëc kɛrɔ̱ kamnikiɛn, "Kaw gatdan ja nikä?"Cu dɔaaŋ kuɔ̱n wi̱cdɛ ruɔ̱ny raar rɛy kɔ̱kädɛ. Cuɛ wee i̱, "Canɛ min ca nyuɔ̱th kɔn nɛn. Mi pɛɛl gua̱n tɛ̈ru rɔɔdɛ i̱ ɛ määthdu, ji̱n guir rɔɔdu kɛ bänydɛ piny."
entries.english_sentence: The cats arrived and asked each other, "Where is the bride for our son?"The old mouse put his head out of his hole. "We've learned our lesson," he said. "When your enemies pretend to be your friends, you must be ready to run away."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Tekɛ cuɛ̈ɛ̈k da̱ŋ rɛw ti cieŋ kɛɛl, Guɔ̱r kɛnɛ Rɔw.Kɛ cäŋ kɛl cu riɛk ben kä cuɛ kɛ jiök i̱ bia rɔ mëk kɛl kä rɛw, "Bia rɔ moc cio̱o̱r kiɛ dhɔɔp."Rɔw go̱rɛ ɣöö bɛ pɛ̈l. Kɛ pɛ̈th, cuɛ mɛk ni dhɔp, kɛ ɣöö bɛ kulɛ ŋot kɛ mi gui̱cɛ. Kä Guɔ̱r cuɛ mɛk ni cio̱o̱r.
entries.english_sentence: There lived a set of twin brothers called Elephant and Hippo.One day, Fate came and gave them two choices. "Choose blindness or leprosy," Fate ordered.Hippo wanted to be clever. He quickly chose leprosy so as to keep using his eyes. Elephant chose blindness.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Rɔw la dho̱o̱l mi ŋɛnynyɛny kɛ ɣöö tëkɛ dhɔp. Cu cio̱o̱r Guɔ̱r jakä ram mi tëë kɛ li̱ep bitdä. Guɔ̱r go̱rɛ luäk duŋdɛ ɣöö cu Rɔw ɛ ciɛŋ ɛ jiäk.Kɛ kɔrɛ, cu Guɔ̱r kɛɛt mi jak jɛ kä bum jek. Ɛn kɛɛt ɛmɔ jak ɛ jɛ kä jäl. Cukɛ rɔ̱ mua̱thmua̱th kɛnɛ kɛɛtdɛ ɛn Guɔ̱r. Ɛn kɛɛt gaŋɛ Guɔ̱r kä ji̱ tɛ̈rɛ.
entries.english_sentence: Hippo became an angry boy because of the leprosy. Blindness gave Elephant patience. Elephant needed help but Hippo treated him badly.Then Elephant found a magical Stick, which helped him to move around. They whispered secrets to each other. Stick helped Elephant to fight enemies.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ ɣöö cɛ Rɔw yɛt tetni kɛnɛ yɛt ciöknikɛ ŋuɔ̱k, jɛn go̱o̱rɛ luäk. Cu Guɔ̱r jɛ luäk.Mëë ca kuän nööŋ, cu Rɔw ɛ go̱r ɛn ɣöö bi Guɔ̱r kuän jɔam tetdɛ min thil yɛt. Ɛn Rɔw /ci lɔcdɛ tɛth.
entries.english_sentence: Because Hippo lost his fingers and toes he also needed help. Elephant was kind to him.When food was served, Hippo needed Elephant to cut the food and place it on his fingerless palms. Hippo was very unhappy.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, kɛ runwaŋ, cu mandiɛn kɛ tha̱l manbɛɛkni. Kɛ ɣöö ci buɔth kɛ näk ɛlɔ̱ŋ, kɛn dhɔɔl /ken kɛn manbɛɛkni li̱ep ɣöö bikɛ kɔ̱a̱c.Cu Rɔw yɛtkɛ diaal guk kä cukɛ ce̱tkɛ tuɔk mieth. Cuɛ wee, "Jɔmni pekdä wanɛmɛ."
entries.english_sentence: One morning, their mother served hot yams. Because they were hungry, the boys did not wait for the yams to cool.Hippo put his palms together and they looked like a plate. He asked, "Put my share here for me."
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Ɛn manbɛk lethɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛ cuɛ pa̱a̱t tetnikɛ waŋ. Cu Rɔw tetkɛ tɛ̈ŋ kɛ ɣöö bi pa̱a̱t tetnikɛ kɔ̱c. Cu manbɛk pɛn piny rɛy litdä.Cu Guɔ̱r manbɛkdɛ gua̱a̱l tetnikɛ, kä /kenɛ pɛn piny. Cu Rɔw lɔcdɛ jiääk.
entries.english_sentence: The yam was so hot that it burned their palms. Hippo moved his hands up and down, to cool his palms. The yam fell on the sand.Elephant moved his own yam from one hand to the other without it falling. Hippo was annoyed.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: "Ɣa̱! Luäk ɣä kɛ manbɛkdä," cu Rɔw Guɔ̱r thiec."Ɣän /cä jɛ nɛn," cu Guɔ̱r ɛ loc. "Kämni ɣä tëtdu, bɛ nyuɔ̱th ji̱," cu Rɔw jɛ loc.Cu Guɔ̱r manbɛk jek, kä cuɛ liɛtdɛ kuɔth jɔ̱ɔ̱r. Cuɛ jɛ ka̱m Rɔw.
entries.english_sentence: "Help me pick up my yam, please," Hippo asked Elephant."You know I cannot see it," Elephant replied."Give me your hand, I will show you," Hippo said.Elephant found the yam, and blew the sand off it. He gave it to Hippo.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ thiaŋ, cu mandiɛn kɛ moc manbɛk mi ca ŋuɔ̱k kɛɛl kɛ dhon ri̱i̱ŋ da̱ŋ ŋuaan. Cu Guɔ̱r dhon ri̱i̱ŋ thiap kɛ pɛ̈th, kä cuɛ kɛ kuɛn kɛ yɛtkɛ./Ken Rɔw tekɛ ŋäc ɛn ɣöö ca dhon ri̱i̱ŋ kuɛn ɛ Guɔ̱r.
entries.english_sentence: In the evening, their mother gave them pounded yam, and four pieces of meat. Elephant quickly touched the meat and counted the pieces with his fingers.Hippo did not notice Elephant counting the meat.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Rɔw ɛ ɣɔ̱n kɛ mi kualɛ dhuɔn ri̱eŋ, duŋdɛ ɣöö cuɛ pɛ̈ɛ̈n. Mëë ci gua̱th in ba camni ri̱ŋ cop, cu Guɔ̱r wee, "Kɛn dhon ri̱i̱ŋ /cikɛ ŋuaan ɛ nin?"Rɔw cuɛ kackac i̱, "Kɛ diɔ̱k." Guɔ̱r cuɛ gam thi̱n i̱, "Kɛ ŋuaan." Rɔw cuɛ Guɔ̱r jiök, "Ɛ ji̱n cɔr ɛ puc?"
entries.english_sentence: Hippo tried to steal a piece of meat but he dropped it. When it was time to share the meat, Elephant asked, "Were there not four pieces of meat?""There were three," Hippo lied. "There were four," Elephant insisted. "Are you really blind?" Hippo asked.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Kɛ cäŋ kɛl, ci buɔthkɛ näk, kä te mandiɛn jɔ̱ɔ̱r. Rɔw cuɛ Guɔ̱r jiök i̱, "Wanɛ ŋar kɛ ɣöö ban buɔth pa̱l ruëëc."Cu Guɔ̱r ɛ nhɔk, Rɔw cuɛ wee i̱, "Wanɛ kɛt yieer." Kä ŋäcɛ jɛ ɛn ɣöö Guɔ̱r kui̱cɛ kët. Go̱rɛ ɣöö bi däman wä mua. Guɔ̱r kɛnɛ kɛɛtdɛ cukɛ te kɔɔr Rɔa.
entries.english_sentence: One day, they were hungry but their mother was away. "Let us go and play to forget our hunger," suggested Hippo.Elephant agreed, so Hippo said, "Let us swim in the river." He knew Elephant could not swim. He planned to kill his brother!Elephant and Stick followed Hippo.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Min tekɛ jäl, cu Rɔw coth rɛy ruɔ̱ɔ̱p. Cuɛ do̱l mi di̱i̱t kuany, cuɛ jɛ kɔat rɔ̱ɔ̱thdɛ. Kä nho̱o̱kɛ rɔ kɛ kapdɛ nhiaal. Cuɛ ŋot kɛ mi nho̱o̱kɛ rɔɔdɛ amäni mëë wäkɛ yieer.Cu Guɔ̱r ɛ thiec, "Ɛŋu mi nho̱o̱ki rɔ kɛ jɛ." Cu Guɔ̱r Kɛɛt thiec.
entries.english_sentence: On the way, Hippo went into the forest. He picked up a heavy stone and put it under his arm. He grunted as he picked up the stone. He was still grunting as they walked to the river."Why is he grunting like that?" Elephant asked Stick.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë cikɛ cop yieer, cu Rɔw wee i̱, "Bi kɔn kacni ɣän yieer kɛ nhiam, kɛ kɔrɛ bi cu luäk kɛ kët."Cuɛ rɔ jakä na̱n kɛ Guɔ̱r. Cuɛ do̱lɛ kap nhial, kä cuɛ jɛ yuɔr yieer."Ɛn jɔw ɛmɔ kuiyɛ ɛlɔ̱ŋ. Jɛn /ciɛ Rɔw ɛn min ci rɔ yuɔr yieer," cu Kɛɛt jɛ mua̱th Guɔ̱r.
entries.english_sentence: When they reached the river, Hippo said, "I will jump in first and help you to swim."He moved away from Elephant. He lifted the stone and threw it into the river."That sound is too small for the size of Hippo," Stick whispered in Elephant's ear.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.nuer_sentence: Cu Guɔ̱r Kɛɛt thiec kɛ ɣöö ba la̱t ti ŋuan. Cuɛ ŋot kɛ mi yi̱i̱thɛ Kɛɛt. Cu Kɛɛt, cuɛ Rɔw yɔ̱t ɛ bɛc. Cu Rɔw wak, "Wa̱a̱y! Kä cuɛ rɔ yuɔr piny."Cu Kɛɛt in tekɛ wal Rɔw loc ɛ la ley yiëër. Kä cuɛ Guɔ̱r jakä ley raar, cu Kɛɛt rɔ loc ni luth Gua̱r.
entries.english_sentence: Elephant asked Stick to find out more. He started swinging Stick round and round. Stick hit Hippo very hard. "Ayei!" Hippo cried and jumped into the river.The magical Stick turned Hippo into a water animal. He turned Elephant into a land animal and became Elephant's trunk.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëëdan tëëkɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan ti cieŋ kɛɛl kɛ mandiɛn dhɔɔriɛn.Cu mandiɛn jiɛɛn wëë kä thuk, kä cuɛ kɛ jiök i̱, "Cuarɛ ram mi dɔ̱ŋ lep thi̱i̱k, bia lɛp ɛ ci bën ni puɔ̱nydä," cuɛ gaatkɛ guɔk.
entries.english_sentence: There were four lambs living in a house with their mother.Mother was on her way to the market. "You will open the door only when I say open the door, my children," she warned her lambs.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Kä ɛn guäth ɛmɔ, te wan li̱ŋ gekä duëël, liŋɛ min ci mandiɛn ɛ la̱r kɛ. Cu wan ben thok duëël kä cuɛ jiök i̱, "Dɛykä, lɛ̈pɛ thi̱i̱k ɛ ɣän mandun."Cu dɔw dɛ̈ɛ̈l kɛl ɛ luoc i̱, "Ɣëy, nɔmɔ /ciɛ jɛn jɔw maara, Jɔw maara kuiyɛ." Kä cu wan gaak.
entries.english_sentence: Meanwhile, a fox was nearby and heard the mother. He went to the house and said, "My children, open the door."One of the lambs said, "No, that is not our mother's voice. Our mother's voice is soft." The fox was angry.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ rɔɔdɛ moc kɛ ca̱p, cɛ go̱r i̱ bi̱i̱ jɔwdɛ ca̱a̱t ce̱tkɛ jɔw mandeet. Jɛn cuɛ jɛ go̱r i̱ bɛ liɛɛth cam.Jɛn cuɛ wä kä gua̱n thuɔk luaak. "Moc ɣä kɛ liɛɛth, kiɛ bä ji̱ näk." Cu wan gua̱n thuɔk luaak dua̱c dual inɔ.Jɛn gua̱n thuɔk luaak cuɛ liɛɛth thöp wan.
entries.english_sentence: The fox wanted to make his voice like the lambs' mother. He decided to eat butter.He went to a shopkeeper. "Give me some butter, or I will kill you," threatened the fox.The shopkeeper gave him butter.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu wan wä kä dɛy deet kä cuɛ jɛ lar, "Dɛykä, lɛ̈pɛ thi̱i̱k." Dɔw kɛl cuɛ guic kɛ kuil thi̱ekä kä cuɛ ci̱o̱o̱k wan nɛn ɛ mi ca̱r."Ɣëy, cuɛ wak! Ciök maara kɛ ti luaal." /Kenɛ rɔ luɔ̱t wan.
entries.english_sentence: The fox went to the lambs and said, "My children, open the door." A lamb looked through the keyhole of the door and saw the black leg of the fox."No, our mother's legs are red!" shouted the lamb. Fox was not successful.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Wan cuɛ ca̱r kɛ duɔ̱ɔ̱p dɔ̱diɛn. Ɛn guäth ɛmɔ cuɛ guic ni ɣöö bɛ ciökɛ bil kɛ nup citɛth.Cuɛ wä kä guäär citɛth. "Moc ɣä kɛ nup citɛth, kiɛ bä cam ni ji̱." Jɛn cuɛ jɛ dua̱c dual inɔ.Cu guäär citɛth nup citɛ̈th thöp.
entries.english_sentence: Fox thought of another way. This time he planned to paint his legs with pepper powder.He went to a miller. "Give me pepper powder, or I will eat you," the fox threatened.The miller gave him pepper powder.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Wan cuɛ ciök kɛ bil kɛ nup. Jɛn cuɛ wä dueel kä dɛy deet kä cuɛ jɛ lar, "Dɛykä, lɛ̈pɛ thi̱i̱k."Kɛn dɛy deet cua thi̱i̱k lɛp. Cu wan dɛy deet da̱ŋ diɔ̱k roc.
entries.english_sentence: Fox painted his legs with the powder. He went to the lambs' house and said, "My children open the door."The lambs opened the door. Fox swallowed three of them.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu ŋuaan dɛɛni rɔ tɛ̱̈ɛ̱̈.Cu mandiɛn luny jɔk kä thuk. Cuɛ jɛ lar, "Dɛykä, ɣän cä ben. Lɛ̈pɛ thi̱i̱k."Dɔw ɛ ŋuaandiɛn cɛ dual ɛlɔ̱ŋ ɛ /kenɛ mandiɛn luäŋ kɛ le̱p thi̱i̱k.
entries.english_sentence: The fourth lamb was hiding.Mother came back from the market. She said, "My children, I have come. Open the door."The fourth lamb was terrified and couldn't open the door for her mother.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë cɛ thiɛl dɔw kɛl kä kɛ mi ci thi̱i̱k lɛp, cu mandeet kuɛt ni thi̱i̱k kɛ lëpdɛ. Jɛn cuɛ dɛykɛ cɔl.Cu dɔw ɛ ŋuaandiɛn ben raar gua̱a̱th in cɛ rɔ wä tɛ̱̈ɛ̱̈ thi̱n. Cu man ɛ thiec, "Kä tha̱a̱ŋkun ɛ ni?"
entries.english_sentence: When no one opened the door, the mother sheep kicked it open. She called her lambs.The fourth lamb came out of hiding. Her mother asked "Where are the others?"
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Cuɛ jɛ loc kä lathɛ jɛ i̱, "Ci wan kɛ roc kɛn tha̱a̱ŋ kɔ!"
entries.english_sentence: Shivering, the lamb replied, "The fox swallowed the others!"Her mother said, "The fox might eat us too. Let's move to another place." They set off to another place.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë tekɛ jäl cu kɛn wan nɛn tëë ni̱n.Kä cu mandiɛn rɔ ti̱ec thiekä waan. Cuɛ jiööth dɛɛnikɛ liŋ jiic waan."No̱o̱ŋni ɣä reet mi moth kɛ kɛ̈ɛ̈t amäni lipɛ," cu mandiɛn ciöt.
entries.english_sentence: While they were travelling they saw the fox. He was sleeping.The mother approached the fox. She heard the voices of her lambs inside the fox's belly."Bring me a razor blade, thread and a needle," said the mother to her lamb.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Cu mandiɛn jic wan rɛ̈t kɛ reet kä cuɛ dɛykɛ da̱ŋ di̱ɔ̱k jek thi̱n.Cuɛ jic waan piek pääm kä cuɛ jɛ kɔc thi̱n. Kä cuɛ dɛykɛ diaal luɔc cieŋdiɛn.
entries.english_sentence: The mother cut the fox's belly with a razor blade. She found her three lambs inside his belly.She filled his belly with stones and stitched it together. She took all her lambs back to their house.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org

entries.book_title: Wan kɛnɛ dɛy deet da̱ŋ ŋuaan
entries.nuer_sentence: Mëë ci wan keer, cuɛ jɛ jek bumɛ ɛn ɣöö bɛ jiɛɛn.Cuɛ jɛ ɣɔ̱n i̱ bɛ maath pi̱i̱ni kiɛɛr, duŋdɛ ni ɣöö /kenɛ rɔ luäŋ kɛ ɣöö bɛ cuɔ̱ŋ. Cu wan pɛ̈n rɛy pi̱i̱ni kä cuɛ cu mua.
entries.english_sentence: When the fox woke up, he found it very difficult to get up.He tried to drink water at a river, but he lost his balance. He fell into the water and drowned.
entries.citation: African Storybook Initiative and Molteno Institute. 2014. Creative Commons: Attribution 4.0. www.africanstorybook.org
